evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-llm-omp-transports

A DeepSeek Harness LLM transport component for providers whose wire protocols
the vendored `llm-pi-ai` does not speak. It is published from this repository
as `dsh-llm-omp-transports` and installed as a dependency of
`dsh-keys-manager`: installing the Keys Manager plugin brings this component,
and the plugin page lists both bundle components
(`dsh-keys-manager` and `llm-omp-transports`).

| Fact | Value |
|---|---|
| npm package | `dsh-llm-omp-transports` |
| Plugin id | `llm-omp-transports` |
| Routes | `cursor`, `devin`, `google-gemini-cli`, `google-antigravity`, `factory-droid`, `gitlab-duo`, `gitlab-duo-agent` (the seam is provider-generic) |
| Credential scope | `llm-omp-transports/<provider>` — one record per route (`cursor`, `devin`, `google-gemini-cli`, `google-antigravity`, `factory-droid`, `gitlab-duo`, `gitlab-duo-agent`) |
| Runtime | Node 24 (the bundle imports Node builtins only) |
| License | MIT |

The plugin registers its own route on the DSH `llm` seam, so it depends on no
upstream DSH change. `@oh-my-pi/pi-ai` and `@oh-my-pi/pi-catalog` are used at
**build time only**: the build inlines the pinned omp transports into one ESM
artifact per route (`lib/omp/cursor.mjs`, `lib/omp/devin.mjs`), plus one shared
artifact for the two Google routes (`lib/omp/google.mjs`), and the published
package imports nothing from `@oh-my-pi/*` or `bun:*` at runtime.

## Cursor support status

- **Text streaming** — yes. Assistant text and usage are projected onto DSH's
  `StreamChunk` stream.
- **Reasoning streaming** — yes, with the catalog's effort routing. The
  selected effort becomes the routed wire model id; an effort the model does
  not advertise is refused with `UNSUPPORTED_REASONING_EFFORT`.
- **Tool-call handoff** — yes, through DSH's tool loop. Cursor's server drives
  execution over its exec channel, so the transport runs in external-executor
  mode: an unhandled MCP call is emitted as an unresolved tool call and
  answered with a handoff, DSH runs the tool, and the next request replays the
  result from history. The adapter never executes a tool itself.
- **Sign-in and refresh** — yes. The package registers the
  `llm-omp-transports/cursor` authorization flow (a browser login page plus a
  poll, no loopback callback and no device code) and refreshes an expiring
  grant under the credential store's per-key lock. The Keys Manager Web page's
  **Transport accounts** section is the surface that starts the flow.
- **Models** — from the pinned catalog: the Cursor slice of
  `@oh-my-pi/pi-catalog@18.12.3` (123 rows) is generated into
  `src/catalog/cursor.ts` and served without a network call.
- **Route** — `cursor`, declared configurable so the Models page has a profile
  entry for it.
- **Images** — not yet. The route advertises text-only input and refuses image
  blocks with `CONTENT_UNSUPPORTED`; see [known limits](docs/known-limits.md).

## Devin support status

- **Text streaming** — yes. Assistant text and reasoning are projected onto
  DSH's `StreamChunk` stream, with the per-turn usage the chat frames report.
- **Reasoning streaming** — yes as content; no reasoning-effort selector. Both
  pinned rows advertise no efforts, and a request that selects one is refused
  with `UNSUPPORTED_REASONING_EFFORT`.
- **Tool-call handoff** — yes, native to DSH's tool loop. The transport emits
  the call, finishes the turn `toolUse`, and DSH executes it; the result is
  replayed from history on the next request. Unlike Cursor, no call is
  transport-resolved, so nothing is filtered from the handoff.
- **Sign-in** — yes, by pasting the callback. The pinned omp login is a
  declarative `oauth-code` rule whose loopback listener is Bun-only; this
  package registers the `llm-omp-transports/devin` flow, opens the authorize
  page, and asks for the address the browser landed on (or just the code).
  There is **no refresh** (`refresh "none"`): an expired grant demands a new
  sign-in.
- **Models** — from the pinned catalog: the Devin slice of
  `@oh-my-pi/pi-catalog@18.12.3` (2 rows: `swe-1-6`, `swe-1-6-fast`) is
  generated into `src/catalog/devin.ts` and served without a network call.
- **Route** — `devin`, declared configurable so the Models page has a
  `providers.devin` profile with an allow-list.
- **Images** — not yet, same as Cursor: text-only input, image blocks refused
  with `CONTENT_UNSUPPORTED`.

## Google support status

Two routes share one artifact: `google-gemini-cli` (Google's Gemini CLI client)
and `google-antigravity` (the Antigravity hub client). The bundled
`streamGoogleGeminiCli` dispatches on `model.provider`, so the route is a data
difference — separate OAuth client, catalogs, hosts, scopes and credential
records — not a second code path.

- **Text streaming** — yes, including reasoning parts and usage.
- **Reasoning streaming** — yes, with each row's own effort ladder: the
  budget-mode rows send `thinkingConfig.thinkingBudget`, the Gemini-3+ rows send
  `thinkingLevel`. A row with `requiresEffort` refuses a turn that selects no
  effort (`UNSUPPORTED_REASONING_EFFORT`), exactly as omp does.
- **Tool-call handoff** — yes, native to DSH's tool loop, like Devin: the
  transport emits the call and finishes the turn `toolUse`. Antigravity's
  default tool mode (`VALIDATED`) is sent on every request that declares tools.
- **Sign-in** — yes, with a real loopback listener on `127.0.0.1`:
  `:8085/oauth2callback` for Gemini CLI and `:51121/oauth-callback` for
  Antigravity, as the pinned rules declare. The browser redirect completes the
  flow automatically; if the port is taken the listener falls back to an
  ephemeral port and the authorize page names the port it actually bound. The
  full address the browser landed on (or `code#state`) can also be pasted; a
  pasted code without the state is refused, because that is exactly the shape a
  forged callback would have. Anything the listener does not recognise — a
  foreign `state`, an `error=`, a missing code — is answered `400` and dropped
  without ending the attempt, so a stray request cannot kill the sign-in. The
  listener closes on the matching callback, on an aborted attempt and **on a
  timeout** (five minutes, `GoogleFlowOptions.waitMs` for tests): an expired wait
  fails with `AUTH_FAILED` and commits nothing.
- **Refresh** — yes. The resolver refreshes once, under the credential store's
  per-key lock, when `expires - 60 s <= now`, keeps the `projectId` and an
  un-rotated `refresh_token`, and reports a dead sign-in as `REAUTH_REQUIRED`.
- **Credential record** — `llm-omp-transports/<route>` with
  `{access, refresh, expires, projectId, email?}`. The adapter hands the
  transport the structured JSON envelope (`token`, `projectId`, `refreshToken`,
  `expiresAt`, `email`) that omp parses.
- **Project discovery** — sign-in finishes with the Cloud Code Assist project:
  `loadCodeAssist` → (tier onboarding `onboardUser` + LRO poll, or the required
  `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` / `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT_ID` variable for a
  `legacy-tier`/paid account). Antigravity additionally checks free-tier
  eligibility and bounds onboarding at 30 s.
- **Models** — generated from the pinned `@oh-my-pi/pi-catalog@18.12.3`: 7 rows
  for `google-gemini-cli`, 22 for `google-antigravity`, served without a network
  call.
- **Routes** — both declared configurable, so the Models page has
  `providers.google-gemini-cli` and `providers.google-antigravity` allow-lists.
- **Images** — not yet, same posture as the other routes: text-only input, image
  blocks refused with `CONTENT_UNSUPPORTED`. omp's Antigravity image path
  decodes through `Bun.Image`, which does not exist under Node, so that path is
  dead here by construction; the projection never reaches it.

## Factory Droid support status

- **Text streaming** — yes, including reasoning parts and usage.
- **Wires** — four protocols behind one proxy, selected by the model **id** inside the
  artifact (Anthropic Messages for Claude rows, the Responses API for GPT/Grok, Chat
  Completions for Kimi/GLM/DeepSeek, native generateContent for Gemini). The plugin never
  chooses a backend, and rows carry no base URL: the transport derives the per-wire proxy
  path and honours the account's residency host.
- **Sign-in** — WorkOS **device code**: the flow shows the verification page and the user
  code, the human approves in the browser, and the poll completes the grant. No listener and
  no paste; the attempt's own signal is the only cancellation channel.
- **Refresh** — yes: one refresh inside a 60 s window under the credential store's per-key
  lock, keeping the account scope (`orgId`/`region`/`inferenceRegion`), which the adapter
  forwards to the transport as `oauthIdentity` so a EU account gets its own host.
- **Catalog** — 62 rows from the KDL registry seed (`models.json` has no factory-droid key),
  zero-cost Factory credits.
- **Build** — the graph needs three **entry-scoped build substitutions** (empty catalog data,
  a lean provider registry, a lean env-key map) to fit its ceiling; see the limits below.

## GitLab Duo support status

Two routes over GitLab's AI surface, both registered from one catalog pin.

**`gitlab-duo` (proxy).** The transport POSTs for a direct-access token, substitutes the
row's `upstreamModelId` and delegates to one of three generic wire transports
(Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Responses, Chat Completions) through GitLab's gateway.

- 16 catalog rows carrying the upstream id, the wire and the full compat object.
- **Sign-in** — OAuth code with PKCE, the loopback listener on `localhost:8080/callback`
  **without port fallback** (the redirect is registered exactly) and a paste prompt as the
  fallback path. `GITLAB_CLIENT_ID`/`GITLAB_REDIRECT_URI` support a custom OAuth app, and a
  `GITLAB_TOKEN` personal access token works as the bearer.
- **Refresh** — one refresh inside a 60 s window; the artifact's direct-access token cache
  is keyed on the GitLab token, so a rotated token misses it by construction.

**`gitlab-duo-agent` (Duo Workflow).** One WebSocket workflow per turn; GitLab's
server-side loop yields at every tool call, so DSH's native tool loop executes them and the
next turn replays the result through the goal transcript.

- 1 static row (`claude_sonnet_4_6_vertex`, 1M context); live model discovery is not
  implemented, and the server may pin another model on its side.
- **Sign-in** — paste-only: the browser hands the code to VS Code, so the human pastes the
  full `vscode://gitlab.gitlab-workflow/authentication?code=…&state=…` URL. The state is
  mandatory (no listener means it is the only thing tying the paste to the attempt), and a
  refresh echoes the `vscode` redirect.
- **Session state** — a fresh map per request (plan A6): each turn re-seeds a workflow and
  replays the transcript instead of resuming another turn's socket. Correct but heavier;
  sticky resume is a follow-up.

## Hard constraints

- **Pinned, build-time-only omp.** `@oh-my-pi/pi-ai` and `@oh-my-pi/pi-catalog`
  are pinned to `18.12.3` and declared as devDependencies. No runtime package
  may import them: `tests/build.test.ts` checks that every static import of the
  shipped artifact is a Node builtin.
- **Node 24 load.** The artifact is imported through a plain Node ESM loader
  with no Bun global present, and must expose `streamCursor`. The Bun and
  `@oh-my-pi/pi-utils` surface the bundled graph reaches is covered by the
  shims in `scripts/omp-shim/`; a missing shim symbol or a new shim category
  fails the build.
- **Drift gate.** `scripts/omp-manifest.json` records the pinned versions, the
  measured artifact, the shim surface and the hashes of every source the
  transport depends on, plus the shim symbols the esbuild graph actually
  reaches. `tests/build.test.ts` re-checks all of it, and CI asserts the
  committed manifest is unchanged after a build, so an omp bump that changes
  the contract shows up as a reviewable manifest diff before it can reach a
  request.
- **Generated catalogs.** The model tables (`cursor`, `devin`,
  `google-gemini-cli`, `google-antigravity`) are generated from the pinned
  catalog and are not hand-edited. An omp or catalog bump requires
  `pnpm -C packages/llm-omp run generate:catalog`.

## Limits and risks

- **Unofficial Cursor client.** The transport reuses Cursor's vendor-internal
  OAuth client id and announces a released CLI build through the
  `x-cursor-client-version` / `x-cursor-client-type` request identity. The MIT
  license covers the code, not the service, so relying on this client carries a
  terms-of-service (ToS) risk. If Cursor gates non-IDE clients (a `401`/`403`
  on `Run` with a valid account), this transport stops until the product
  decision recorded as stop condition **S4**.
- **Real endpoints unverified.** The login, poll, refresh and agent endpoint
  shapes are ported from the pinned omp sources; this repository's tests replay
  recorded fixtures and never call Cursor, so live behavior is unverified until
  it is exercised against a real account.
- **In-process checkpoint cache.** Per-conversation checkpoints live in a
  module-level, in-process LRU (128 conversations) inside the bundled omp
  transport. Nothing is persisted: an evicted or lost checkpoint rebuilds from
  the request history, exactly like the first request after a restart, and a
  multi-step tool turn must replay its history.
- **Image input is advertised as text-only.** Forwarding is future work; until
  it lands the projection refuses non-text blocks instead of silently dropping
  them. 100 of the pinned catalog's 123 rows claim image support but are
  advertised text-only.
- **Tool handoff uses DSH's external-executor mode.** A turn that needs a tool
  stops at the handoff; the result is only replayed on the follow-up request.
  Tool declarations travel as MCP definitions, and `toolHistory` is accepted
  but cannot be replayed (the active tool set is the projection).
- **Colliding DSH tools are aliased, not dropped.** The transport keeps
  Cursor's own `read`/`bash`/`write`/`delete`/`ls`/`grep`/`todo` names off the
  MCP advertisement, so a DSH tool with one of those names is advertised as
  `dsh_<name>`; the event stream restores the DSH name on the tool call, while
  history replay keeps the advertised alias so the follow-up request stays
  consistent. The seven `dsh_<native>` names are reserved: a DSH tool that
  already carries one is refused with `TOOL_ALIAS_COLLISION`, which fails the
  whole request and requires renaming the tool. Any other tool name travels
  unchanged. Cursor-native exec frames (`read`, `shell`, `write`, `delete`,
  `grep`, `ls`, `diagnostics`, streamed edits) are still answered by the
  transport with `Tool not available` and are **not** executed by DSH (live
  reachability unverified).
- **Advisory request knobs are ignored.** Cursor's agent protocol has no field
  for an output cap, sampling temperature, stop sequences or an auxiliary-call
  purpose; DSH's `maxTokens`, `temperature`, `stop` and `purpose` never reach
  the wire, and Cursor applies the catalog output limit server-side.
- **Unofficial Devin client.** The transport presents the released Devin CLI
  identity (`ideName: "devin-cli"`, `ideType: "chisel"`, `ideVersion:
  "3000.11.3"`) and a `connect-go` client header the omp sources copy from the
  CLI. Same posture as Cursor's S4: a first live turn rejected with `401`/`403`
  stops the route until a product decision, never a retry under another
  identity.
- **Attribution deviates on one call.** The Devin chat request must keep the
  transport's own `connect-go` client header — the backend gates on it. The
  header-less `GetUserJwt` handshake has no identity of its own, so the adapter
  fills DSH's attribution `user-agent` only where a header is absent. Cursor's
  requests keep full attribution.
- **Devin has no refresh.** The pinned rule declares `refresh "none"`, so the
  record is a static bearer with a derived `expires` (JWT `exp` minus five
  minutes, else one year). An expired or corrupt record is `REAUTH_REQUIRED`,
  not renewed. Because the omp loopback listener is Bun-only and the browser
  half is untestable offline, the flow is paste-only for now; a bare pasted
  code skips the state check (the page is the only place the state could
  travel).

- **The Factory Droid artifact strips the registry-derived env-key map.** Its graph would
  otherwise pull omp's whole provider registry, so one entry-scoped substitution keeps the
  pin's `getEnvApiKey` but not the `PROVIDER_REGISTRY` half — the computed Foundry/ADC/Bedrock
  resolvers are gone. That path is unreachable for this route (every request carries the
  stored WorkOS token), and a catalog-declared plain variable (`OPENAI_API_KEY`, …) still
  resolves. The install id is per-process rather than persisted for the same reason: the
  transport must not write to a user's home.
- **Unofficial Google clients.** The Google routes reuse the OAuth clients and
  client identities the pinned omp rules capture — Gemini CLI
  (`GeminiCLI/0.46.0/...` plus `Client-Metadata`) and Antigravity
  (`antigravity/hub/<version> ...`). Same posture as the Cursor and Devin
  routes: the MIT license covers the code, not the service, and a first live
  turn rejected with `401`/`403` on a valid token stops the route until a
  product decision (stop condition **S4**) — never a retry under another
  identity.
- **Antigravity version lookup.** Before the first Antigravity request the
  artifact reads the client version from the public update manifest (D11),
  because the backend gates newer models on that version. A failed lookup is
  silent and falls back to the pinned `2.19.1` for ten minutes; an explicit
  `PI_AI_ANTIGRAVITY_VERSION` skips the lookup. That is the only outbound
  request the routes make besides the vendor API itself.
- **Google sign-in waits at most five minutes.** The loopback listener is
  bounded by a wait budget (five minutes by default): a browser that never
  returns fails the attempt with `AUTH_FAILED`, closes the socket and commits
  nothing. An aborted attempt is reported as a cancellation, not a failure.
  When the configured port is taken, the fallback is an ephemeral port; a host
  that can bind neither fails the sign-in rather than silently dropping the
  browser half (pasting still works only while the listener is up).
- **Google attribution deviates on both routes.** The Cloud Code Assist wire
  sets a vendor `user-agent` that the backend gates on, so DSH's attribution
  `user-agent` is filled only where a request left the header absent — the same
  fill-absent wrapper the Devin handshake uses.
- **Real Google endpoints unverified.** The wire suite drives the bundled
  transport end to end over a stubbed `fetch` (URL, envelope, headers, SSE,
  in-band errors, Antigravity failover and the version manifest), but it never
  calls Google. A first live sign-in and turn is a manual smoke check, not a
  claim of server acceptance.

## Develop and test

```sh
pnpm -C packages/llm-omp typecheck
pnpm -C packages/llm-omp build
pnpm -C packages/llm-omp test
pnpm -C packages/llm-omp run generate:catalog
```

`build` bundles the pinned omp graphs from `scripts/omp-entry.ts`,
`scripts/omp-entry-devin.ts` and `scripts/omp-entry-google.ts` into
`lib/omp/cursor.mjs`, `lib/omp/devin.mjs` and `lib/omp/google.mjs` and rewrites
`scripts/omp-manifest.json`; run it before `test` after a pin or shim change. CI runs the same sequence and then fails if
the committed manifest drifted.

The install proof lives at the repository root and needs `pnpm` and `dsh` on
`PATH`:

```sh
node scripts/verify-install.mjs
```

It packs both packages, installs the root tarball into a fresh DSH profile,
and asserts that the composed profile carries both loader rows
(`dsh-keys-manager` and `llm-omp-transports`). It does not exercise the
plugin-manager UI or any provider network behavior.

## Release

This package is released from the same release PR and carries the same version
as `dsh-keys-manager`; the root `CHANGELOG.md` and its generated sections cover
the root package only. A release-prep run writes one version to both
`package.json` files, and the Release workflow publishes both and pushes the
`dsh-llm-omp-transports@<version>` tag.
The root [release docs](../../docs/release.md) describe the full flow.

Package documentation is English-only; the root `README.md` /
`README.zh-CN.md` and the root `docs/*.zh-CN.md` files carry the bilingual
plugin surface.

# DSH Keys Manager

[![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/dsh-keys-manager)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-keys-manager)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%5E22.19%20%7C%7C%20%3E%3D24-339933)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-keys-manager)
[![DSH](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-%5E0.2.1--rc.4-0969DA)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm)

**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that turns one provider API key into a managed pool.
It extends the Models page rather than replacing it: providers, models, and the
model picker stay where they are; only the API-key source moves behind the
manager.

## What it does

**Pool and routing**

- Several keys per provider, each with an alias and a health state.
- One key pinned to a session, round-robin for new sessions; a failing request
  is retried on its key, then moved to another key.
- Exponential cooldown recovery, capped at seven days.

**Accounts and sign-in**

- Seven pi-ai OAuth providers can join the pool as an account instead of a
  pasted key.
- Two more sign in through the plugin's own bundled clients: Kilo and Z.AI
  Coding Plan.
- Seven companion transport routes for providers the vendored pi-ai cannot
  speak: Cursor, Devin, the two Google routes, Factory Droid, and the two
  GitLab Duo routes.

**Interface**

- A search-driven Keys Manager page on the plugin's own detail page.
- A "managed by Keys Manager" badge inside the existing Models provider cards.
- Extra built-in providers installed as ordinary `llm-pi-ai` routes — 35 of
  them, listed under [Provider coverage](#provider-coverage).

## Quick start

### Install

In the Desktop or Web app, open **Plugins → Add plugin**, enter `dsh-keys-manager`,
click **Install**, then **Enable now**. This installs the same published package
as the CLI path, already carrying its built bundle.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-keys-manager
```

One install yields both bundles, `dsh-keys-manager` and `llm-omp-transports`;
enable both — the manager owns credentials and routing, the transport the seven
routes' wire protocols. Refresh the Web page afterwards for the browser half.

<details>
<summary>Install from a local checkout</summary>

```sh
git clone https://github.com/btspoony/dsh-keys-manager
cd dsh-keys-manager
pnpm i
dsh plugin --profile web link .
```

`add` installs the published tarball with its built `lib/` and client bundle;
`link .` builds them via `prepare` during `pnpm i`, as does `prepack` when packing.

</details>

## Use it

### Take over a provider and add keys

1. Search for a provider. Open **Plugins → Keys Manager → View** (`Plugins →
   密钥管理 → 查看` in the Chinese locale); the manager renders on the plugin's
   detail page. Existing DSH providers appear first; the plugin also ships the
   curated extra catalog described under [Provider coverage](#provider-coverage).
2. Adopt a provider. For an existing provider the manager imports the
   currently resolved credential, writes a broker reference into the provider
   profile, and leaves the original key in the credential store so release can
   restore it.
3. Add more keys with an alias. Every key is stored in the Harness credential
   store under its own reference; the manager state document never contains a
   key literal.
4. Manage a key from the three-dot menu: rename, pause/resume, delete. A key
   row shows status, last use, and the recovery time while cooling.
5. Tune retry count (1–3), base cooldown, and recovery grace in the settings
   card.

### Accounts and sign-in

Providers that ship a native OAuth sign-in offer two ways to join the pool:
**Add key** stores a static API key, while **Add account** runs the provider's
OAuth sign-in flow and stores the result as an account row in the same pool.
Nine routes join as an **account**: seven through pi-ai's own flows, `kilo` and
`zai` through the plugin's bundled clients (device code, pasted `zcode://`
redirect), which mint a **static** credential renewed only by **Sign in again**.

| Route group | How it joins | Refresh / renew |
|---|---|---|
| 9 OAuth accounts | **Add account** — seven pi-ai flows, two plugin clients | provider-managed for the seven; **Sign in again** for the two static credentials |
| 7 transport routes | **Transport accounts** — one grant per route | see [Transport routes](#transport-routes) |

**API keys form the selection ring** — sticky sessions, round-robin, retry
failover and cooldowns operate across the provider's keys — while **one
projected OAuth grant serves its provider**, and an account row's counters
reflect only that account's own successes and failures. Per-account ranking is
future work. When the projected grant fails, the account cools down and the
pool falls back to its keys, or stops serving on an OAuth-only route until a
manual re-login.

**`muse-code` needs no transport or account row of its own**: the vendored pi-ai
`meta` route (`openai-responses` on `https://api.meta.ai/v1`) serves it, the
agreement check was static, and the first live call is a manual smoke check per
[Known limits](docs/known-limits.md).

### Transport routes

Providers the vendored pi-ai cannot speak are served by the companion
`dsh-llm-omp-transports` component:

- One grant per route, at `llm-omp-transports/<route>` — no key pool and no
  per-account rotation. Sign-in happens in the **Transport accounts** section of
  the Keys Manager page.
- Models are generated from the pinned `@oh-my-pi/pi-catalog@18.12.3` table when
  the transport is built, and the clients are unofficial: read the
  [transports package docs](packages/llm-omp/README.md) and its
  [known limits](packages/llm-omp/docs/known-limits.md) before relying on them.

| Route | Sign-in | Refresh | Model rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | browser page + poll | on the credential seam | 123 |
| `devin` | paste the landed callback URL | none — sign in again | 2 |
| `google-gemini-cli` | loopback `8085` + paste fallback | on the credential seam | 7 |
| `google-antigravity` | loopback `51121` + paste fallback | on the credential seam | 22 |
| `factory-droid` | WorkOS device code (URL + user code) | one refresh in a 60 s window, keeps `orgId`/`region` | 62 |
| `gitlab-duo` | PKCE loopback `localhost:8080/callback`, no port fallback, paste fallback | one refresh in a 60 s window | 16 |
| `gitlab-duo-agent` | paste the `vscode://` URL | one refresh, echoes the `vscode` redirect | 1 |

<details>
<summary>Per-route notes</summary>

- **Cursor** — streams text and reasoning and hands tool calls to DSH's tool
  loop; images are refused with a typed error. The client presents Cursor's
  vendor-internal OAuth identity.
- **Devin** — no refresh: a static bearer whose expiry is derived from the token
  (JWT `exp` minus five minutes, else one year), and without a readable expiry
  the row shows `active` with a blank countdown column.
- **Google routes** — both share one generated `lib/omp/google.mjs` artifact yet
  keep separate grants, account rows and catalogs. The grant is
  `{access, refresh, expires, projectId, email?}`; sign-in resolves the Cloud
  project the route bills, and a `legacy-tier` or paid account whose project
  cannot be discovered fails `AUTH_FAILED` until `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` (or
  `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT_ID`) is set.
- **Factory Droid** — four

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
荣哥技能卷轴收藏馆

Ronge's Adaptive Skill Cockpit（沉浸式体验版）

不是「最大的技能库」，而是「最懂你此刻该用哪个技能的驾驶舱」——本地、可解释、会记住效果。

🌐 在线落地页 / Landing page


会话右侧的「技能」抽屉：6,399 条公开 SKILL.md 索引、上下文推荐、正在使用、经验与自进化都在这里。

## 30 秒开始 ```bash # 1) 安装（在任意 DSH 会话里让 Agent 执行；npm 发布前建议用 GitHub tag） plugin_manager install_bundle target=git+https://github.com/bugtakue/ronge-adaptive-skill-archive.git#v2.1.2 # 2) 打开任意会话 → 右上角「技能」→ 右侧抽屉 # 3) 顶部切换「计划模式 / 沉浸模式」，然后正常发任务 ``` --- ## 为什么是「驾驶舱」而不是「货架」 大多数 skill 工具回答的是「有哪些 skill、怎么装」。这个插件回答三个更贴近当下任务的问题： 1. **现在这个项目、这句话，适合用哪个 skill？** —— 结合会话最近内容 + 项目文件名，给出 Top 4 和匹配理由。 2. **我现在到底在用哪些 skill？** —— 从真实的 `skill` 工具调用里读，不靠猜。 3. **哪些做法真的有效？** —— 任务完成后写入经验，你的 👍/👎 会反过来教推荐器。 它不替代 Agent 自己的 skill catalog，只是把「该用哪个」变成一眼可见，并让系统随使用变准。 ### 和同类项目比 > 口径：竞品信息来自其公开文档/README（2026-10 整理），可能随版本变化；本行只比较与本插件重叠的维度。它们在生态规模、跨宿主、企业治理上远超本插件——那是它们的主场，不是我们的。**这是单宿主（DeepSeek Harness）的深度插件，不是通用技能市场。** | 维度 | 本插件 | skills.sh 生态 | Claude Code plugins | DSH 内技能管理插件 | |---|---|---|---|---| | 主形态 | DSH 右侧抽屉，单宿主深做 | 跨 agent 市场 + CLI | 官方插件市场 + skills | 目录 / 搜索 / 启停 / 安装 | | 推荐 + 理由 | 会话上下文 → Top 4，附名称/关键词/类别/经验/手感理由 | 按安装量排行，无用户可见理由 | 模型按 `description` 自动加载，无用户可见排序 | 以列表、搜索为主 | | 正在使用 | 真实 `skill` 工具调用，实时显示 | — | `/skill-doctor` 历史频次、Last used | 部分有使用记录 | | Plan / Immersive | **skill 编排级**双模式：先问 = 计划，不问 = 沉浸 | — | Plan 属权限模式，不针对 skill 选择 | — | | 经验 → 自进化 | 经验记忆 + 👍/👎 归因 + 本地权重学习 + 探索配额 | 安装量统计 | skill-creator 面向作者做评估 | 少数有使用记录，无权重学习 | | 安装前安全 | 本地启发式扫描 + 信任分级 + 许可证 | 合作方审计（Vercel 公布） | 市场分层 + 来源校验 + sha256 | 部分有 trust score | | 更新 / 回滚 | 内容 diff + 更新前备份 + 一键回滚 | lockfile + update | 市场内更新 | 部分有更新检查，回滚少见 | | 数据 / 遥测 | **全本地，无遥测** | 安装遥测默认开启（可关） | 使用数据不回传作者 | 本地 | | 规模口径 | 6,399 条 GitHub 公开 `SKILL.md` 可复核快照（2026-10-28） | 官方博客称 69,000+；站点另有 1.5M 级数字，口径未注明 | 官方 marketplace 精选，未公布总量 | 各家不同 | > 「四项同时具备」的判断来自我们对 28 个相关项目的公开资料梳理（自报口径，欢迎 issue 指正）；如果你发现有项目已做到，告诉我们，我们会更新这张表。 --- ## 核心功能 ### 上下文推荐（带理由） 读取当前会话**最近 8 条用户消息**和**项目根最多 80 个文件名**，对技能的 `name + description + whenToUse` 做本地打分：中英文 token 重叠 + 技能名命中 + 类别线索 + 经验/手感加权，只返回得分 > 0 的 **Top 4**。每条都带结构化理由：命中的名称、关键词、类别、经验次数、「手感」或「探索」。面板打开时每 10 秒静默刷新，不打断输入。 ### 正在使用 / 最近使用 从会话真实的 `skill` 工具调用读取当前 turn 正在用的技能；空闲时显示最近使用。不是分析推测，是工具调用事实。 ### 计划模式 / 沉浸模式 | 模式 | 行为 | |---|---| | **计划模式**（默认） | 下一次任务开始前先给方案和 1–3 个推荐 skill，**先问你确认**，确认后再执行 | | **沉浸模式** | **不询问**，按上下文自动匹配并组合 1–3 个 skill 执行，结束时说明用了哪些、为什么 | 两种模式都是 prompt 级默认行为，不是硬编码固定管线（诚实边界，见文末）。 ### 经验记忆 + 反馈 主会话任务完成、且用了至少一个 skill 时，自动写入一条经验：任务、Skills、结果摘要、耗时、会话。人读的写在 `experience.md`，机读的写在 `experience.json`。推荐分里会加 `min(4, uses × 0.8)`，好评再加、差评再减——用得越稳的 skill 越容易被优先想到。支持跨会话成功率、平均耗时、连续失败，以及经验 JSON 导出/导入。 ### 自进化：10% 探索 + 权重学习 推荐权重不是写死的常数，而是**可学习参数**：反馈会被归因到「产生这条推荐的 top 理由类型」，然后以小步长、有上下界地微调。探索配额保证系统不会「越推荐越窄」：**默认 10% 的推荐位给平时很少被推荐的技能；如果探索长期没人采用会自动调低，采用率高会自动调高（可调范围 0–30%）**。完整参数见下一节。 ### 安装前安全扫描 预览/安装任何第三方 `SKILL.md` 前，在本机跑一遍启发式静态扫描：shell 执行、`curl | bash`、动态解码（eval/base64）、提示注入语句、网络访问、凭据路径、文件写入、过宽 `allowed-tools`。输出低/中/高风险与命中行号，并展示来源信任级别（official / verified / community / local / unknown）和 `license` 字段。**只读文本，不联网、不上传、不执行。** ### 更新 diff / 更新全部 / 回滚 `skills-lock.json` 记录每个已安装 skill 的来源、repo、SHA-256、信任、许可证与时间戳。检查更新时返回**内容 diff**（新增/删除/改动行）；支持单条更新、一键全部更新，更新前自动备份到 `backups//.md`，随时回滚到上一版。 ### 6,399 条卷轴馆 GitHub 公开、可检索的 `SKILL.md` 元数据快照（2026-10-28）：**6,399 条，其中 5,398 条带描述，14 个分类**（AI 2,070 / 编程 789 / 设计 663 / 数据 512 / 其他 1,662 / 视频 163 / 写作 155 / 效率 122 / 办公 86 / 营销 53 / 安全 48 / 研究 41 / 商业 24 / 教育 11）。按分类、最低评分、关键词筛选，预览全文后安装。口径写清楚：这不是「全网所有 skill」，只覆盖 GitHub 上公开可检索到的 `SKILL.md`，且不存正文。 ### MCP 目录 + 小功能 「工具」页浏览 MCP 官方 registry 的服务器（只发现，不自动安装/配置）。另有中英双语技能简介、主任务完成提示音（子智能体/fork 不响）、新建 Skill 到 `~/.dsh/skills/`。 --- ## 越用越好用：机制与参数 ``` 你的反馈（复制 /skill = adopt，👍 / 👎）──归因到理由类型──► 权重微调 ──► 下一次排序更准 ▲ │ └──────────── 经验记忆 + 10% 探索配额持续采样 ◄───────────┘ ``` | 信号 | 记录位置 | 影响 | |---|---|---| | 复制 `/skill`（采用） | `rec-feedback.json` + `kindBySkill` | 归因到产生该推荐的 top 理由类型 | | 👍 / 👎 | 同上，另加类别与技能「手感」 | 同类理由、类别权重、该技能亲和度一起学习 | | 经验条目 👍 / 👎 | `evolution.json` | 通过上次推荐归因，不污染无关技能 | - **评估节奏**：每累计 10 条反馈评估一次；任一理由类型样本 ≥ 8 才调整，冷启动完全不动。 - **权重默认值**：名称 8 / 关键词 1 / 经验 1 / 类别 0.6 / 完成度 1；命中率 ≥ 70% 时 ×1.1、≤ 40% 时 ×0.9（步长 10%），带上下界（如名称 4–14、类别 0.2–1.5）。 - **类别权重**：视频、办公、Harness、通用四类，范围 0.5–2，按你的真实好评/差评调整。 - **探索配额**：默认 10%，范围 0–30%。命中时把推荐末位换成一条用得少的候选（标记「探索」）；累计 20 次探索后，若采用率 < 5% 则降 5%，≥ 30% 则升 5%。 - **护栏**：全部本地、无网络、无模型调用；变更历史最多 50 条，可查看、回滚、重置；不自动删数据。 --- ## 安装 ### 前置 - DeepSeek Harness（Desktop / Web profile） - macOS（提示音用系统 `afplay`；Linux 可改为 `paplay`） - 安装插件需要 `danger-full-access` 或审批 ### 三种方式（profile 级，所有会话生效） | 方式 | 命令 | 适合 | |---|---|---| | **GitHub tag** | `plugin_manager install_bundle target=git+https://github.com/bugtakue/ronge-adaptive-skill-archive.git#v2.1.2` | 现在就能用、固定版本、可审源码 | | **npm** | `plugin_manager install_bundle target=ronge-adaptive-skill-archive@2.1.2` | 已发布到 npm（`ronge-adaptive-skill-archive@2.1.2`，2026-10-29） | | **本地目录** | `plugin_manager install_bundle target="/absolute/path/to/ronge-adaptive-skill-archive"` | 开发、改代码、离线 | ### 升级（v1.x / v2.0.0 → v2.1.0） - 已装 **v2.0.0**：直接覆盖安装 v2.1.0，数据目录、经验与权重沿用。 - 从 **v1.x** 升级：v1.x 与 v2.x 的包名、路由前缀不同，同一 profile 不能同时启用——先移除旧 bundle，再装 v2.1.0；旧数据目录会在首次启动时**自动复制**（旧目录保留，不删除）。 重命名细节见 [v2.0.0 发布说明](docs/release-notes-v2.0.0.md)，v2.1.0 的变更见 [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md)。 ### 数据在哪 | 路径 | 内容 | |---|---| | `~/.dsh/ronge-adaptive-skill-archive/config.json` | 模式（plan / immersive） | | `~/.dsh/ronge-adaptive-skill-archive/experience.md` / `.json` | 经验（人读 / 机读） | | `~/.dsh/ronge-adaptive-skill-archive/evolution.json` | 权重、探索配额、变更历史 | | `~/.dsh/ronge-adaptive-skill-archive/rec-feedback.json` | 推荐反馈 | | `~/.dsh/ronge-adaptive-skill-archive/skills-lock.json` | 安装来源 / SHA-256 / 信任 / 许可证 | | `~/.dsh/ronge-adaptive-skill-archive/backups//.md` | 更新前备份 | | `~/.dsh/skills//SKILL.md` | 已安装 / 新建的技能 | 技能来源（优先级从高到低）：项目 `.dsh/skills` → 项目 `.agents/skills` → profile 目录 → `~/.dsh/skills` → 用户 agents 目录 → 预设包，并合并会话 `ctx.skills` 注册表。 ### 插件市场索引（可选） [docs/plugin-market.json](docs/plugin-market.json) 是 DSH format 1 市场索引，可托管到 https URL 后在 DSH 的自定义插件市场里被发现。发版后运行 `npm run build:market-index` 更新版本。 --- ## 隐私与安全边界 - **推荐、扫描、自进化全部在本机完成**，不调用外部模型或网络；不上传、不写日志、无遥测。 - 推荐只读取当前会话最近的消息和项目根目录文件名；面板显示来自真实工具调用的数据。 - 安装前扫描是**本地启发式提示，不是安全保证**（静态扫描无法覆盖全部攻击面）；安装前仍应预览全文。 - 只允许从 `raw.githubusercontent.com/**/SKILL.md` 拉取，最大 256 KiB，不自动拉脚本/资源，不覆盖已有 skill。 - 新建技能只写入 `~/.dsh/skills//SKILL.md`，名称白名单拒绝 `/`、`..` 和绝对路径。 - MCP 目录只做发现，不自动安装配置；提示音失败不影响任务。 - 换提示音：`export DSH_TASK_CHIME_SOUND=/System/Library/Sounds/Ping.aiff` --- ## 架构 ``` ┌─ DeepSeek Harness ──────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ session header ──[技能]──► 右侧抽屉（client.js，无构建） │ │ │ │ │ │ session events HTTP（仅 loopback，无新端口） │ │ └───────────┬──────────────┘ │ │ ▼ │ │ Host（index.js，仅 Node 内置模块） │ │ catalog · 推荐 · 经验 · 自进化 · 安全扫描 · lock/diff/回滚 │ │ MCP 目录 · 卷轴馆索引 · 提示音 · system prompt 注入 │ │ │ │ │ ~/.dsh/ronge-adaptive-skill-archive/ ← 配置/经验/权重 │ │ ~/.dsh/skills/ ← 安装/新建的 skill │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` Host 只依赖 Node 内置模块；Client 是 plain JS，经 `window.__ModuleLoader__.load` 注册，无需构建、无 JSX。路由只监听 loopback，由 `webServer` 注册。 --- ## 路线图 以下是接下来想补的方向（计划，不是承诺；欢迎 PR 认领）： - **输入框推荐 chips**：面板内 Top 2 chips 已有一键复制 `/skill`，下一步接进 composer。 - **按项目置顶**：每个 workspace 记住常用 skill，打开面板先显示 pinned。 - **本地语义搜索**：词典/本地 embedding 混合，搜「帮我做张海报」也能命中图片类技能。 - **推荐理由三段式**：任务类型 / 项目指纹 / 经验值分组展示，并扩大离线金标集。 - **原生右侧栏 tab 与快捷键**：不再用抽屉，`Cmd+Shift+S` 打开面板。 - **健康报告迭代**：frontmatter 缺失、重名、断链一次标出。 --- ## 贡献 见 [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)。无构建步骤、无运行时依赖；改完跑： ```bash npm run check # 校验 client factory id 与包名一致 npm test # 单元 + 路由 + 迁移测试（不联网） npm run eval:recommend # 离线推荐金标集 Recall@K node --check index.js && node --check client.js ``` 欢迎从 [Issues](https://github.com/bugtakue/ronge-adaptive-skill-archive/issues) 里的「推荐不准」「某个 skill 该降权」开始——这类反馈比 star 更有用。 --- ## License MIT。见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)。 ---

如果这个面板帮你少翻一次目录、少装错一个 skill，欢迎点一个 Star。
也欢迎把「我这里推荐不准」发到 Issues——那是最有价值的反馈。

--- ## English **Ronge's Adaptive Skill Cockpit (Immersive Edition)** is a context-aware, self-evolving skill cockpit for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/bugtakue/ronge-adaptive-skill-archive). A single bundle adds a right-side drawer that answers three questions most skill tools ignore: *which skill fits this task now*, *which skills am I actually using*, and *which ones actually work for me*. - **Contextual recommendations with reasons** — recent session messages + project file names → Top 4, with name / keyword / category / experience / affinity reasons. Local heuristic, no model calls. - **Now using** — read from real `skill` tool calls, not inferred. - **Plan / Immersive modes** — ask-first skill orchestration, or no-ask auto-composition of 1–3 skills. - **Experience memory + feedback** — `experience.md/json`, cross-session success rate, export/import. - **Self-evolution** — feedback-attributed, bounded weight tuning plus a 10% exploration quota; fully local, logged, and rollback-able. - **Pre-install safety scan** — local heuristic scan (shell exec, pipe-to-shell, dynamic eval, prompt injection, credentials, over-broad `allowed-tools`), trust level and license. - **Update center** — content diff, update-all, backup before overwrite, one-click rollback. - **6,399-skill index** — snapshot of public GitHub `SKILL.md` files (14 categories, 1–5 rating), plus a browsable MCP registry and completion chime. **Install** (in a DSH session): ```bash plugin_manager install_bundle target=git+https://github.com/bugtakue/ronge-adaptive-skill-archive.git#v2.1.2 # then open any session → 「技能」in the header → switch Plan / Immersive ``` **Privacy**: everything (recommendations, scans, learning) runs locally; no telemetry, no uploads. The safety scan is a heuristic hint, not a security guarantee. MIT licensed — see [LICENSE](LICENSE) and [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

# dsh-vaultwarden

[English](README.en.md) | 中文

把 **Vaultwarden / Bitwarden** 接入 DeepSeek Harness：每个会话都能按需检索和读取密码库；服务器变更通过 WebSocket 实时同步；请求发出前自动脱敏，落盘日志中的明文可被擦除，并在「设置 → 密码库」提供密码浏览与脱敏看板。

## 界面预览

| 密码库面板 | 脱敏轨迹 |
| --- | --- |
| ![密码库面板](assets/panel-list.png) | ![脱敏轨迹页面](assets/panel-trail.png) |

## 主要能力

- **实时同步**：登录后订阅 SignalR WebSocket，服务器变更即时刷新；不支持 WebSocket 时自动降级轮询并定期重试升级。
- **密码库面板**：分区导航、搜索、列表分页、条目详情、TOTP 倒计时、复制、归档/回收站与可选的写操作。
- **脱敏模式**：工具读取到的密码、TOTP、卡号等以稳定占位符返回；需要明文时按条目 + 字段单次取回。
- **日志擦除**：定期把会话日志中的 Bitwarden 明文替换为 `[REDACTED:BW]`，支持增量扫描与立即擦除。
- **脱敏看板**：按天统计脱敏量，展示脱敏量前三的会话与模型；每根连接线一颗灰色粒子穿过门禁，左灰右蓝分别表示脱敏前/后；底部保留脱敏流水与详情页。
- **安全边界**：面板走宿主已认证的 `/api` connection RPC，插件不注册自己的 HTTP 路由；主密码和 API 密钥是只写字段。

## 安装

```sh
# 最新稳定版（市场条目使用的地址）
dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/BuvkB/dsh-vaultwarden/releases/latest/download/dsh-vaultwarden.tgz

# 或从 npm 安装
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-vaultwarden@latest
```

要求 Node.js >= 22。

## 配置

在 **设置 → 插件 → dsh-vaultwarden** 填写：

| 字段 | 说明 |
| --- | --- |
| `serverUrl` / `email` | Vaultwarden 地址与登录邮箱 |
| `masterPassword` | 主密码；只写，不落浏览器 |
| `apiKeyClientId` / `apiKeyClientSecret` | 可选，API 密钥登录（可绕过两步验证） |
| `accessMode` | `readonly` / `ask` / `auto`，控制模型工具的写回权限 |
| `maskMode` / `sweepMode` | 占位符脱敏与日志擦除开关 |

也支持 `DSH_BITWARDEN_*` 环境变量和 profile 组合配置。完整字段见 [docs/ui-design.md](docs/ui-design.md)。

## 工具

`bitwarden_find` · `bitwarden_get` · `bitwarden_status` · `bitwarden_sync` · `bitwarden_folders` · `bitwarden_create` · `bitwarden_update` · `bitwarden_delete` · `bitwarden_restore`

另有 `bitwarden_sweep` 立即擦除本地会话日志中的明文。

## 脱敏说明

- 占位符形如 `{{BW_PASSWORD_xxxxxxxx}}`，由 HMAC 生成，不可逆；只能引用、比较或按字段取回。
- 脱敏看板与流水详情见 [docs/ui-design.md](docs/ui-design.md)。
- 擦除标记 `[REDACTED:BW]` 表示明文曾经落盘、随后被擦除；它没有可反查的盐。

## 开发

```sh
bash scripts/build.sh        # 全量门禁
node test/client-card.test.mjs
node test/trail.test.mjs
```

发布流程见 [docs/release.md](docs/release.md)。

## 链接

- [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/BuvkB/dsh-vaultwarden/releases)
- [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-vaultwarden)
- [问题反馈](https://github.com/BuvkB/dsh-vaultwarden/issues)

## 许可

MIT。第三方项目见 [THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md](THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md)。

# `third-party-backend` — the D-5 dogfood bundle A third-party backend bundle **as it would be published**: written against the frozen `tui.dsh/v1alpha1` `Backend` contribution family and nothing else — no `@deepseek-ai/*` dependency, no `src/` import, no host service. It is never published; `scripts/verify-backend-assembly.ts` installs it into a throwaway profile and drives the real assembly chain over it. What a bundle must get right, and where each piece lives here: | Piece | Why | File | |---|---|---| | `dsh.bundle.patch` | Only an installed package whose `package.json` declares it becomes a profile *layer* (`dsh.profile.bundles`), and that list is what the D-1 assembly reads | `package.json`, `cordis.patch.yml` | | package-root `dsh-plugin.json` | The declaration the host admits; it counts only beside the `package.json` that establishes the entry's package root (#1568) | `dsh-plugin.json` | | `contributes['x-dsh-tui']` with `kind: 'Backend'` | The writing surface: `apiVersion` + `kind` + contribution `id` + `name` + `spec` (`spec.id` is the backend id) | `dsh-plugin.json` | | handler export named `backend` | The registry's documented default (`backendExport` is in-tree only, so a declaration cannot name another export) | `backend.js` | | `spec.unloadExport` | Module-level/process-wide pools only; session-scoped resources belong to `session.dispose()` | `dsh-plugin.json` → `backend.js` | | `exports: { ".": "./backend.js" }` | Resolution goes through the entry the Loader's own resolver picks — an `exports` map that hides `./package.json` is fine on purpose | `package.json` | A bundle currently declares one backend: the fixed `backend` export must pass the handler assertion and carry the same id as `spec.id`. Multiple declarations are refused, as are manifests whose canonical projection rejects duplicate contribution identities. Entries awaiting authorization are not probed or loaded. The full field semantics are in [`notes/0009-backend-contribution.md`](../../../tui-profile/notes/0009-backend-contribution.md) and the seam write-up in [`docs/plugin-admission-and-development.md`](../../../tui-profile/docs/plugin-admission-and-development.md) (接缝十四). The published type face is exported from this package's entry (`BackendSpec`, `validateBackendSpec`, `backendAdmission`, …). This fixture stops at the picker: `detect()` says honestly that it ships no runtime, and `open()` refuses. Everything past the assembly chain — detection, sessions, catalogs, the install wizard — is a real backend's own work. `closeEchoPool()` is inert (there is no runtime to close) but counts its calls, and `echoPoolCloseCount()` exposes that count read-only. The regression reads it through the Loader's own module instance, so it observes that the host closes the declared pool exactly once, only for a backend it actually loaded.

# dsh-TUI > An interactive terminal UI for DeepSeek Harness. It ships a pixel-whale > header, live work status, streaming thinking, double-Esc time rewind, a > context progress bar, and a TPS gauge. Zero core changes: it consumes only > DSH's public exports, and is moving from a mounted plugin to an app with its > own entry and composition root, where DSH loads in process as the first-party > backend. Install to enable; uninstall leaves no patches behind. The prompt footer hides completed goals once the turn is idle; the Todo side panel retains their history. `Ctrl+Q` folds todos while working and hides/restores the idle goal/todo footer. Clicking its todo header also hides it while idle. Hiding changes only this display: a new goal/todo snapshot or session reveals it again, and `/goal clear` does not clear todos. Split diff cards give one-sided additions and deletions the full body width, without an empty opposite pane. Ordinary edits remain side by side, and mixed files choose their layout separately before folding or streaming reveal. Compaction status stays on one line in narrow panes: phase and cancellation hints yield first, then the label is shortened; elapsed time is shown only as a complete field. Image files referenced with `@path` use the same admission and resize/conversion policy as pasted images. Adjustment notices report the stored dimensions and format; required animation conversion is refused instead of dropping frames. Mention images and staged images still share count and stored-byte limits in source order. ## Highlights Panels without a verified Component identity are temporary: settings show their title and a distinct number for this run. The default reasoning-effort setting offers the current backend/model’s declared tiers, including custom IDs. On DSH, Auto follows the saved `/effort` choice, then the configured effort, then the model default. Claude/Codex retain backend preferences for Auto at startup and for resumed sessions; explicitly choosing Auto resets the model default. Explicit settings changes affect the next request; unsupported preferences fall back with a notice and are never forced onto a route. Resuming a DSH session preserves its recorded reasoning effort (or its live selection when reattaching). The saved default seeds new sessions; explicit `/effort` and effort-default settings changes still apply to the current session’s next request. - **Pixel whale pet** — three startup intros, click to wake; freezes after the first task. - **Launchpad and first-run guide** — every ordinary launch lands on a landing page with a **real input box** (big text + whale + quick actions, dropping whole blocks on short/narrow terminals; whale-girl images use a compact native-canvas footprint instead of leaving a large gap before the title; on by default — /settings `launchpad` off boots straight into chat); command completion matches chat: `Tab` fills the input, `Enter` runs the command and clears it. The first run walks a four-step wizard (API key / language+theme / model+workspace / shortcuts), re-runnable with `/setup`. - **Terminal-native UI** — streaming Markdown, tool cards, `/` and `@` completion, `#L12-14` ranges, history search, zh/en UI. - **Task completion notifications** — DSH, Claude and Codex notify after successful live work settles, with no queued follow-up or active goal. The title is “dsh-TUI · Task complete”; the body shows the latest settled reply as a single-line plain-text preview (Markdown formatting removed, up to 200 characters). OSC 777/9 apply an additional 2048-byte sequence budget, including title and protocol bytes, preserving whole graphemes. No reply shows only the title; BEL only rings. `/settings` → Conversation: `taskNotifications` = `unfocused` (default), `always`, or `off`; `notificationMethod` = `auto` (default), `osc9`, `bel`, or `windows`. Auto uses separate title/body fields on Ghostty/WezTerm (OSC 777) and Kitty (OSC 99); iTerm2/Warp and explicit `osc9` use a title prefix; other terminals ring the bell; delivery follows your terminal's notification/bell settings. On local Windows, `auto` resolves to `windows`, the system's native notifications: a task-completion toast. The first toast registers that user's AppUserModelID under HKCU, the toast appears about 3 seconds after the task ends (the PowerShell cold start that buys the no-extra-install route), and for DSH sessions an enabled, active external DSH notification plugin in the running profile makes dsh-TUI yield to it (no toast, no bell); an installed but disabled plugin does not suppress notifications; if that AppUserModelID cannot be written, the notification falls back to the bell instead of going silent. SSH sessions keep the attached terminal's notification protocol in `auto` mode; explicit `windows` still selects the host's native transport. tmux requires `set -g allow-passthrough on` for OSC notifications and `set -g focus-events on` for focus reporting. Terminals without focus reporting need `always`. Replay, cancellation and failures do not notify. Works in inline and fullscreen modes. - **Native cursor** — focused text inputs inherit your terminal's cursor shape, color, blinking, and enabled animation or trail effects in both inline and fullscreen modes. The `/model` picker shows the same cursor during movement between provider tabs, model rows, and effort levels, then hides it after **0.5 seconds at rest**; clipped regions fall back to the model row. The session manager also moves this cursor between the workspace rail, session rows, and search box; typing claims the search caret, and navigation returns it to the focused row. Configure animation and trail effects in your terminal. - **Images** — Kitty/Sixel thumbnails, centered preview with zoom and pan, paste-time fitting, text fallback. Kitty images scale to the reserved cells' physical pixels, including on HiDPI terminals. - **Mermaid diagrams** — ````mermaid ```` fences drawn as Unicode diagrams. - **LaTeX math** — `$…$` and `$$…$$` formulas as Unicode text, fractions and limits stacked in display blocks; `mathRendering: image` typesets block and one-row inline formulas as terminal images on graphics terminals. - **Timeline rail** — every turn clickable; timeline / scrollbar / hidden gutter. - **Side panel** — `Ctrl+B` splits the chat with a panel column once the terminal is wide enough; drag the divider to resize it. In the `todo` panel a long goal wraps to the panel width with its phase on a separate row; when the content exceeds the viewport, focus the panel and scroll with `↑`/`↓` or the wheel (every todo is reachable too) (the compact goal row above the chat input stays a single truncated line with a hover tooltip). - **Live state** — activity animation, context bar, TPS, cache hit rate, effort, tokens, session cost estimate (main + subagents), Git and session metadata. Title, trajectory-strip and session-state animations update independently of the transcript and pause when idle or unfocused. Context-bar fill follows backend occupancy; colors estimate content composition. Compaction clears obsolete estimates, and missing composition displays a single used block with a measured used count in both hover details. - **One session manager** — `/resume` `/home` `/agentview` `/bg` `⌸`. - **Session workflow** — `/new` `/compact` `/export` `/btw`, model hot-switch, fork, rewind, vim, fullscreen draft editor. `/btw` uses an overlay when its sidebar cannot render. Main-task questionnaires and the fullscreen draft editor take priority while preserving the side question and draft. - **IDE selection channel** — a VS Code selection lands in the prompt. - **DSH integrations** — presets, skills, MCP, goals, todos, subagents, questionnaires. - **Account sign-in** — the standard profile offers pi-ai OAuth for ChatGPT/Codex, Claude, and Grok (plus OpenAI direct and Meta Muse when available), and Host-owned DeepSeek browser sign-in as `deepseek-account` on DSH 0.2.0-rc.1+. Use `/provider` or `/auth` without another plugin. A profile-only update from a global TUI patch that already mounts `dsh-tui-auth` can still start the official loopback callback listener on demand; fixed-port SSH forwarding still requires the global package to be aligned. - **Extensions** — browser interaction, computer use and more. - **Built for long sessions** — event-driven projection, virtualization, bounded caches. Keys and commands: [Interaction and commands](docs/interaction.en.md). Everything else: [documentation index](docs/README.md). Plugin side panels stay enabled when unrelated settings change. Editing the enabled panel list still applies your explicit selection. Workspace side-panel counts match the session manager: the current conversation counts; empty logs, subagents, fork ancestors and archived sessions do not. Registered workspaces with no visible conversations remain at zero. Loading and read errors are shown separately; press `r` to refresh. When a DSH 0.2.1+ Agent moves its session to another directory (the `working_directory` tool or a Git worktree), the status line, Git branch, `@` completion, `!` commands, clicked paths, skill commands and loaded context follow it, including after `/resume`. The session stays registered under the project it started in. Relative paths in cards rendered before a move resolve against the session's current directory when clicked; absolute paths keep their target. Fullscreen mouse selection stays in the pane where the gesture starts, including chat, sidebar and either diff column. Diagonal, word and line selection copy that pane’s text; soft wraps join independently, source newlines remain, and divider drags only resize. ## Preview

## Quick Start ### Windows one-click installer (x64) Download `dsh-tui-setup-win-x64.exe` from [Releases](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI/releases) and run it. Per-user, no administrator, fully offline, and no preinstalled Node or DSH. ### Command-line installation Prerequisites: [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en) and [deepseek-harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). The `deepseek-official` API-key route needs `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`. On DSH 0.2.0-rc.1+, the standard profile can instead use `/auth login deepseek-account` and select the separate account route through `/model`. Other supported accounts can sign in through `/provider` or `/auth` after startup. The primary compatibility target is DSH `0.2.1-rc.3`. This adapter supports its Shell API, V4 session messages, declarative presets, and profile-backed settings; older supported hosts retain their compatibility paths. See [configuration](docs/configuration.en.md). On DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 and later, `/settings` also selects DeepSeek Search / Fetch APIs and edits their endpoint and result limits, supporting custom Loader entry IDs and a masked API key input saved through DSH's credential store. Official Flash model labels show the `1017` release marker while retaining the `deepseek-flash` model ID. `/settings` groups its sections into pages: the TUI's own settings sit under **General**, and plugins that declare a page get their own tab (`Tab` / `Shift+Tab`, or a click on the strip in fullscreen, switches pages; the strip is hidden when only one page exists). On DSH 0.1.7, `/settings` uses the TUI's actual Loader entry ID, including custom IDs. It requires matching profile dependencies with `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` 3.18.3 or newer; an incompatible schema stops TUI startup with repair guidance instead of showing an uneditable settings page. Older hosts keep their legacy settings scope. The `dsh-tui` section of `/settings` is saved in `~/.dsh-tui/settings.json`, shared by every kernel; the first launch imports it once from the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (and an older host's `~/.dsh/settings.yaml`) (see [configuration](docs/configuration.en.md#tui-configuration)). ```sh # Install the CLI and this plugin globally (ships the dsh-tui command) npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui # Start (first run auto-initializes the profile; needs pnpm) dsh-tui # Both `dsh-tui` and the short `dst` alias start the same TUI. dst ``` Manual alternative: `dsh plugin --profile dsh-tui add @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui`. The repo's `sh install.sh` runs that step and checks the required commands. Afterwards `dsh-tui` and `dsh --profile dsh-tui` are equivalent. > **New-user note**: pnpm ≥11 blocks dependencies with install scripts by > default and reports `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS`. Updates skip foreign-platform > natives — the `@img/sharp-*` packages and the Claude SDK's per-platform > bundles — so only this machine's binaries are fetched. `/update` and > `dsh-tui update` write both settings automatically. An update never installs > the Claude SDK on its own: it enters a profile only when you pick that > backend in the kernel picker, which then installs the pinned SDK for the > running platform. No manual step needed. Details: > [Getting started](docs/getting-started.en.md#pnpm-install-script-blocks-and-foreign-platform-natives). After startup the TUI checks for newer versions in the background. It never blocks the first frame. Type `/update` for a one-shot upgrade. It restarts automatically and resumes the current session. See [Getting started](docs/getting-started.en.md) for the profile lifecycle, source builds, and troubleshooting, including migration from the former `dsh-cc-tui` package. ### CLI Automation: `dst -p "task"`, `dst run --json`, `dst session list --json`. The independent engine does not load the TUI or inherit its profile/preferences; it uses official DSH headless/services (validated on 0.2.0-rc.2, 0.2.1-rc.2 and 0.2.1-rc.3). `dst cli --help` lists its commands; `dst dsh ` forwards native DSH. See [Automation CLI](docs/cli.en.md) for protocol, limits, resume restrictions, and Node/Python/PowerShell integration examples. | Command | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `dsh-tui` / `dst` | Start the TUI; `dst` is a short alias for the same program | | `dsh-tui --resume [id]` · `dsh-tui update` · `dsh-tui doctor` | Resume a session · update the profile and align the launcher · pre-flight environment checks | | `dsh-tui safe` | Read-only diagnostics, plugin inventory and repair guidance; `safe --rescue` builds a clean rescue profile | | `dsh-tui version` · `dsh-tui help` | Launcher and profile versions and usage; both work even without a `dsh` install | Leading DSH options such as `--dump-config` and `--patch ` are forwarded unchanged; other arguments go to the app in `dsh --profile dsh-tui`. Use `dsh-tui -- --resume=sid-1 ./notes` to send `--resume=sid-1 ./notes` as literal prompt text, without selecting a session or workspace. When invoking DSH directly, use `dsh --profile dsh-tui -- -- --resume=sid-1 ./notes`: the first `--` belongs to DSH, the second to the app. Host options can precede a literal prompt: `dsh-tui --patch ./overlay.yml -- --resume=sid-1` applies the overlay and sends `--resume=sid-1` as prompt text without resuming that session. Safe mode: [Getting started](docs/getting-started.en.md). ### Importing conversations from other agents (`dsh-tui migrate`) Bring Claude Code, Codex, OMP, zcode, or Grok Build conversation histories into the DSH session store, then browse and resume them by their original working directory via `/resume`: ```sh dsh-tui migrate # list importable counts per agent (writes nothing) dsh-tui migrate claude-code # import every Claude Code conversation (likewise codex / omp / zcode / grok-build) dsh-tui migrate codex --dry-run # preview what would land, write nothing ``` - **Read-only source**: migration only reads the foreign agent's local store; artifacts are written through the official `JsonlSessionPersistence` backend, so imported sessions are first-class (openable, continuable). - **Idempotent**: one deterministic UUID per source conversation — re-importing skips what is already present instead of stacking duplicates. - **Structure preserved**: user/assistant messages, reasoning traces, tool calls with their results, and the source's context compactions (as native compaction checkpoints) are rebuilt turn by turn; harness-injected machine text opens no turn. An imported session can pick the work straight up. In-TUI browsing: the session screen (`/resume`) shows a tab per agent that has conversations; picking one imports just that conversation and opens it. In-TUI: `/migrate` (optionally `/migrate [--dry-run]`) runs the same import in a child process and reports through the notification flow. CLI alternative: `dsh-tui migrate ...` from any shell runs the same import. Full guide: [Session migration](docs/migrate.en.md). - More agents (pi, opencode, …) extend the adapter registry as adapters land; grok-build reads `GROK_HOME` when set. **VS Code**: use the integrated terminal or the `dsh-tui-vscode` extension. See [VS Code guide](docs/vscode.en.md). **Herdr**: run `dsh-tui` in a [Herdr](https://herdr.dev) pane; `idle` / `working` / `blocked` are reported through its local integration API. **Any terminal**: dsh-tui reports `idle` / `working` / `blocked` / `done` / `error` over the pty with [OSC 7501 (Program Status Protocol)](https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/build/program-status), so terminals and agentic inboxes that implement it can show what the session is doing; terminals that do not implement it ignore the sequence. Set `DSH_TUI_PROGRAM_STATUS=0` to turn it off. Bare `--resume` (`-c`, `--continue`) reopens the last session of the backend this launch selected. Startup recovery only ever targets that backend: a backend with no last session, or a derived target that belongs to a different backend than the one that actually booted (an unknown backend id falling back to DSH, `--backend` naming a backend that is not installed, a remembered kernel that is not the marker's source), refuses with a clear error and exit code 1 — never a silent cold start, never another backend's session, never a new session. An explicit `--resume ` passes that id to the selected backend as-is. The one exception is safe mode's "retry normal startup": it retries the kernel and session recorded in `last-run.json`, so a record whose backend is gone degrades to a warning plus a cold start — that retry is the last way back. ### Experimental: Claude backend dsh-TUI can also run its session on Claude: the same interface, driving the Claude Code CLI through the Claude Agent SDK. Your project's `CLAUDE.md`, settings, hooks, MCP servers and plugins load as the CLI loads them. ```sh # once, in the dsh-tui profile directory (the SDK is an optional dependency) cd ~/.dsh/profiles/dsh-tui && pnpm add @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk@0.3.287 dsh-tui --backend claude # or pick Claude in /kernel; that choice is remembered ``` The easiest install: open the kernel picker (the launchpad "Kernel" entry or `/kernel`) and press Enter on the dim Claude row — the wizard locates the profile directory and installs the pinned SDK for you; the command above is its manual equivalent. The confirmation shows the exact package and version. Closing the wizard, including clicking outside it on the launchpad, cancels a pending installation. - **Sign-in**: a `/channel` relay profile, your dsh-auth `anthropic` sign-in (`/login`), `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or cloud-provider variables, or an existing `claude login`, in that order. A `claude` on `PATH` is used when present, then one in the native install directory under your home (`~/.local/bin`, or `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin` on Windows); every candidate has to launch and report a version, and the SDK's bundled binary is used only when none does. - **Works**: streaming, tool cards, approvals and questions, `/model`, `/effort`, Claude's permission modes (`/permission`, `Shift+Tab`), `/compact`, `/context`, `/mcp`, `/resume`, `/fork`, double-`Esc` rewind, subagents, background jobs, images, `/btw`, and the USD cost Claude reports. - **Not available**: DSH-only commands such as `/tree`, `/preset`, `/provider`, `/workspace`, `/agentview` and `/bg`. One process runs one backend; `/kernel` switches by restarting into a new session. - **Startup**: the screen appears before the session opens, with only a light profile composed (this package plus the profile's third-party plugins); see [Claude backend](docs/claude-backend.en.md#known-limitations). The DSH kernel starts from the same entry and loads DSH in the same process behind its first screen; `DSH_TUI_HOST_ENTRY=0` restores the old launch path for every kernel. Details and known limitations: [Claude backend](docs/claude-backend.en.md). ### Experimental: native Codex backend Run your own Codex through `codex app-server`, sharing its configuration, login, instructions, skills, hooks, MCP and native threads: ```sh npm install -g @openai/codex@0.160.1 dsh-tui --backend codex dsh-tui --backend codex --resume ``` Protocol baseline **0.160.1**, minimum **0.144.0**; other versions may show drift. `CODEX_EXECUTABLE` selects a binary; `/kernel` remembers the backend. `codex resume ` can open the same thread after the other writer exits. This is not `migrate codex`, which imports history into DSH. With native credentials, a writer conflict for an idle thread retained by the official background server triggers a reconnection to that server. Managed subscription credentials and `/channel` connections use private app-server processes. Streaming/tool cards, approvals, questions, steer/queue/interrupt, model and effort controls, Plan, `/review`, `/diff`, `/usage`, `/init`, skills and MCP share the existing UI. Async questions open the questionnaire while Codex continues working; answers steer the turn (or queue if unavailable), and dismissing the question leaves work running. **Shift+Tab only toggles Plan**, keeping its underlying permission preset; Full Access requires an explicit choice. Existing Codex settings are respected, not overwritten with defaults. `/login` offers ChatGPT OAuth, a device code or an API key (the last writes to Codex’s own credential store). Relay `/channel` connections take precedence; managed subscription tokens are only injected on first-party routes. dsh-TUI does not write `~/.codex/config.toml` or log out your native Codex account. A provider `env_key` from your own config (e.g. `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`) that the shell did not export is injected from the DSH credential store when the ref is stored there — the active store first, then the default `~/.dsh` one — so keep the key in the store, no per-shell export needed. When nothing can supply it, the session still starts and the reason is reported once as a start notice: Codex itself rejects every turn of that provider. For Claude and Codex, `/channel` tokens (`CHANNEL_*` refs) belong to the active `DSH_HOME` only. Disconnecting a channel cannot revive a token from the default home; reconnect it in the active home if needed. Provider `env_key` credentials retain the fallback described above. TPS includes hidden reasoning time and excludes tool execution time. Live text estimates are corrected when Codex reports output token usage. Decode spans of 500ms or less are excluded from TPS samples; token and cost totals still include all reported usage. Native browsing/archive, fork/conversation rewind (the first message requires Codex app-server 0.160.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-remote

[![CI](https://github.com/Char0nChengg/dsh-remote/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Char0nChengg/dsh-remote/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

让 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)（DSH）在 Windows 上直接操作 WSL 发行版或远端 SSH 服务器：执行命令、读取/写入文件、上传下载，并为每个服务器预置 `module`、Conda、Slurm/PBS 等环境提示。

**服务器不需要安装 Agent、桥接程序，也不需要主动连接外网。** 连接始终由 Windows 本机的 `ssh.exe` / `scp.exe` / `wsl.exe` 发起；服务器只需要已有的 SSH 服务（WSL 目标则完全本地）。

## 环境要求

- Windows 上的 DSH Desktop / Web Profile；
- Windows 自带 OpenSSH Client（`ssh.exe`、`scp.exe`），或自行配置 `sshPath` / `scpPath`；
- 可选：WSL 2 和至少一个发行版；
- SSH 目标：Linux + `sshd` + GNU coreutils（`bash`、`stat`、`find`、`head`、`tail`、`timeout`）；
- 认证：SSH key 或 ssh-agent。插件不读取、不保存密码，`BatchMode=yes` 禁止交互式密码提示。

## 安装

### 从 GitHub 安装

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/Char0nChengg/dsh-remote.git D:\dsh-remote
```

然后在 DSH 里让 Agent 安装这个本地 bundle：

```text
plugin_manager install_bundle({ target: "D:\\dsh-remote" })
```

安装后插件会出现在 **设置 → 插件**，名称为 **远程终端与文件 / Remote Shell & Files**。bundle 默认带一个 WSL 目标 `wsl-ubuntu`，没有 WSL 时可以删掉，直接使用 SSH 目标或临时目标。

### npm

包名预留为 `@char0nchengg/dsh-remote`。发布到 npm 后可以用 DSH 的插件安装器直接安装；目前推荐 GitHub 安装。

## 快速使用

不需要记工具名，直接在聊天里说：

```text
列出 gpu 上 ~/project 的文件
读一下 gpu 上 ~/project/run.log 最后 100 行
把 gpu 上的 submit.sh 下载到 D:\results
在 gpu 的 ~/project 下提交 sbatch submit.sh
在 WSL Ubuntu 里看一下 GPU 和当前目录
```

如果服务器已经在 `~/.ssh/config` 里有别名，可以直接用 `ssh:<别名>`，不需要改插件配置：

```sshconfig
Host gpu
  HostName gpu.example.edu
  User alice
  IdentityFile C:\Users\you\.ssh\id_ed25519
  IdentitiesOnly yes
```

```text
remote_targets({ "check": true })
remote_exec({ "target": "ssh:gpu", "command": "nvidia-smi" })
```

`remote_targets` 会列出已配置目标和 `~/.ssh/config` 里的 Host 别名（不会主动连接它们）。

## 配置服务器与环境提示

在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 追加/覆盖 `dsh-remote` 这一行。`config` 会整体替换，所以需要把想保留的 WSL 目标一起写上。完整示例见 [`targets.example.yml`](targets.example.yml)。

```yaml
- id: dsh-remote
  name: '@char0nchengg/dsh-remote'
  config:
    # 可选：所有目标共享的使用习惯
    prompt: |
      不要在登录节点跑重计算；优先用 sbatch 提交。
      读日志优先用 remote_read 的 tail/range，不要整文件 cat。
    targets:
      - id: wsl-ubuntu
        label: WSL Ubuntu
        transport: wsl
        distro: Ubuntu
        defaultCwd: "~"
        environment: |
          Local WSL distro; no sshd required. Use the distro's default user.
      - id: gpu
        label: GPU 登录节点
        transport: ssh
        host: gpu                    # 复用 ~/.ssh/config 的 Host 别名
        defaultCwd: /data/project
        environment: |
          - Slurm 登录节点，批处理分区常用 `fat`，示例脚本 32 核。
          - `module load intel/2022 netcdf/4.7.4`
          - Conda：`conda activate torch`。
          - 项目数据在 `/data/project`，临时目录在 `/scratch/$USER`。
          - 不要在登录节点跑长时间计算；用 `sbatch` 提交后读 `.out` / `.err`。
```

`environment` 也可以写成字符串数组：

```yaml
environment:
  - "module load intel/2022 netcdf/4.7.4"
  - "conda activate torch"
```

### 预加载提示词是怎么工作的

当配置里存在 `prompt` 或任一 `targets[].environment` 时，插件会在 **system prompt** 中注册一段 `dsh-remote:targets` 上下文。模型在每次请求开始前就能看到这些环境说明，不必先调用 `remote_targets`。

- 只注入配置里的文字，**不会自动执行** `module load`、`conda activate` 或任何命令；
- 它只是提示，环境变化后模型仍应用 `remote_exec` 验证；
- 每个目标的 `environment` 最多 4000 字符，整段提示最多 6000 字符；
- `remote_targets` 也会显示同样的环境说明，方便核对；
- 不要把密码、token、私钥内容写进 `environment`，它会进入模型上下文和会话记录。

## 工具

| 工具 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `remote_targets` | 列出已配置目标、SSH config 别名、环境提示，可选连通性检查 |
| `remote_exec` | 在目标上以 `bash -lc` 执行命令，返回退出码、stdout/stderr（有界） |
| `remote_read` | 读取远端文本文件；总是返回大小、mtime、权限、属主；大文件只给预览，支持 `head`/`tail`/`range` 字节窗口 |
| `remote_list` | 列目录，返回类型、大小、mtime、权限、符号链接目标 |
| `remote_write` | 原子写入 UTF-8 文件（临时文件 + rename），可设 `mode=755` 提交脚本 |
| `remote_transfer` | Windows 与目标之间上传/下载；SSH 支持目录递归，WSL 仅文件 |

所有工具都接受临时目标：

- `ssh:gpu`：使用 `~/.ssh/config` 的 `Host gpu`，或直接主机名；
- `ssh://alice@gpu.example.edu:2222`；
- `wsl:Ubuntu`（或 `wsl:` 使用默认发行版）。

大文件/二进制文件不要直接 `cat`：`remote_read` 的 `auto` 模式对超过 2 MiB 的文件只返回元数据和 4 KiB 预览；需要完整数据时用 `remote_transfer` 下载，或 `remote_exec` 调用 `ncdump -h`、`h5dump -H` 等领域工具看参数。

## 配置字段

| 字段 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| `prompt` | 可选，所有目标共享的预加载说明 |
| `targets[].id` | 工具里使用的目标 id，唯一 |
| `targets[].label` | 显示名称 |
| `targets[].transport` | `ssh` 或 `wsl` |
| `targets[].host` | SSH 主机名、IP 或 `~/.ssh/config` 别名 |
| `targets[].user` / `port` | 可选；不填则沿用 ssh config |
| `targets[].identityFile` | 私钥路径，支持 `~` |
| `targets[].proxyJump` | 可选，对应 `ssh -J` |
| `targets[].sshOptions` | 追加的 `-o` 选项数组 |
| `targets[].distro` | WSL 发行版名；省略表示默认发行版 |
| `targets[].defaultCwd` | 远端默认工作目录；`~` 或绝对路径 |
| `targets[].environment` | 该服务器的环境说明，字符串或字符串数组 |
| `strictHostKeyChecking` | `accept-new`（默认）/ `yes` / `no` / `ask` |
| `connectTimeoutSec` | SSH 连接超时，默认 10 秒 |
| `defaultTimeoutMs` | `remote_exec` 默认远端超时，默认 120000 |
| `transferTimeoutMs` | 单次上传/下载超时，默认 1800000（30 分钟） |
| `maxOutputBytes` | `remote_exec` 每路输出上限，默认 262144 |
| `defaultReadBytes` | `remote_read` 默认上限，默认 262144 |
| `largeFileBytes` / `previewBytes` | `auto` 模式的大文件阈值 / 预览字节数 |
| `sshPath` / `scpPath` / `wslPath` | 可选，覆盖本机客户端路径 |

## 安全模型

这是一个**高权限**插件：`remote_exec` 等价于远端 SSH 用户的 shell 权限，`remote_write` / `remote_transfer` 可以修改或覆盖远端文件。

- 只使用专用、最小权限的 SSH key；不要把密码写进配置或环境说明；
- 默认 `StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new`，首次连接记录指纹，之后指纹变化会拒绝；
- `BatchMode=yes` 禁止密码提示，避免密码进入进程参数或日志；
- 服务器只接受 Windows 的入站 SSH，不需要反向连接或外网访问；
- 如果你的 `~/.ssh/config` 开了 `ForwardAgent yes`，认证 agent 会被转发到服务器；不需要时在目标里加 `sshOptions: ["ForwardAgent=no"]`；
- `prompt` / `environment` 会进入模型上下文，不要放密钥、token 或隐私数据。

## 限制

- 只面向 Linux 远端（依赖 GNU `stat --printf`、`find -printf`、`head -c`/`tail -c`、`timeout`）。macOS/BSD 和 Windows OpenSSH 服务器未适配。
- SSH 文件传输使用本机 `scp` 的 SFTP 模式；服务器需要启用 SFTP 子系统（OpenSSH 默认启用）。
- WSL 的目录上传/下载未实现；需要时在 WSL 内用 `tar`，或通过 `remote_exec` 操作。
- `remote_write` 单次内容上限 8 MiB；更大的文件或二进制文件用 `remote_transfer`，脚本请使用 LF 换行。
- 不提供持久 shell、端口转发、反向隧道或远程 DSH Agent；长任务用 Slurm/PBS 或 `nohup`。
- 服务器必须能被 Windows 主动访问（VPN 或端口映射）。

## 发布到插件市场

仓库结构满足 [dsh.so](https://www.dsh.so/zh/submit/) 和 [DSH-Store](https://github.com/AI-Scarlett/DSH-Store) 的静态上架要求：

- 标准 DSH Bundle，`package.json` 声明 `dsh.bundle.patch`；
- 唯一入口 id `dsh-remote`，不覆盖任何 `@deepseek-ai/*` 官方组件；
- MIT 许可证、README、图标、en/zh locale；
- 没有 `preinstall` / `install` / `postinstall` / `prepare` 生命周期脚本；
- 无运行依赖、无原生构建；
- `dsh.compatibility.dshReleases` 精确声明已在 `0.2.1-rc.3` 上验证。

提交入口：

- dsh.so：<https://www.dsh.so/zh/submit/>
- DSH-Store：<https://github.com/AI-Scarlett/DSH-Store/issues/new?template=plugin-submission.yml>

插件会执行任意远端 Shell，属于高权限工具；提交时应在权限说明中明确文件、网络、命令访问范围。

## 开发与测试

```bash
npm test
npm run check
```

测试只覆盖本地纯函数和配置解析，不连接网络、不写真实 Profile：

- shell 引号转义；
- ad-hoc `ssh:` / `wsl:` 目标解析；
- `environment` / `prompt` 归一化与长度限制；
- 预加载提示词内容。

端到端验证记录：

- WSL Ubuntu：连通性检查、命令执行/非零退出/超时、含引号和 `$` 的路径写入与读取、目录列表、大文件预览、二进制识别、文件上传下载；
- 临时 WSL sshd：公钥认证、首次主机指纹、命令、文件读写、带空格路径、文件与目录 scp 传输，验证后已停止并移除；
- 未连接任何第三方真实服务器。

## License

MIT © 2026 Char0nChengg

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-annotate-sync

> Open an HTML preview in DeepSeek Harness and the annotation overlay is already there.
> Pick elements, write notes, hand the batch to the agent, and the agent edits the
> source file by path. No server, no `<script>` tag, no target picker.

![icon](./icon.svg)

## What it is

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that takes over `.html` / `.htm` document previews:

- open any HTML file in the right-sidebar **Files** panel (including one the agent just
  generated) and the **点选批注 / Mark** overlay appears automatically;
- hover highlight, click an element, write a note; numbered pins follow scrolling,
  resizing and layout changes;
- annotations are saved **per file**, with selector, sampled text, computed styles and
  the change instruction;
- leave picking with `Esc`, or press **Send to Agent**, and the batch goes into the
  current conversation as one structured message;
- the agent calls `read_annotations`, receives **file path + selector + note**, and edits
  that HTML/CSS directly;
- after the file changes the preview rebuilds; annotations stay; the agent can call
  `set_annotation_status` when done.

The old Agentation demo experience is preserved, without manually adding
`agentation.js`, without the 8765 sync server, and without a local-service list to pick.

## Install

```bash
# bundled CLI (macOS Desktop)
"/Applications/DeepSeek Harness.app/Contents/Resources/runtime/cli/bin/dsh" \
  plugin --profile desktop add dsh-annotate-sync@2.0.0
```

Add `"dsh-annotate-sync"` to `dsh.profile.bundles` in
`~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json`, then **fully quit and restart DeepSeek Harness**.

Local development / tarball:

```bash
npm pack
dsh plugin --profile desktop add /absolute/path/to/dsh-annotate-sync-2.0.0.tgz
```

## Use

1. Restart DSH.
2. Open any `.html` file from the right-sidebar **Files** panel — or open the bundled
   [`demo/index.html`](./demo/index.html) to try it.
3. The floating **点选批注 / Mark** button appears in the preview; click it and then
   click an element.
4. Write the note and press `Enter`; `Esc` leaves picking.
5. **Auto-send** is on by default: leaving picking sends the batch into the current
   conversation. You can also press **Send to Agent** at any time, or turn auto-send off.
6. The agent reads the annotations and edits the source file; the preview refreshes when
   the file changes.
7. If the agent does not mark them, say "apply my annotations" so it calls
   `read_annotations`.

The toolbar above the preview shows the file name, pending count, send, auto-send and
clear.

## Annotation data

```jsonc
{
  "id": "uuid",
  "page": {
    "url": "dsh-resource://file/session/<sessionId>/<encoded path>",
    "origin": "",
    "path": "demo/index.html",
    "title": "index.html"
  },
  "file": { "sessionId": "...", "path": "demo/index.html", "name": "index.html", "address": "dsh-resource://..." },
  "selector": "#hero-title",
  "tag": "h1",
  "className": "hero-title",
  "textSample": "Simple pricing",
  "styles": { "fontSize": "26px", "color": "rgb(15,23,42)", "backgroundColor": "rgba(0,0,0,0)" },
  "rect": { "x": 120, "y": 340, "w": 420, "h": 32 },
  "note": "Make the title shorter",
  "status": "pending",
  "order": 0,
  "createdAt": "ISO",
  "updatedAt": "ISO"
}
```

Store: `~/.dsh/annotate-sync/annotations.json` plus readable `annotations.md`.
Legacy v0/v1/v2 files migrate to v3 automatically; old HTTP-page annotations remain
readable.

## Model tools

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `read_annotations({ status?, pageUrl?, includeDone? })` | Read annotations; pending by default; Markdown includes `文件：<path>` per file |
| `set_annotation_status({ ids?, status, all?, pageUrl? })` | Mark applied (or back to pending) after editing |
| `clear_annotations({ pageUrl? })` | Clear all, optionally per file |

## Configuration

`config` in `cordis.patch.yml`:

| Field | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `dir` | `~/.dsh/annotate-sync` | annotation storage directory |
| `route` | `/__dsh-annotate-sync` | internal API/overlay prefix |
| `legacyRoute` | `/api/annotate-sync/annotations` | old sync bridge; empty disables |
| `maxBodyBytes` | `262144` | request body cap |
| `tool` | `true` | register the model tools |

## Architecture

```
DSH Web
└─ Client: custom HTML document-preview renderer (priority: external)
   ├─ reuses the builtin bytes-complete renderer + relative CSS/JS packing + opaque blob iframe
   ├─ injects window.__DSH_ANNOTATE__ + overlay.js
   ├─ toolbar: send / auto-send / clear
   └─ postMessage bridge: overlay ↔ document component
Host: routes + v3 annotation store + three model tools
Overlay: picking, pins, comment cards, status
```

- The iframe stays `sandbox="allow-scripts"` with an opaque origin; the overlay and the
  document component only exchange `postMessage`; the parent validates `event.source`
  plus the channel.
- Relative CSS/JS are read through DSH's workspaceFiles and packed into the blob, same as
  the builtin preview.
- No extra HTTP server is started and no network requests are injected into the page.

## Known limitations

- A page CSP that blocks external scripts also blocks the overlay; the preview itself
  still renders.
- The custom renderer always allows the page's own scripts (the overlay needs them); it
  is not gated by the builtin interactive-preview setting.
- Elements inside cross-origin iframes or closed shadow roots cannot be picked.
- Only `.html` / `.htm` are taken over; other document types keep the builtin preview.
- Pins rely on CSS selectors and geometry; large DOM changes can misplace a pin, while
  the note and file path remain.

## Upgrading from 1.x

v2 removes the local-service preview and the right-sidebar annotation panel. The old
`annotations.json` migrates; the legacy `/api/annotate-sync/annotations` bridge stays.
`sync-server.mjs` is no longer needed.

## Development

```bash
npm test          # node --test
npm run check     # node --check all runtime files
npm run pack:check
```

Protocol: [docs/PROTOCOL.md](./docs/PROTOCOL.md) · Publishing: [docs/PUBLISH.md](./docs/PUBLISH.md)

## License

MIT. The HTML renderer is adapted from DeepSeek Harness (MIT); see [NOTICE](./NOTICE).
