# dsh-better-git-worktree

Git worktree **sessions** for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): a session can live in its own self-contained git working copy permanently, instead of the harness's review/acceptance lifecycle.

It borrows the UX of [`dsh-git-worktree`](https://github.com/wloops/dsh-git-worktree) (the composer switch, the session-list status indicator, the session-header menu) and drops everything else: there is no review checkpoint, no preview/apply, no delivery handoff. A working copy here is simply where the session works.

**Usage guide:** [`docs/USAGE.md`](docs/USAGE.md): surfaces, statuses, workflows, and a screenshot gallery.

![Session list statuses](docs/screenshots/02-session-list-statuses.png)

> The screenshots were taken on dsh 0.1.5 with the earlier, inlined version of this plugin. The session-row badge is now an icon in the row's leading cell instead of a text pill, so they are out of date until they are retaken on a 0.2.0 UI.

## What it does

- **Composer switch (blank sessions).** A `Worktree` toggle sits in the composer tool row. Turning it on opens one confirmation dialog; confirming creates the branch and working copy immediately and continues **that** session inside it. The toggle then reads ON and disabled.
- **`worktree_convert` tool.** Takes a session running in a checkout, creates a working copy, moves its uncommitted work into it (kept recoverable as a `git stash` entry), and continues the conversation in a session rooted there. The continuation carries the conversation **through the last completed turn**; see *Known limits* for what that means when the tool is called in a session's first turn. Once a session is in a working copy the tool is denied for that agent's scope, so it leaves the tool list.
- **Session-list status badge**, on the session row: **blue** Progressing, **green** Up To Date / In Sync, **amber** Behind, **grey** Unknown/Missing, plus a **yellow glow** when the branch needs rebasing. The row's hover card spells out the full status.
- **Header pill and menu, for every session.** The pill reads `<name> - <status>` (`brave-otter - Progressing`, `main - In Sync`). Its menu offers *Git Changes*, *Review branch vs `<default>`*, *git fetch*, *Copy worktree path* / *Open worktree folder* for working-copy sessions, and *Move this session into a worktree* for the rest.
- **Session "..." menu**: *Copy worktree path* and *Open worktree folder* on a session that has a working copy.
- **Archiving a worktree session asks about the working copy.** The official *Archive* actions (the row's hover button and the "..." menu row) are shadowed: a session with a working copy opens one dialog (*Remove*, *Keep*, *Cancel*) that names the path and branch and warns about uncommitted paths and unpushed commits. *Remove* also retires the dead workspace registration. Every other session archives exactly as before.
- **Background git with a cache.** TTL cache (single-flight, stale-while-revalidate), a 15 s background refresher, and a 90 s-throttled `git fetch` of the source checkout that never blocks a read (a copy's own refs update when the copy fetches; see Working copies).

The official Workspace UI stays in charge of the sidebar; this plugin only adds to it through the seats that UI declares (see [How it plugs in](#how-it-plugs-in)). It does not replace or disable any core row.

## Install

Installed from a git tag of this repository; it is not published to npm. Replace `<version>` with a released version (tags are named `dsh-better-git-worktree-v<version>`; see [the tag list](https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins/tags)):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-better-git-worktree-v<version>&path:/packages/better-git-worktree"
```

That installs the package into the profile and enables its bundle. If you manage the profile's `package.json` yourself, the pnpm equivalent is below, then also add `dsh-better-git-worktree` to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`:

```sh
pnpm add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-better-git-worktree-v<version>&path:/packages/better-git-worktree"
```

> **Warning:** never install it by bare name. Unscoped `dsh-*` names on the npm registry can belong to unrelated authors.

Restart dsh. If you ran an earlier, in-tree version of this plugin, also **remove its old `ui-workspace` row** (the one whose `disabled` expression tests `betterGitWorktreeWorkspaceProvider`) and its old `better-git-worktree` row pointing at an `entry-rN.mjs`: the official Workspace UI must stay active, and this plugin no longer elects itself in its place. A fresh install needs no other row.

## Configuration

Nothing is required.

| Key | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stateDir` | `<dsh home>/plugins/dsh-better-git-worktree` | Directory holding the session-to-working-copy registry (`worktrees.json`). Unset, it is where earlier releases kept it, so an existing registry is found with no configuration. A relative value resolves against the dsh home (`$DSH_HOME`, else `~/.dsh`), never the working directory; `~` is expanded. A blank or non-string value falls back to the default with a warning. |

A misspelled key is warned about once at boot and ignored. A bundle patch layer replaces a row's whole `config`, so if you set `stateDir` on your row, restate any other key you rely on.

## Working copies

A worktree session gets its own **self-contained working copy**, nested inside the checkout it was branched from:

```
<repo>/.dsh-worktrees/<pet-name>/
```

It owns its git database (`git init` in place) and reads the checkout's objects through `.git/objects/info/alternates`, so nothing is downloaded, no object is duplicated, and no file is copied by a clone. The working tree is materialised from the session's starting commit, on a branch `dsh/<pet-name>`. A checkout that cannot be written to hosts its copies under `~/.dsh-worktrees/<pet-name>` instead.

That layout is what makes the sandbox sufficient. `dsh-sandbox` grants a session exactly one writable root, its own cwd, and a *linked* worktree keeps its index and refs in the source repository, one directory outside it, so `git add`, `commit`, `push` and anything that shells out to git would stop for an escalation. Here every write git makes (index, refs, new objects) lands inside the copy, so plain `workspace-write` is enough.

Two trade-offs, deliberately accepted:

- It is not a linked worktree: the checkout's `git worktree list` does not show it, and its branch lives in the copy until it is pushed (pushes go to the same `origin` the checkout uses).
- It borrows the checkout's object store, so deleting that checkout loses history the copy has not republished.
- A new copy has only its own branch: `origin`'s refs (and so the comparison with the default branch, the *In Sync* state and the rebase glow) arrive with the copy's first `git fetch`, from the header menu or the agent.

The checkout's own `git status` stays clean because creating a copy writes `.dsh-worktrees/` into `<repo>/.git/info/exclude`: local to the clone, no tracked file touched. If that entry is ever missing, the header menu offers to write it again.

## Status semantics

| Badge | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| blue `Progressing` | work is not published yet: no upstream, or commits ahead of it |
| amber `Behind` | the upstream moved on and the branch has nothing of its own |
| green `Up To Date` | exactly in step with its upstream, but not identical to `origin/<default>` |
| green `In Sync` | in step with its upstream **and** identical to `origin/<default>` |
| grey `Missing` | the recorded working-copy directory is gone |

A **yellow glow** is a separate overlay: the branch has its own commits and `origin/<default>` has moved on, so it needs rebasing. Working-tree detail (staged / modified / untracked) is in the hover text, not the colour.

## The registry

`$DSH_HOME/plugins/dsh-better-git-worktree/worktrees.json` is the only record of which session works in which copy. Its format (`"version": 1`) is the one every release of this plugin has written, and it is read unchanged. It is written atomically (temp file in the same directory, then rename), it is never written before it has been read, and records or fields this release does not understand are written back as they were. If the file exists but cannot be read, parsed, or has another version, the plugin says so at boot, **leaves the file alone**, runs with an empty in-memory registry, and refuses to create new copies (it could not record them).

## How it plugs in

Verified against `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace` 0.2.0-rc.2 (`lib/types/client/contract/slots.d.ts`, `lib/client.js`):

| Seat | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| `sidebar.session.row.leading` | the status badge (rendered only by an idle row; a busy or pending row shows its own state dot instead) |
| `sidebar.session.row.hover` | the status text on the row's hover card |
| `sidebar.workspaces.session.menu.item` | *Copy worktree path*, *Open worktree folder*; and a same-id `archive` entry at priority -1 that shadows the official one |
| `sidebar.workspaces.session.row.action` | the same shadow for the hover archive button |
| `shell.overlay` | the archive dialog |
| `conversation.input.left` | the composer switch |
| `conversation.session.header.actions` | the header pill and menu |

A shadow reuses the official component and locale and the official inject result unchanged except for the `archiveSession` callback, which is wrapped so the dialog can run first. If the shadow ever crashes the renderer retires it and the official entry shows again.

`dsh-better-sidebar` is an optional integration: with it the header menu's *Review branch* opens a right-sidebar tab (and *Git Changes* opens its git lens); without it the review opens in a modal and *Git Changes* does the same.

## Known limits

- The keyboard shortcut for *Archive session* calls the official archive directly and is not intercepted: it archives without the dialog and leaves the working copy on disk (the *Keep* outcome).
- The status badge is drawn only in a row's leading seat, which the official UI renders only for an idle row. There is none on a busy row, a row with a pending interaction, a completed-unread row (its dot), a row with running subagents, an archived row or a blank session, and none in search results. The hover card still shows the status text where the row's hover seat is mounted.
- A working-copy session is a workspace of its own in the sidebar (named after the copy) and is listed in the new-session workspace dropdown; the official UI offers no seat to regroup it under the project it was branched from. The sidebar's "Group by: Workspace Tree" view option nests a copy under a registered repository workspace by path, but that is a per-browser setting the plugin cannot set.
- *Remove* in the archive dialog archives the session first and deletes the copy only if that succeeded, so it does nothing while the session is running (the harness refuses to archive running work): stop the session, then archive it again. The dialog's warnings count uncommitted paths, unpublished commits (on HEAD, any branch or any tag, minus anything on a remote-tracking ref, in the source repository or at the commit the copy started from, so a fresh copy's local commits count before it has ever fetched) and stash entries. If any of that could not be read (git failed or timed out, or the source repository moved), the dialog says it could not verify the copy and **Remove is disabled**; Keep still works. Remove is also unavailable while another session still works in the copy (the source row of a conversion).
- The host re-checks before deleting: the `remove` endpoint forces a fresh read and refuses a copy that cannot be verified (including one that is not a repository of its own, whose `git` would otherwise resolve to the source checkout), and refuses one with uncommitted paths, unpushed commits or stash entries unless the request confirms exactly the plan the host just computed. Ignored files and folders (`.env`, `node_modules/`) are summarized in the dialog but never block it.
- Not counted: unpushed work inside a nested repository or submodule of the copy (it appears only as an untracked or modified path of the copy), and work in other worktrees of the copy.
- A copy created from a source on a detached HEAD, from a registry record written before `baseOid` was stored, may show that starting commit as one unpushed commit (a conservative false warning).
- A running session cannot change its checkout (`session.header.cwd` is immutable), so *convert* creates a session in the working copy and continues the conversation there. The new session is seeded with the source's events through its **last completed turn**. The turn that makes the call (the `worktree_convert` tool call, or the turn in progress when the header menu is used) has not ended yet, so it is not carried: when the source has no completed turn, which is the case when the agent calls the tool in a session's first turn, the new session starts **blank** (the tool reports "A new session (...) was created in the worktree; open it to continue there", with `conversationCarried: false`) and the source session is **not archived** (it is archived only when the conversation was carried). The harness's own session fork has the same rule (it answers `session/fork-unavailable: ... has no completed turn to fork from`). The in-tree plugin this was extracted from behaved identically.
- `Open worktree folder` needs a desktop opener on the host (`xdg-open`, `gio`, ... `open` on macOS, `explorer` on Windows); without one the menu says so.

## Session format

This plugin writes no messages of its own into sessions. A continuation session is seeded with the source session's events through its last completed turn (format V4 events, unchanged).

## Checks

```sh
node --test packages/better-git-worktree/test/*.test.mjs
node scripts/verify.mjs --package dsh-better-git-worktree
```

The tests use real temporary git repositories for creation, change-move, status folding and review, and mount the real host on a mock context.

## Compatibility

Requires dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 or later (`engines.dsh` and the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` peer: `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0 || >=0.3.0-0`).

## License

MIT. See [`NOTICE`](NOTICE) for attribution.

# dsh-plugins

Public [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugins by [Chris Johnson](https://github.com/chrisjohnson). One repository, independently installable plugins — each with its own README, its own tests, its own changelog and its own version.

## Install

**Nothing here is published to npm.** Every release is a git tag on this repository, named `<package>-v<version>` (for example `dsh-model-switch-v0.2.1`), and you install a plugin by pinning that tag plus the package's subdirectory:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#<package>-v<version>&path:/packages/<dir>"
```

`dsh plugin add` hands that spec to pnpm and also lists the package under the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`, which is what activates its configuration layer. If you manage a profile's `package.json` yourself, the same spec works with pnpm directly — but then add the package name to `dsh.profile.bundles` by hand, because a plain `pnpm add` installs the plugin without enabling it:

```sh
pnpm add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#<package>-v<version>&path:/packages/<dir>"
```

Pick the tag from [the repository's tags](https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins/tags); `<dir>` is the folder under `packages/` in the index below.

> **Warning — do not install these by bare name.** `pnpm add dsh-model-switch` (or `dsh plugin add dsh-model-switch`) resolves against the npm registry, and the npm package called `dsh-model-switch` belongs to an unrelated author: it is **not** this plugin. The same can happen to any unscoped `dsh-*` name. Always use the git-tag spec above.

## Index

| Plugin | What it is for | Latest | Directory |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **[dsh-model-switch](./packages/model-switch/)** | Let the agent switch its own model mid-session, with a context-window fit guard so neither it nor a human in the composer can strand a conversation on a model too small to read it. | 0.2.1 | `packages/model-switch` |
| **[dsh-image-search-searxng](./packages/image-search-searxng/)** | A model-facing `image_search` tool over your own SearXNG, rendered inline in the Web GUI. | 0.2.0 | `packages/image-search-searxng` |
| **[dsh-continue-kicker](./packages/continue-kicker/)** | Automatically send "continue" when a turn halts on the output-token limit (or after a crash, or on a reasoning-only empty stop), with a runaway guard that stops after repeated kicks with no progress. | 0.2.0 | `packages/continue-kicker` |
| **[dsh-loop-watchdog](./packages/loop-watchdog/)** | Detect an agent stuck in a loop before each step (a deterministic repetition check plus an optional model judge), keep an audit ledger of every check, optionally steer the session, and chart the ledger in a `dsh-better-sidebar` panel. | 0.1.0 | `packages/loop-watchdog` |
| **[dsh-scheduled-queue](./packages/scheduled-queue/)** | Schedule the composer's draft to be sent to its own session later, with a per-session dock to edit, cancel or send now. Runs alongside the official schedule bundle. | 0.1.0 | `packages/scheduled-queue` |
| **[dsh-kanban](./packages/kanban/)** | Ticket-centric work organizer and code-driven workflow engine: a local SQLite board whose phases spawn sandboxed role sessions, gate on per-provider capacity, verify machine-readable conditions, and record a complete time/token ledger. | 0.1.0 | `packages/kanban` |
| **[dsh-model-capacity](./packages/model-capacity/)** | Process-wide, per-provider model-call capacity: interactive calls queue FIFO, subagent dispatch gets an immediate capacity error with free-route suggestions, and a panel inspects active leases, waiters and reservations. | 0.1.0 | `packages/model-capacity` |
| **[dsh-better-git-worktree](./packages/better-git-worktree/)** | Run a session in its own self-contained git working copy: a composer Worktree switch, a `worktree_convert` tool, session-list status badges, a header menu, and an archive prompt that decides the working copy's fate. | 0.1.1 | `packages/better-git-worktree` |
| **[dsh-session-cost](./packages/session-cost/)** | A compact estimated-cost badge in the composer stats bar: reads the session billed-token buckets and prices them with public models.dev rates, hidden at $0. | 0.1.0 | `packages/session-cost` |
| **[dsh-math-literal](./packages/math-literal/)** | Keeps single-`$` dollars literal in web chat: unpaired `$` in settled markdown renders as a literal dollar sign (matching the streaming arm) instead of opening an inline-math pair, while real math and code regions are untouched. | 0.1.0 | `packages/math-literal` |
| **[dsh-browser](./packages/browser/)** | One browser context per DSH session on a single shared remote Browserless connection for `dsh-playwright-browser`'s tools, with reconnect after a dropped connection, context cleanup when a session ends, and an announced local fallback. | 0.1.0 | `packages/browser` |

Install lines for the latest release of each package:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-model-switch-v0.2.1&path:/packages/model-switch"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-image-search-searxng-v0.2.0&path:/packages/image-search-searxng"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-continue-kicker-v0.2.0&path:/packages/continue-kicker"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-loop-watchdog-v0.1.0&path:/packages/loop-watchdog"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-scheduled-queue-v0.1.0&path:/packages/scheduled-queue"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-kanban-v0.1.0&path:/packages/kanban"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-model-capacity-v0.1.0&path:/packages/model-capacity"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-better-git-worktree-v0.1.1&path:/packages/better-git-worktree"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-session-cost-v0.1.0&path:/packages/session-cost"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-math-literal-v0.1.0&path:/packages/math-literal"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-browser-v0.1.0&path:/packages/browser"
```

Each package's README is the contract: what it does, every configuration key and what happens when it is unset, how it fails, how to install it, and how to run its checks. Nothing important lives only here.

## Releases

1. A release is a normal pull request that bumps one package's version and moves its CHANGELOG `Unreleased` entry under that version.
2. After it merges, the tag `<package>-v<version>` is cut on that merge commit and pushed. Nothing is committed directly to `main`.
3. Consumers pin the tag with the install spec above. A tag is never moved or rewritten once pushed.

# dsh-browser

**One browser context per DSH session, on one shared remote Browserless connection, for `dsh-playwright-browser`'s tools.**

A host-plane plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). It registers no tools and replaces no prompt. [`dsh-playwright-browser`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-playwright-browser) keeps its ten `browser_*` tools, their schemas, snapshots and prompt exactly as they are; this plugin only changes where their browser comes from.

Without it, every `browser_*` call from every session goes to one local Chromium and one browser context built when the original plugin starts: sessions see and click each other's tabs, and once that browser dies nothing recovers it. With it:

- **One context per session.** A session's tabs, cookies and logins are invisible to every other session. The context is created on the session's first `browser_*` call and closed when the session ends (`agent/disposed`, and `session/disposed`).
- **One connection to Browserless for all of them.** Contexts on a connection cost no extra Browserless slot, so five sessions use one of its concurrent slots, not five. When the last session ends the connection is closed, so an idle DSH holds no slot.
- **Survives a dropped connection.** Browserless kills even active connections at its per-connection timeout (one hour by default). The plugin drops the dead browser and every context on it, and the next call transparently reconnects and opens a fresh context. The result tells the model so, because its old tabs are gone.
- **Says so when it is not remote.** If Browserless cannot be reached, sessions get a local Chromium instead, and every tool result for them carries a line saying the browser is a local fallback and why. It never pretends to be remote.

## How it works

The original plugin builds one `BrowserController` and every tool closes over it; controller methods are never told which session called. So this plugin:

1. wraps each `browser_*` call (the `tools/execute` event) in an `AsyncLocalStorage` store holding the calling agent's id (`exec.agent.id`, the session id);
2. patches the twelve public methods of `BrowserController.prototype` (`open`, `navigate`, `snapshot`, `click`, `fill`, `press`, `history`, `wait`, `screenshot`, `listTabs`, `selectTab`, `closeTab`) so that, when a session id is in the store, the call runs the **original method** on that session's own controller. That controller is a subclass of the original `BrowserController` whose only change is that its browser context comes from the shared connection instead of a private launch. Tab bookkeeping, locators, snapshots and cancellation are the original code, untouched;
3. with no session in the store, falls straight through to the original method, so anything else using the controller behaves as before.

Notices for the model travel on the call's own result via `tools/post-execute`.

### Module identity

The patch only works if the `BrowserController` it patches is the same module instance the original plugin's tools use. Both import `dsh-playwright-browser`'s one `lib/browser-controller.js` (this plugin through the package's `./controller` export), and Node's module cache is keyed by that file's URL, so they share it as long as there is **one installed copy** of `dsh-playwright-browser` that both resolve to. Install them side by side in the same `node_modules`, as a flat (hoisted) tree does.

If they ever do not share it (a second copy of `dsh-playwright-browser`, or a hot reload that replaced only one of them), the patch would silently do nothing. The plugin checks for this: a `browser_*` call that succeeds without reaching a patched method is logged as an error and its result says that session isolation and the remote browser are **not** in effect. [`scripts/browser-live-check.mjs`](../../scripts/browser-live-check.mjs) verifies the sharing against a real dsh process.

## Install

Installed from a git tag of this repository — it is not published to npm. Replace `<version>` with a released version (tags are named `dsh-browser-v<version>`; see [the tag list](https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins/tags)):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-browser-v<version>&path:/packages/browser"
```

That installs the package into the profile and enables its bundle. If you manage the profile's `package.json` yourself, the pnpm equivalent is below — then also add `dsh-browser` to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`, because `pnpm add` alone installs the plugin without enabling it:

```sh
pnpm add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-browser-v<version>&path:/packages/browser"
```

> **Warning:** never `pnpm add dsh-browser` (or `dsh plugin add dsh-browser`) by bare name. That resolves from the npm registry, where an unscoped `dsh-*` name may belong to an unrelated author and is **not** this plugin.

It needs, in the same installation:

- `dsh-playwright-browser` **exactly `0.1.3`** (enabled in the same profile). The patch targets that version's controller internals; the peer range is pinned so a different version is reported at install time instead of misbehaving.
- `playwright-core` (any release from 1.49; `dsh-playwright-browser` already brings one).

With either missing, the plugin logs one error at boot and does nothing; it never stops the profile from starting.

## Configuration

Set these on the plugin's row in your own profile patch (`config:` block). **A top-level row with a `config:` block replaces the whole config object**, so list every key you want to differ from the default in the same row. The bundle's own layer carries no config for the same reason.

| Key | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `connectUrl` | `ws://127.0.0.1:3100/chromium/playwright` | Playwright websocket endpoint of the Browserless to connect to (`chromium.connect`). Include a `?token=` query if your Browserless needs one; it is never logged or shown to the model. Set to an empty string (`''`) to switch remote off and always use a local browser. A value that is not `ws://` or `wss://` is ignored with a warning. |
| `connectTimeoutMs` | `10000` | How long one connection attempt may take before it counts as unreachable. |
| `retryRemoteAfterMs` | `30000` | After a failed connection, how long new sessions go straight to the local fallback without trying Browserless again. `0` tries on every new session. |
| `fallbackExecutablePath` | unset | Chromium/Chrome executable for the local fallback (and for `connectUrl: ''`). Unset uses the Chromium Playwright manages itself. |
| `viewportWidth`, `viewportHeight` | from `dsh-playwright-browser`'s row | Viewport of each session's context. |
| `actionTimeoutMs`, `navigationTimeoutMs` | from `dsh-playwright-browser`'s row | Per-action and navigation timeouts. |
| `maxSnapshotChars`, `screenshotDir` | from `dsh-playwright-browser`'s row | Snapshot size cap and screenshot directory. |
| `logToStderr` | `false` | Write this plugin's own log lines to stderr (dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 installs no logger exporter, so without it they reach nobody). |

The page and timeout keys exist only to override: when unset, each session's controller is built from the configuration `dsh-playwright-browser` itself resolved (its `playwright-browser` row), so you do not state viewport and timeouts twice. The original's `executablePath`, `channel`, `browser`, `headless` and `userDataDir` have no effect on session browsers: they belong to a local launch, which this plugin only does as a fallback (use `fallbackExecutablePath`).

Resolution lives in [`src/config.mjs`](./src/config.mjs) and is [tested](./test/config.test.mjs). An unknown key or an unusable value prints one warning at boot and falls back to the default. The default `connectUrl` is a loopback address, the usual place a Browserless published on the same host is reachable; every other deployment-specific value is configuration.

Example row:

```yaml
- id: browser
  name: dsh-browser
  config:
    connectUrl: ws://127.0.0.1:3100/chromium/playwright
    connectTimeoutMs: 10000
    retryRemoteAfterMs: 30000
    fallbackExecutablePath: /usr/bin/chromium
    logToStderr: true
```

## Behaviour to know about

- **Tab ids restart after a lost connection** (new context), but keep counting upward, so an id from before the loss is rejected as unknown instead of silently naming a different page.
- **A call in flight when the connection dies fails** with Playwright's own error; the next call recovers.
- **Sessions that fell back to the local browser stay there** until they end, even if Browserless comes back; new sessions try Browserless again after `retryRemoteAfterMs`.
- **Subagents are sessions too**, and each gets its own context.
- **Screenshots are written by DSH, on the DSH host**, as before, into `screenshotDir`.
- **Browserless limits still apply**: its concurrent-connection cap counts connections, and this plugin uses one. Its own memory and CPU limits count open pages across all contexts.
- **The original prompt still tells the model, on a startup failure, to explain `npx playwright install chromium`.** That text is inside `dsh-playwright-browser`'s own prompt section and cannot be edited without replacing it. This plugin adds a short section after it saying not to install browsers here and to report the diagnostic instead.

## Logging

Lines go through the host logger under the name `browser`, and to stderr with `logToStderr: true`:

```
2026-10-28T18:22:00.641Z INFO browser opened remote context for session sess-a (contexts=1)
2026-10-28T18:22:01.186Z WARN browser context for session sess-a was closed by the browser (connection lost); the next call opens a new one
2026-10-28T18:22:03.020Z WARN browser remote browser unavailable, falling back to a local browser: browserType.connect: WebSocket error: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:1
```

## Development

```sh
node --test packages/browser/test/*.test.mjs       # unit tests, no install needed
node scripts/verify.mjs --package dsh-browser      # release contract
node scripts/compose-smoke.mjs browser             # real dsh composition
node scripts/browser-live-check.mjs --install-dir <dsh install> --browserless http://127.0.0.1:3100
```

`src/config.mjs`, `src/pool.mjs`, `src/routing.mjs` and `src/bridge.mjs` import nothing from dsh or Playwright; `src/host.mjs` is the thin wiring. `test/real-controller.test.mjs` runs the routing against the real controller class and is skipped when `dsh-playwright-browser` is not resolvable.

### The live check

`scripts/browser-live-check.mjs` (repository root) boots a throwaway dsh (own `DSH_HOME` and `HOME`, inside the install directory you give it) with both plugins and a test-only driver plugin (`scripts/live/browser-driver.mjs`, not shipped) that creates real agents and runs tool calls through the real tool runtime, with no model involved. Against a reachable Browserless it asserts: the patched and original controller are one file; two sessions calling the original `browser_open`/`browser_tabs` see only their own tabs while Browserless `/pressure` rises by exactly one; killing that connection server-side (`/kill/<id>`, only a session that appeared during the run) is survived and announced; disposing sessions closes their contexts and finally frees the slot; and an unreachable `connectUrl` yields a working local browser with the fallback notice. The install directory needs `@deepseek-ai/dsh`, `dsh-playwright-browser@0.1.3` and this package (a `file:` dependency copies it the way a git install does) in a hoisted `node_modules`, and Chrome for the fallback step (`--fallback-chrome`, or Playwright's own Chromium). Run it only against a Browserless you may load: it opens one connection and two contexts.

# dsh-plugins

Public [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugins by [Chris Johnson](https://github.com/chrisjohnson). One repository, independently installable plugins — each with its own README, its own tests, its own changelog and its own version.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#<package>-v<version>&path:/packages/<dir>"
```

```sh
pnpm add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#<package>-v<version>&path:/packages/<dir>"
```

Pick the tag from [the repository's tags](https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins/tags); `<dir>` is the folder under `packages/` in the index below.

> **Warning — do not install these by bare name.** `pnpm add dsh-model-switch` (or `dsh plugin add dsh-model-switch`) resolves against the npm registry, and the npm package called `dsh-model-switch` belongs to an unrelated author: it is **not** this plugin. The same can happen to any unscoped `dsh-*` name. Always use the git-tag spec above.

## Index

| Plugin | What it is for | Latest | Directory |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **[dsh-model-switch](./packages/model-switch/)** | Let the agent switch its own model mid-session, with a context-window fit guard so neither it nor a human in the composer can strand a conversation on a model too small to read it. | 0.2.1 | `packages/model-switch` |
| **[dsh-image-search-searxng](./packages/image-search-searxng/)** | A model-facing `image_search` tool over your own SearXNG, rendered inline in the Web GUI. | 0.2.0 | `packages/image-search-searxng` |
| **[dsh-continue-kicker](./packages/continue-kicker/)** | Automatically send "continue" when a turn halts on the output-token limit (or after a crash, or on a reasoning-only empty stop), with a runaway guard that stops after repeated kicks with no progress. | 0.2.0 | `packages/continue-kicker` |
| **[dsh-loop-watchdog](./packages/loop-watchdog/)** | Detect an agent stuck in a loop before each step (a deterministic repetition check plus an optional model judge), keep an audit ledger of every check, optionally steer the session, and chart the ledger in a `dsh-better-sidebar` panel. | 0.1.0 | `packages/loop-watchdog` |
| **[dsh-scheduled-queue](./packages/scheduled-queue/)** | Schedule the composer's draft to be sent to its own session later, with a per-session dock to edit, cancel or send now. Runs alongside the official schedule bundle. | 0.1.0 | `packages/scheduled-queue` |
| **[dsh-kanban](./packages/kanban/)** | Ticket-centric work organizer and code-driven workflow engine: a local SQLite board whose phases spawn sandboxed role sessions, gate on per-provider capacity, verify machine-readable conditions, and record a complete time/token ledger. | 0.1.0 | `packages/kanban` |
| **[dsh-model-capacity](./packages/model-capacity/)** | Process-wide, per-provider model-call capacity: interactive calls queue FIFO, subagent dispatch gets an immediate capacity error with free-route suggestions, and a panel inspects active leases, waiters and reservations. | 0.1.0 | `packages/model-capacity` |
| **[dsh-better-git-worktree](./packages/better-git-worktree/)** | Run a session in its own self-contained git working copy: a composer Worktree switch, a `worktree_convert` tool, session-list status badges, a header menu, and an archive prompt that decides the working copy's fate. | 0.1.1 | `packages/better-git-worktree` |

# dsh-continue-kicker

**Automatically send "continue" when a turn halts, and stop when that is not helping.**

A host-plane plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). A session that hits its output-token limit just stops, silently, until somebody notices. This plugin notices: it sends one follow-up user message that tells the model to stop re-deriving its reasoning and act, and it gives up after a configurable number of kicks with no progress in between, so a task genuinely too big for its budget surfaces in the log instead of burning GPU-hours.

## What it kicks on

| Halt | Detected as | Kick |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Output budget exhausted | last `turn/end` reason `max-tokens` | "Do NOT re-derive your thinking: state your conclusion, then act. Be succinct." |
| Reasoning-only empty stop | `completed` turn whose final assistant message has no text and no tool call, with at least `emptyCompletionMinReasoningChars` of reasoning | Same "be decisive" framing |
| Failed turn (opt-in: `kickOnError`) | last `turn/end` reason `error` (the model backend dropped, a provider error) | "The previous turn failed with an error and was cut off before it finished. Please continue from where you left off." |
| Crash-orphaned turn | last `turn/end` reason `interrupted` (synthesized when a session is loaded) | "Please continue from where you left off." |

It never kicks over `aborted` (an explicit Stop, a parent or hook cancel, a disposal), `error` unless `kickOnError` is on, `blocked`, `forked`, a completed turn with real content, or a tail already followed by a user or assistant message.

Two doors feed one decision: `agent/created` (reopening a session, crash recovery) and a live watcher that re-analyses the tail `liveKickDelayMs` after every turn end, so an unattended halt is caught without anyone reopening the session. A third door is explicit: another plugin can ask for one kick of one session through the [`continueKicker` service](#provided-service-continuekicker), which runs the same decision and applies the same guards.

## Install

Installed from a git tag of this repository — it is not published to npm. Replace `<version>` with a released version (tags are named `dsh-continue-kicker-v<version>`; see [the tag list](https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins/tags)):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-continue-kicker-v<version>&path:/packages/continue-kicker"
```

That installs the package into the profile and enables its bundle. If you manage the profile's `package.json` yourself, the pnpm equivalent is below — then also add `dsh-continue-kicker` to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`, because `pnpm add` alone installs the plugin without enabling it:

```sh
pnpm add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-continue-kicker-v<version>&path:/packages/continue-kicker"
```

> **Warning:** never `pnpm add dsh-continue-kicker` (or `dsh plugin add dsh-continue-kicker`) by bare name. That resolves from the npm registry, where an unscoped `dsh-*` name may belong to an unrelated author and is **not** this plugin.

Restart dsh. With no configuration it works with the defaults below.

## Configuration

Set these on the plugin's row in your own profile patch (`config:` block). **A top-level row with a `config:` block replaces the whole config object**, so list every key you want to differ from the default in the same row; unlisted keys fall back to the defaults below. The bundle's own layer carries no config for the same reason.

| Key | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cooldownMs` | `60000` | Minimum time between kicks for the same session. |
| `liveKickDelayMs` | `3000` | Delay between a live turn end and the tail re-analysis. Lets a fast manual recovery land first. |
| `maxConsecutiveKicks` | `5` | Runaway guard: after this many kicks (all flavors together, counted from the session's event log) with no normally completed turn and no genuine user message in between, the plugin stops kicking that session and logs an error. `0` disables kicking entirely, quietly (the `kickOn*` flags are the finer-grained off switches). |
| `kickOnInterrupted` | `true` | Kick crash-orphaned turns. |
| `kickOnMaxTokens` | `true` | Kick output-token-limit halts. |
| `kickOnEmptyCompletion` | `true` | Kick reasoning-only completed turns. |
| `kickOnError` | `false` | Kick turns that ended with `reason.kind: 'error'`. Off by default because blindly retrying a failing backend can loop; the runaway guard and cooldown bound it. You would want it for unattended work on a backend that drops now and then (a gateway restart, a network blip): the session resumes by itself once the backend is back instead of sitting dead until someone notices. |
| `includeSubagents` | `false` | Also kick delegated child sessions (`origin: subagent` or `delegationDepth > 0`). Off by default: auto-kicking a child fights the parent's own delegation and retry flow. |
| `logToStderr` | `false` | Write this plugin's log lines to stderr (see Logging). Needed to see them at all on dsh 0.2.0-rc.2. |
| `emptyCompletionMinReasoningChars` | `500` | Reasoning length below which a content-empty completed turn is left alone. |
| `interruptedKickText` | built in | Text sent for an interrupted turn. |
| `maxTokensKickText` | built in | Text sent for a max-tokens halt. Forbids re-deriving the lost reasoning; a plain "please continue" invites another long think straight back into the wall. |
| `emptyCompletionKickText` | built in | Text sent for a reasoning-only empty stop. |
| `errorKickText` | built in | Text sent for a failed turn when `kickOnError` is on. |

Resolution lives in [`src/config.mjs`](./src/config.mjs) and is [tested](./test/config.test.mjs). An unknown key, a string where a number belongs, or an empty text prints one warning at boot and falls back to the default.

Example row (the default for `maxConsecutiveKicks` is 5; 3 here is just an example):

```yaml
- id: continue-kicker
  name: dsh-continue-kicker
  config:
    cooldownMs: 60000
    liveKickDelayMs: 3000
    maxConsecutiveKicks: 3
    kickOnInterrupted: true
    kickOnMaxTokens: true
    kickOnEmptyCompletion: true
    kickOnError: true
    includeSubagents: false
    logToStderr: true
```

## Which turn-end reasons kick

From `TurnEndReasonMap` in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session`:

| `reason.kind` | Meaning | Kicked? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `max-tokens` | output budget hit | yes, `kickOnMaxTokens` |
| `interrupted` | crash-orphaned turn closed on load | yes, `kickOnInterrupted` |
| `completed` | model stopped itself | only a reasoning-only empty one, `kickOnEmptyCompletion` |
| `error` | the turn failed (`error` holds message and code) | yes, only with `kickOnError` |
| `aborted` | cancelled on purpose (`user`, `parent`, `hook`, `disposed`, `legacy`) | never |
| `blocked` | a step was rejected before running | never |
| `forked` | fork-seed marker, never emitted live | never |

## The runaway guard

A kick can itself end in the same halt, so the plugin counts kicks and stops at `maxConsecutiveKicks`.

The count is derived from the session's own event log on every analysis, not kept in memory, so it survives a dsh restart and the live and reopen paths always agree. It is the number of this plugin's kick messages (source kind `plugin:continue-kicker`; the retired bare `plugin` kind counts only when it names this plugin and carries one of the known kick texts) found walking back from the end of the log, up to the nearest reset signal:

- a **genuine user message**: source kind `user` and nothing else. The plugin's own kicks and any other producer's user-role messages (goals, other plugins) neither reset nor count.
- a turn that **completed normally**. A reasoning-only completion is a kickable halt, not progress, so it does not reset.

Every flavor counts together: max-tokens, empty-completion, error and interrupted. So the cap also bounds a crash loop: a session that keeps getting killed mid-turn and resumed stops being resumed after `maxConsecutiveKicks` kicks until a user message or a completed turn arrives. At the cap the plugin logs an error naming the session ("needs human attention") and does not kick. Only the cooldown timestamp is in memory; a restart forgets it, which at worst allows one extra kick that the stateless cap still bounds.

Changed from 0.1.0: the old reset fired only when a genuine user message was the *last* event, but a halted turn always ends in `turn/end`, so a new prompt after the cap never reset it; the count lived in memory and was lost on restart; and interrupted kicks were not counted at all.

The kick is written with source kind `plugin:continue-kicker`. Session format V4 refuses the bare kind `plugin`, so a session carrying such a message could not be reopened after a restart.

## Provided service: `continueKicker`

Besides watching sessions on its own, the plugin provides a service named `continueKicker` so another plugin that owns a session's lifecycle can ask for one explicit recovery kick instead of waiting for the automatic doors. `dsh-kanban` uses it: when a role turn halts, the engine asks for a kick and waits for the result, so the recovery is part of the workflow rather than something that happens to a parked session.

```js
const kicker = ctx.get('continueKicker')   // undefined when this plugin is not installed
```

| Member | Shape | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | `1` | the contract version. It goes up only on a breaking change; a consumer that sees an unknown version should treat the details as unreliable. |
| `kick(sessionId, options?)` | `(string, { bypassCooldown?: boolean }) => result` | runs one decision for one live session and sends the kick if it is due. Synchronous; never throws. |

`kick` returns one of:

| Result | When |
| --- | --- |
| `{ kicked: true, flavor, consecutive }` | a kick was sent. `flavor` is `max-tokens`, `interrupted`, `empty-completion` or `error`; `consecutive` is this kick's number in the runaway count. |
| `{ kicked: false, why }` | nothing was sent: the session is not live, its tail is not a kickable halt, the halt's `kickOn*` switch is off, the session is an excluded subagent, or the cooldown is running. |
| `{ kicked: false, why, stopped: true }` | the runaway guard declined: this session has already had `maxConsecutiveKicks` kicks with no progress and needs a human. |

The service is the **same decision, not a second one**: `kick()` runs `decide()` over the session's own event log with this plugin's resolved settings, sends the same message with the same `plugin:continue-kicker` source kind, records the same cooldown, and is bounded by the same runaway counter. A caller therefore gets the plugin's policy instead of a private copy of it, and the automatic doors keep working alongside it — a kick sent through the service lands in the log like any other, so the watcher's delayed re-analysis of the same halt sees a kick already awaiting its result and does nothing.

`bypassCooldown: true` opens only the cooldown gate. It exists because a caller that just watched a turn fail is asking for recovery, not re-analysing a halt it kicked a second ago; every other gate (the per-kind switches, the subagent scope, `maxConsecutiveKicks`) still applies.

One consequence of removing that spacing is worth knowing about: a kick message only lands in the session's event log when the turn it starts claims it, so a caller that asks for kicks back to back can be reading a log one kick behind its own sending. The guard takes the higher of the log count and the kicks this process has actually sent, so the lag cannot buy an extra kick; a genuine user message or a normally completed turn resets both together.

**The service is optional for the consumer.** A caller must resolve it lazily (`ctx.get` at use time, not at boot), duck-type `typeof kicker?.kick === 'function'`, and degrade to its own behaviour when it is absent — the same rule `dsh-kanban` follows for the `betterGitWorktree` service. Nothing here requires a caller: with no consumer installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

## Logging

Every decision, kick or skip, is logged with its reason, through the host logger under the name `continue-kicker`.

**Where those lines go (dsh 0.2.0-rc.2):** nowhere you can read. The harness registers no console or file exporter on the logger; plugin lines only land in an in-memory ring buffer (`ctx.logger.buffer`, 1000 entries) that nothing displays, and only startup warnings and errors are surfaced, inside a startup failure. So `journalctl -u dsh | grep continue-kicker` finds nothing by default. Set `logToStderr: true` and the plugin registers its own exporter that writes only its own lines to stderr, which a service manager (journald under systemd) captures:

```
2026-10-15T18:28:05.590Z INFO continue-kicker created: kicked session s1 (flavor=max-tokens, consecutive=1)
```

The kick itself is also visible in the conversation as a notice row ("Auto-resumed after a max-tokens halt (2/5)"), but the "needs human attention" error at the cap appears only in the log. A general fix (surface plugin logs in the harness) belongs upstream or in a separate plugin.

## Compatibility

Requires dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 or later. Declared in `package.json` under `engines.dsh` and on every `@deepseek-ai/dsh*` peer as `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0 || >=0.3.0-0`. dsh checks these ranges itself, counting prereleases, so it accepts every harness build from 0.2.0-rc.2 on; on a harness outside them `dsh plugin add` refuses the install, and a profile that already has it skips the bundle with a log line. pnpm's own peer check is narrower: it admits only `0.2.0-rc.*` and `0.3.0-*` prereleases (plus every stable release from 0.2.0), so on other prereleases it reports a peer mismatch that dsh does not.

## Development

```sh
node --test packages/continue-kicker/test/*.test.mjs   # decisions + config
node scripts/verify.mjs --package dsh-continue-kicker  # release contract
node scripts/compose-smoke.mjs continue-kicker         # real dsh composition
```

`src/decide.mjs` and `src/config.mjs` import nothing from dsh; `src/host.mjs` is the thin Cordis wiring. See [`../../docs/authoring.md`](../../docs/authoring.md).

# dsh-plugins

Public [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugins by [Chris Johnson](https://github.com/chrisjohnson). One repository, independently installable plugins — each with its own README, its own tests, its own changelog and its own version.

## Install

**Nothing here is published to npm.** Every release is a git tag on this repository, named `<package>-v<version>` (for example `dsh-model-switch-v0.2.1`), and you install a plugin by pinning that tag plus the package's subdirectory:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#<package>-v<version>&path:/packages/<dir>"
```

`dsh plugin add` hands that spec to pnpm and also lists the package under the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`, which is what activates its configuration layer. If you manage a profile's `package.json` yourself, the same spec works with pnpm directly — but then add the package name to `dsh.profile.bundles` by hand, because a plain `pnpm add` installs the plugin without enabling it:

```sh
pnpm add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#<package>-v<version>&path:/packages/<dir>"
```

Pick the tag from [the repository's tags](https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins/tags); `<dir>` is the folder under `packages/` in the index below.

> **Warning — do not install these by bare name.** `pnpm add dsh-model-switch` (or `dsh plugin add dsh-model-switch`) resolves against the npm registry, and the npm package called `dsh-model-switch` belongs to an unrelated author: it is **not** this plugin. The same can happen to any unscoped `dsh-*` name. Always use the git-tag spec above.

## Index

| Plugin | What it is for | Latest | Directory |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **[dsh-model-switch](./packages/model-switch/)** | Let the agent switch its own model mid-session, with a context-window fit guard so neither it nor a human in the composer can strand a conversation on a model too small to read it. | 0.2.1 | `packages/model-switch` |
| **[dsh-image-search-searxng](./packages/image-search-searxng/)** | A model-facing `image_search` tool over your own SearXNG, rendered inline in the Web GUI. | 0.2.0 | `packages/image-search-searxng` |
| **[dsh-continue-kicker](./packages/continue-kicker/)** | Automatically send "continue" when a turn halts on the output-token limit (or after a crash, or on a reasoning-only empty stop), with a runaway guard that stops after repeated kicks with no progress. | 0.2.0 | `packages/continue-kicker` |
| **[dsh-loop-watchdog](./packages/loop-watchdog/)** | Detect an agent stuck in a loop before each step (a deterministic repetition check plus an optional model judge), keep an audit ledger of every check, optionally steer the session, and chart the ledger in a `dsh-better-sidebar` panel. | 0.1.0 | `packages/loop-watchdog` |
| **[dsh-scheduled-queue](./packages/scheduled-queue/)** | Schedule the composer's draft to be sent to its own session later, with a per-session dock to edit, cancel or send now. Runs alongside the official schedule bundle. | 0.1.0 | `packages/scheduled-queue` |
| **[dsh-kanban](./packages/kanban/)** | Ticket-centric work organizer and code-driven workflow engine: a local SQLite board whose phases spawn sandboxed role sessions, gate on per-provider capacity, verify machine-readable conditions, and record a complete time/token ledger. | 0.1.0 | `packages/kanban` |
| **[dsh-model-capacity](./packages/model-capacity/)** | Process-wide, per-provider model-call capacity: interactive calls queue FIFO, subagent dispatch gets an immediate capacity error with free-route suggestions, and a panel inspects active leases, waiters and reservations. | 0.1.0 | `packages/model-capacity` |
| **[dsh-better-git-worktree](./packages/better-git-worktree/)** | Run a session in its own self-contained git working copy: a composer Worktree switch, a `worktree_convert` tool, session-list status badges, a header menu, and an archive prompt that decides the working copy's fate. | 0.1.1 | `packages/better-git-worktree` |
| **[dsh-session-cost](./packages/session-cost/)** | A compact estimated-cost badge in the composer stats bar: reads the session billed-token buckets and prices them with public models.dev rates, hidden at $0. | 0.1.0 | `packages/session-cost` |
| **[dsh-math-literal](./packages/math-literal/)** | Keeps single-`$` dollars literal in web chat: unpaired `$` in settled markdown renders as a literal dollar sign (matching the streaming arm) instead of opening an inline-math pair, while real math and code regions are untouched. | 0.1.0 | `packages/math-literal` |
| **[dsh-browser](./packages/browser/)** | One browser context per DSH session on a single shared remote Browserless connection for `dsh-playwright-browser`'s tools, with reconnect after a dropped connection, context cleanup when a session ends, and an announced local fallback. | 0.1.0 | `packages/browser` |

Install lines for the latest release of each package:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-model-switch-v0.2.1&path:/packages/model-switch"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-image-search-searxng-v0.2.0&path:/packages/image-search-searxng"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-continue-kicker-v0.2.0&path:/packages/continue-kicker"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-loop-watchdog-v0.1.0&path:/packages/loop-watchdog"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-scheduled-queue-v0.1.0&path:/packages/scheduled-queue"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-kanban-v0.1.0&path:/packages/kanban"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-model-capacity-v0.1.0&path:/packages/model-capacity"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-better-git-worktree-v0.1.1&path:/packages/better-git-worktree"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-session-cost-v0.1.0&path:/packages/session-cost"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-math-literal-v0.1.0&path:/packages/math-literal"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-browser-v0.1.0&path:/packages/browser"
```

Each package's README is the contract: what it does, every configuration key and what happens when it is unset, how it fails, how to install it, and how to run its checks. Nothing important lives only here.

## Releases

1. A release is a normal pull request that bumps one package's version and moves its CHANGELOG `Unreleased` entry under that version.
2. After it merges, the tag `<package>-v<version>` is cut on that merge commit and pushed. Nothing is committed directly to `main`.
3. Consumers pin the tag with the install spec above. A tag is never moved or rewritten once pushed.

Details: [docs/releasing.md](./docs/releasing.md).

## What "a plugin from this repo" means

- **Plain ESM, no build step.** `git clone && npm test` works with nothing installed. No bundler, no TypeScript layer, no generated client — what the harness loads is what is in `src/`.
- **Every plugin declares `dsh.bundle.patch`**, so one command installs *and* activates it; nothing here needs a hand-edited `cordis.yml`.
- **Deployment-specific values are configuration, never defaults.** A plugin that "works on my machine" because it hard-codes my provider ids is broken for everyone else. `node scripts/verify.mjs` fails the build on author-local paths and provider ids.
- **Nothing is required to be configured.** Optional features report themselves unavailable and name the key that enables them, instead of throwing at boot or failing at first use.
- **Every decision worth testing lives in a module that imports nothing from dsh**, which is what makes the tests real rather than decorative.

## Checking this repository

```sh
npm run check          # verify + hook gate + all tests, no install needed
node scripts/verify.mjs            # the release contract (see below)
node scripts/compose-smoke.mjs     # install into a throwaway profile, import, compose
```

`scripts/verify.mjs` is the interesting one: it enforces the rules that make a plugin installable and trustworthy — `dsh.bundle.patch` present and loading the package by name, `dsh.client` matched by an `./client` export, one harness peer range across every package (`>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0 || >=0.3.0-0`; dsh checks it with prereleases included, while plain node-semver/pnpm admit only `0.2.0-rc.*` and `0.3.0-*` prereleases from it), every shipped file inside the `files` allowlist (all a git-tag install ships), a git-tag install line (and no bare-name one) in every package README, every config key documented in its README, every package listed in the index above, and no deployment leakage. It runs on CI for every push and it runs on a bare clone.

## Contributing

Issues and pull requests are welcome — see [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md). If you are an agent working in this repository, read [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) first; it is short and it exists because these plugins run with your user's credentials.

For how these plugins get developed, tested against a live harness, released and consumed by the deployment they came from, see [docs/testing.md](./docs/testing.md) and [docs/releasing.md](./docs/releasing.md).

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](./LICENSE).

If you manage the profile's `package.json` yourself, the pnpm equivalent is below — then also add `dsh-image-search-searxng` to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`, because `pnpm add` alone installs the plugin without enabling it: ```sh pnpm add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-image-search-searxng-v&path:/packages/image-search-searxng" ``` > **Warning:** never install this plugin by bare name from the npm registry. Nothing from this repository is published there, so whatever a bare `pnpm add dsh-image-search-searxng` resolves to — now or later — is not this plugin. (The sibling name `dsh-model-switch` is already taken on npm by an unrelated author.) Restart dsh. The tool is then available to every agent preset — the bundle's patch layer mounts the plugin at the profile level, so no per-preset `agent.cordis.yml` editing is involved. Zero configuration is required if your SearXNG answers on `http://localhost:8888`. ## Configuration | Key | Environment | Default | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `baseURL` | `SEARXNG_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8888` | Where your SearXNG lives. Trailing slashes are trimmed; a value that is not an `http(s)` URL is rejected at boot rather than failing at the first search. | | `apiKey` | `SEARXNG_API_KEY` | — | Sent as `preference[api_key]`, for SearXNG instances with API support enabled. | | `maxResults` | `SEARXNG_NUM_RESULTS` | `8` | Default result count the model gets if it does not ask. A per-call `maxResults` argument still wins, clamped to 1–30. | Precedence is **config → environment → default**. To override in your profile patch, add the keys to the row this plugin inserts: ```yaml - id: image-search-searxng name: dsh-image-search-searxng config: baseURL: http://searxng.internal:8080 maxResults: 5 ``` If the plugin is already mounted by its bundle, a config-only row keyed by `id` is enough, and `!!js` lets the row pass environment variables through. Unset variables arrive as `undefined` and fall back exactly as an absent key would: ```yaml - id: image-search-searxng config: baseURL: !!js process.env.SEARXNG_BASE_URL ``` One caveat worth knowing about patch layers generally: a patch **replaces a row's entire `config` object**, it does not deep-merge. Restating `baseURL` in a later layer drops `apiKey` unless you restate that too — which is why this plugin ships its row with no `config` block at all and resolves defaults in code. ## What the model actually receives Titles, source pages, resolutions, and one markdown image link per result: ``` 1. **NEMA 14-50 wiring** ![NEMA 14-50 wiring](https://example.com/diagram.png) Source: https://example.com/receptacles Resolution: 1024x768 ``` The tool's canonical value is `{ results: [{ title?, imgSrc, sourceUrl, resolution? }] }`, and its model-facing result is that list rendered as a single `text` content block — no `image` blocks, no attachments. The plugin writes no session messages of its own. That link is not decoration. dsh's own `dsh-client-ui-primitives` renderer turns `![alt](url)` into a real `` for any `http(s)` URL — there is no domain allowlist — and falls back to alt text only when the browser's own image request fails (hotlink protection, dead link). So results appear as pictures whenever the source host cooperates, with no code-level distinction between the two cases. The tool description tells the model to copy the links verbatim precisely because rewriting one into a plain `[text](url)` link removes the picture. ## Why a separate tool instead of extending `web_search` Because the shared web seam has nowhere to put an image. `WebSearchRequest` and `WebSearchSource` in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web` carry no category and no image fields, so adding them means patching multiple upstream packages that every future dsh upgrade would then have to be re-verified against. A standalone tool with its own schema costs one registration and stays working across upgrades. This is the same shape `dsh-web-search-searxng` chose. ## What this plugin deliberately does not do - **It does not show the model the images.** The model receives text: titles and URLs. It cannot describe, compare, or verify what is depicted, and the tool description says so in as many words, because "I looked at the diagram and it shows…" is otherwise a very tempting hallucination. - **It does not fetch images through your model's attachment pipeline.** Real image *attachments* would route arbitrary third-party URLs through the vision/attachment path — a much larger blast radius than "the user can see search results" warrants. - **It does not fall back to a hosted search API.** If SearXNG is unreachable the tool call fails with the HTTP status, rather than silently querying somebody else's service. ## Compatibility Requires dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 or later. Declared in `package.json` under `engines.dsh` and on the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` peer as `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0 || >=0.3.0-0`. dsh checks the range itself, counting prereleases, so it accepts every harness build from 0.2.0-rc.2 on; on a harness outside it `dsh plugin add` refuses the install, and a profile that already has it skips the bundle with a log line. pnpm's own peer check is narrower: it admits only `0.2.0-rc.*` and `0.3.0-*` prereleases (plus every stable release from 0.2.0), so on other prereleases it reports a peer mismatch that dsh does not. ## Development The plugin is plain ESM with no build step. ```sh node --test packages/image-search-searxng/test/*.test.mjs # logic, no dsh needed node scripts/verify.mjs --package dsh-image-search-searxng # release contract node scripts/compose-smoke.mjs image-search-searxng # real dsh composition ``` `src/searxng.mjs` holds the logic and the tests; `src/index.mjs` is the Cordis wiring. The split is not ceremony — it is what lets the tests run before anything is installed. See [`../../docs/authoring.md`](../../docs/authoring.md). ## License MIT # dsh-plugins Public [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugins by [Chris Johnson](https://github.com/chrisjohnson). One repository, independently installable plugins — each with its own README, its own tests, its own changelog and its own version. ## Install **Nothing here is published to npm.** Every release is a git tag on this repository, named `-v` (for example `dsh-model-switch-v0.2.1`), and you install a plugin by pinning that tag plus the package's subdirectory: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#-v&path:/packages/" ``` `dsh plugin add` hands that spec to pnpm and also lists the package under the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`, which is what activates its configuration layer. If you manage a profile's `package.json` yourself, the same spec works with pnpm directly — but then add the package name to `dsh.profile.bundles` by hand, because a plain `pnpm add` installs the plugin without enabling it: ```sh pnpm add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#-v&path:/packages/" ``` Pick the tag from [the repository's tags](https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins/tags); `` is the folder under `packages/` in the index below. > **Warning — do not install these by bare name.** `pnpm add dsh-model-switch` (or `dsh plugin add dsh-model-switch`) resolves against the npm registry, and the npm package called `dsh-model-switch` belongs to an unrelated author: it is **not** this plugin. The same can happen to any unscoped `dsh-*` name. Always use the git-tag spec above. ## Index | Plugin | What it is for | Latest | Directory | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **[dsh-model-switch](./packages/model-switch/)** | Let the agent switch its own model mid-session, with a context-window fit guard so neither it nor a human in the composer can strand a conversation on a model too small to read it. | 0.2.1 | `packages/model-switch` | | **[dsh-image-search-searxng](./packages/image-search-searxng/)** | A model-facing `image_search` tool over your own SearXNG, rendered inline in the Web GUI. | 0.2.0 | `packages/image-search-searxng` | | **[dsh-continue-kicker](./packages/continue-kicker/)** | Automatically send "continue" when a turn halts on the output-token limit (or after a crash, or on a reasoning-only empty stop), with a runaway guard that stops after repeated kicks with no progress. | 0.2.0 | `packages/continue-kicker` | | **[dsh-loop-watchdog](./packages/loop-watchdog/)** | Detect an agent stuck in a loop before each step (a deterministic repetition check plus an optional model judge), keep an audit ledger of every check, optionally steer the session, and chart the ledger in a `dsh-better-sidebar` panel. | 0.1.0 | `packages/loop-watchdog` | | **[dsh-scheduled-queue](./packages/scheduled-queue/)** | Schedule the composer's draft to be sent to its own session later, with a per-session dock to edit, cancel or send now. Runs alongside the official schedule bundle. | 0.1.0 | `packages/scheduled-queue` | | **[dsh-kanban](./packages/kanban/)** | Ticket-centric work organizer and code-driven workflow engine: a local SQLite board whose phases spawn sandboxed role sessions, gate on per-provider capacity, verify machine-readable conditions, and record a complete time/token ledger. | 0.1.0 | `packages/kanban` | | own self-contained git working copy: a composer Worktree switch, a `worktree_convert` tool, session-list status badges, a header menu, and an archive prompt that decides the working copy's fate. | 0.1.1 | `packages/better-git-worktree` | | **[dsh-session-cost](./packages/session-cost/)** | A compact estimated-cost badge in the composer stats bar: reads the session billed-token buckets and prices them with public models.dev rates, hidden at $0. | 0.1.0 | `packages/session-cost` | | **[dsh-math-literal](./packages/math-literal/)** | Keeps single-`$` dollars literal in web chat: unpaired `$` in settled markdown renders as a literal dollar sign (matching the streaming arm) instead of opening an inline-math pair, while real math and code regions are untouched. | 0.1.0 | reconnect after a dropped connection, context cleanup when a session ends, and an announced local fallback. | 0.1.0 | `packages/browser` | Install lines for the latest release of each package: ```sh "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-image-search-searxng-v0.2.0&path:/packages/image-search-searxng" dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-loop-watchdog-v0.1.0&path:/packages/loop-watchdog" dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-scheduled-queue-v0.1.0&path:/packages/scheduled-queue" dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-kanban-v0.1.0&path:/packages/kanban" dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-model-capacity-v0.1.0&path:/packages/model-capacity" dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-better-git-worktree-v0.1.1&path:/packages/better-git-worktree" dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-session-cost-v0.1.0&path:/packages/session-cost" dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-math-literal-v0.1.0&path:/packages/math-literal" dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-browser-v0.1.0&path:/packages/browser" ``` Each package's README is the contract: what it does, every configuration key and what happens when it is unset, how it fails, how to install it, and how to run its checks. Nothing important lives only here. ## Releases 1. A release is a normal pull request that bumps one package's version and moves its CHANGELOG `Unreleased` entry under that version. 2. After it merges, the tag `-v` is cut on that merge commit and pushed. Nothing is committed directly to `main`. 3. Consumers pin the tag with the install spec above. A tag is never moved or rewritten once pushed. Details: [docs/releasing.md](./docs/releasing.md). ## What "a plugin from this repo" means - **Plain ESM, no build step.** `git clone && npm test` works with nothing installed.
