# DSH Remote Agents

**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

Use remote Claude Code, Codex, DSH, Grok, CodeBuddy and Antigravity directly in DSH's ordinary model picker and main conversation. DSH connects to each CLI's native protocol over system OpenSSH. **No Paseo daemon, SDK or remote service is required.**
## Main conversation

Each CLI appears as a separate provider in DSH's ordinary model picker:

1. Open **Settings → Remote agents** and add an SSH host and select the CLIs you want to enable. Saving discovers only their models; you can also save a machine first and choose its CLIs later. **No project name or project path is required.**
2. Select a remote workspace in DSH (see [Remote workspaces](#remote-workspaces)), then choose a model labelled with its host under **Claude**, **Codex** or another CLI provider. The native picker and `/model` only show models belonging to that workspace’s machine. Local, missing or unverified workspaces hide remote models. Because the workspace already identifies the machine, the composer button and the menu’s **Model** row show only the model name, such as **Opus 5.5**; the model list shows the host in muted text after each name, and the button’s tooltip shows the full name.
3. Send messages in the normal composer. Conversations execute in **the current workspace’s verified remote directory**, translating dsh-remote mirrors and Claude SSH placeholders. Every send and follow-up checks machine and directory placement again, so an old model selection cannot send to another machine after a workspace switch. Missing remote directories fail explicitly.

Change the CLI checkboxes on a machine card and click **Apply selection**. Disabled CLIs are neither probed nor shown in the model picker; existing agents keep running. New machines start with no CLIs selected, while older saved machines retain their existing provider scope.

The native model-label contribution coexists with other plugins' label renderers. Custom Codex-style composer pickers also omit the host from captions that match a saved remote model catalog, while retaining their full tooltip, reasoning effort and selection controls. Model catalogs and saved selections keep their original names and IDs.

**Collapsible model groups:** click a provider heading, such as **CodeBuddy Code**, to expand or collapse its models. The current model’s group starts expanded; other groups start collapsed. Manual choices are remembered in this browser. Searching expands matching groups, and clearing the search restores your choices. The plugin adds folding to the provider headings inside the native model list. DSH retains the outer menu, model labels, reasoning controls and any additional selection options.

Model catalogs are saved per machine on the DSH server and shared between clients. The same model entry works across workspaces on that machine without per-project duplicates. The picker reads cached models and filters by the workspace’s SSH host, user and port; process-routed workspaces verify the actual machine identity. Use **Refresh models** beside the machine after CLI/account changes or to discover an existing host after upgrading. Discovery uses the remote account's home directory; execution uses the conversation's workspace directory, and project-specific model availability is validated at startup.

- Each DSH conversation and selected machine / CLI has an independent native CLI session, with its working directory bound on the first message. Follow-ups reuse it, including after a DSH restart when that CLI supports resume. Switching models within a CLI resumes that same session; a non-resumable CLI asks you to start a new conversation. Previously separate model sessions remain accessible. Switching machines or CLIs supplies available conversation text as context; DSH's local system prompt, injected workspace instructions and local tool schemas are excluded.
- Replies and thinking stream into the main conversation. Remote tool calls appear as native DSH tool cards; they execute on the remote machine. They are recorded as completed external work, so DSH never executes them again. Approvals and questions use DSH's native prompts.
- The DSH thinking selector uses the CLI's discovered reasoning levels. Claude and Codex follow the conversation's DSH permission (the composer or `/permission`): **Read Only** runs Claude in `default` (ask before tools) and Codex in read-only, **Workspace Write** runs Claude in **Accept edits** and Codex in workspace-write, **Full access** runs both without approval prompts, and **Auto review** runs Claude in **Auto** and Codex in workspace-write. A change applies from the next message and overrides a mode chosen in Open sessions. A custom DSH permission keeps the session's current mode; a new conversation with one uses the remote CLI's own settings. **Stop** or cancelling the response interrupts the remote CLI turn. Quitting DSH or reloading the plugin does not; see [Persistence and recovery](#persistence-and-recovery).
- **Codex Fast:** Codex models that offer a faster service tier also appear as a separate picker entry, such as **GPT-5.5 Fast · build-box**. Fast uses more of the remote account's quota. Switching between the normal and Fast entries keeps the same Codex thread. The normal entry uses the remote Codex configuration, including a `service_tier` set there.
- **Usage ring:** a ring before the send button shows how full the remote session's context window is. Hover over it, or click it, to see the remote account's plan limits for Claude and Codex, such as the session and weekly windows. These come from the CLI on the SSH host, so credentials never leave it. Limits are read when the panel opens, cached for five minutes and read again after a turn finishes; use the refresh button to check now.
- **Prompt cache:** the same panel shows input/output tokens, cache reads/writes and the fraction of input tokens served from cache for the latest reported Claude or Codex model request. This is per model request, so a tool loop may update it several times in one turn. Codex also offers an expandable thread total. Counts are saved with the session and remain available after detach or restart. Unreported fields show **Unknown**; a reported zero stays **0**. Cached tokens still occupy the context window. These are CLI-reported token counts, not a billing estimate.
- Lost responses can replay the saved output by message identity without sending the task again. Unconfirmed delivery or an unfinished response after disconnection is reported explicitly. Send a new message to continue the saved session.
- Main chat accepts **text, uploaded images and files**. Claude and Codex receive images through their native protocols; ACP CLIs expose image input only when their initialization reports support. Files are streamed over SSH into the verified remote workspace and supplied as read-only paths for the CLI’s file tools. Only attachments from the conversation are transferred. The CLI uses its own credentials, tools, instructions and context management. DSH summarization runs in a disposable CLI session, separate from the coding conversation.

## Remote workspaces

Use DSH's **Add workspace** to work on a directory of a saved machine. With machines saved, it opens a dialog with two tabs: **This computer** uses the system folder picker as before, and **Remote machine** browses the selected machine's directories over SSH. Choose a folder and **Use this folder** to add it; the remote models of that machine are then available in its conversations. Without saved machines, **Add workspace** opens the system folder picker directly.

- The dialog remembers the last tab and each machine's last folder. Paths may start with `~/`. Hidden folders are listed after **Show hidden folders**.
- Files stay on the remote machine. DSH records the workspace as a local anchor under `$DSH_HOME/remote-workspaces/`, in the same format as the dsh-remote plugin. Use the **Remote workspace** panel for live files and select **Remote workspace** in the native terminal's shell menu for an interactive SSH terminal. The default local Files view and local shells still refer to the anchor.
- If dsh-remote is also installed, its **Add workspace** dialog takes precedence.

### Integrated workspace tools

In a conversation on a remote workspace, the right sidebar's **Workspace files** (and its shortcut, ⌘P on macOS) opens the remote files instead of the empty local anchor, and **Remote workspace** there opens all the tools below. In local conversations, Workspace files is DSH's own and Remote workspace is not listed. The tools are also in **Settings → Remote agents → Remote workspace**. They follow the current conversation's verified machine and directory. No separate `dsh-remote` installation or second machine registry is required.

- **Files:** browse directories, create files/folders, search text, edit UTF-8 files, rename/delete files, and upload/download binary files. Saving checks the file's SHA-256 revision and refuses stale edits; **Reload file** fetches the latest version. The editor limit is 256 KiB and the transfer limit is 50 MiB per file. File operations stay inside the verified remote workspace and reject symlinks that escape it. Native session file links open the remote editor after the active workspace has been verified.
- **Commands and terminal:** run a command in the workspace with separate stdout/stderr, exit status, a 30-second timeout and bounded output. For interactive programs or longer jobs, choose **Remote workspace** in the native terminal's shell menu. Commands and terminals use the remote account's normal privileges. A missing or invalid binding fails explicitly.
- **Sync:** preview **Pull remote → local mirror** or **Push local mirror → remote**, then **Apply preview**. A three-way content comparison preserves files changed on both sides as conflicts. The preview lists copies and deletions; changes to that plan require another preview. Git, dependency/build directories, plugin metadata and symbolic links are skipped. Sync is explicit and does not run while an agent edits files unless you request it.
- **Tunnels:** save local or reverse SSH forwards and start/stop/remove them. Local forwards bind to `0.0.0.0`; **Open** uses this machine's Tailscale address. Reverse listeners use remote loopback. Definitions survive restart but must be started again. Closing DSH stops tunnels without stopping persistent coding agents.
- **Remote DSH:** start an isolated remote `dsh web` instance, or enter an existing remote loopback login URL, then connect over SSH and open it locally. Starting requires a compatible `dsh` on the remote login PATH; this feature does not install DSH. Managed data lives under `~/.dsh-remote-agents/web-ui/<port>/home`. **Stop managed instance** stops only the process recorded for this workspace. Closing its tunnel leaves the remote instance running. Login tokens are not saved in tunnel definitions.

Ordinary DSH models also receive a **`remote_workspace`** tool for session-scoped file access and commands, plus guidance to read remote `AGENTS.md`. File mutations and commands request native DSH approval. Remote CLI models continue using their own native tools and approval modes.

### Moving from dsh-remote

In **Settings → Remote agents**, expand **Import machines from dsh-remote**. Import reuses SSH aliases, skips already registered endpoints, starts with no CLIs enabled, and leaves the old registry, current-machine selection and workspace metadata untouched. Enable the CLIs you need afterward. Existing compatible workspaces continue to work.

This implementation supports **Linux/macOS remote hosts with Node.js 18+ and system OpenSSH key/SSH-agent authentication**. Passwords, keychain secrets and native-only authentication/proxy settings are not copied. Move such connection settings into `~/.ssh/config` and load encrypted keys into your SSH agent first. Native Windows remote workspaces, password/OTP authentication and automatic remote DSH installation are not included.

After importing, use **Test connection** and verify live files, terminal and models before uninstalling `dsh-remote`. Keep `$DSH_HOME/remote-workspaces/` and its metadata. The plugin can coexist with `dsh-remote` during migration; uninstalling the old plugin is a separate action.

## Unified remote sessions

Open **Settings → Remote agents → Open sessions**. There is no remote sessions entry in the sidebar. The list includes main-chat bindings and delegated agents, with search by title, CLI, host or path, and **In progress / History / Archived** views. The default view shows running tasks, pending approvals and errors; idle sessions move to History and remain available to continue. The two-pane interface groups sessions by date and shows the project, host and update time. Read conversations on the right; permission modes and renaming are in the header’s Session options. Archived sessions are linked at the bottom of the list. Agent replies render Markdown, and consecutive tool calls are collapsed into an expandable group.

Choose **Permission mode** when creating a session or while an existing session is idle. Changes apply to the next message. In a main chat, the DSH permission replaces this choice with its next message. Claude defaults to **Remote CLI settings**, preserving the remote account/project permission configuration instead of forcing `default`. Existing sessions keep their explicit mode; select **Remote CLI settings** to return to the remote default. DSH workspace access does not grant remote CLI permissions. **Accept edits** still asks for commands requiring approval; **Full access** permits commands and edits without individual approval.

**Claude Auto:** select **Auto · safety checks** to launch or resume with `--permission-mode auto`, including existing sessions saved before this option was added. This keeps Claude's classifier checks. **Remote CLI settings** uses the non-interactive `claude -p` default, which can differ from an interactive terminal: with Claude Code 2.1.302+, an unset permission mode starts `-p` in Manual even when a terminal starts in Auto. The plugin does not change saved modes automatically. Auto requires a CLI/model/account that supports it. See [Claude permission modes](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#tool-calls-denied-in-claude--p-and-agent-sdk-runs).

Native DSH approvals remain one-time grants. When Claude supplies matching allow-rule suggestions, its pending request in this panel also offers session or project approval. Review **Details** before selecting one: project approval sends only those native rules to the remote `.claude/settings.local.json`, so matching requests can be approved in future sessions. The plugin does not create global allow rules or save a one-time approval as a lasting grant. Requests without a suitable suggestion continue to offer one-time approval.

- **Create:** select a remote DSH workspace, then choose its machine's CLI and model and describe the task. The session uses the verified remote directory, translating local workspace anchors. Creation rechecks the workspace so a changed directory or machine cannot use a stale selection.
- **History and follow-ups:** read streaming output, expandable reasoning and tool details, and load earlier history. Send follow-ups to background agents here; use **Open in main chat** for bound conversations so their native DSH history stays consistent.
- **Approvals:** the sidebar counts sessions needing attention. Dismissing a native DSH approval keeps the request pending; respond in the session panel using the CLI's actual permission choices or question form. **Stop** explicitly interrupts the turn.
- **Manage:** rename remote records, archive and restore them. Use **Archive listed history** to archive the current search results in History. Each session is checked again before archiving so newly active sessions and pending approvals are skipped. Archiving preserves history and ends the CLI process. These actions affect the remote record, not the native DSH conversation's title or archive state.
- **Delivery:** wait for the current turn or stop it before sending. After a lost response, **Check delivery** checks the same message without resending it. Pending messages survive reloads and reopening the session within the same browser tab.

Closing the panel leaves background work running, and so do quitting DSH and losing SSH; see [Persistence and recovery](#persistence-and-recovery). Sessions show **Reconnecting** while DSH re-establishes their SSH connection.

## Delegation from DSH

DSH's own agent gets six tools to hand work to remote CLIs, the counterpart of Paseo's `create_agent` and `send_agent_prompt`:

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `remote_agent_list` | Hosts, recent projects and agents with their status |
| `remote_agent_providers` | CLIs, models, modes, thinking levels and speeds available in a remote project |
| `remote_agent_create` | Start an agent with a self-contained task; waits for its reply by default |
| `remote_agent_send` | Follow up with an agent (ID or prefix); refuses to interrupt a working agent unless `interrupt: true` |
| `remote_agent_wait` | Wait for one or more agents and return their replies; a timeout leaves them running |
| `remote_agent_stop` | Interrupt an agent's turn |

Ask DSH something like *"have Codex on build-box fix the failing tests in /srv/app, and Claude review /srv/web in parallel"*. Use `remote_agent_list` to inspect their status and `remote_agent_send` to steer them in the conversation.

- While a tool waits, the remote agent's approval requests and questions appear as **native DSH prompts** in the conversation. A one-time DSH approval never selects a session-wide CLI permission. If you dismiss a prompt, the request stays pending and the tool reports it; `remote_agent_wait` can show the prompt again.
- Starting an agent in a mode that doesn't ask before acting (full access, bypass permissions) requires your explicit approval.
- Stopping the DSH response stops waiting but does **not** stop the remote agents, matching Paseo's independent agents. Stop them with `remote_agent_stop`.
- The tools load when DSH provides agent tools and approvals. Native model routes and settings work without the delegation tool registry.

## Supported CLIs

| CLI | Direct protocol |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code | Native stream-json / control channel |
| Codex | Native `codex app-server` over stdio |
| DSH | ACP v1 `dsh --profile acp` |
| Antigravity | Native `agy` stream-json |
| Grok | ACP v1 `grok agent --no-leader stdio` |
| CodeBuddy | ACP v1 `codebuddy --acp` |

Detection initializes each CLI's protocol and reads its model and mode catalogs without sending a prompt. ACP supports both legacy model/mode fields and `configOptions`, including model-specific reasoning choices. A listed model does not guarantee account access or quota. Install and sign in to each CLI on the remote machine first.

DSH uses the remote `acp` profile's providers, models and credentials. Antigravity needs Node.js 22+ on the remote host for a small inline process forwarder, and **its headless mode denies operations that need interactive approval**. Configure permissions in `agy` first. Grok runs with leader mode disabled. References: [DSH ACP](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/packages/acp/acp/README.md), [Antigravity headless](https://antigravity.google/docs/cli/headless/), [Grok Build](https://docs.x.ai/build/overview), [CodeBuddy ACP](https://www.codebuddy.cn/docs/cli/acp), [ACP config options](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v1/session-config-options).

## Hosts

**Remove** stays available when a host is offline or SSH fails. Hosts with saved sessions ask for confirmation first. **Remove host and sessions** stops attached CLI processes and permanently deletes that host’s plugin sessions (including archived sessions), saved output and model catalog without reconnecting over SSH.

Add machines under **Settings → Remote agents**. Pick a `Host` alias from the DSH machine's `~/.ssh/config` (including `Include` files) or enter `build-box`, `user@build-box` or `ssh://user@build-box:2222`. The original alias is saved, so OpenSSH resolves `HostName`, `User`, `Port`, `IdentityFile` and `ProxyJump` when connecting. The picker never expands wildcards, runs `Match exec` or opens a connection.

The DSH server needs noninteractive key or agent access and verified host keys (`BatchMode=yes`, `StrictHostKeyChecking=yes`). Passwords are not stored. Remote machines need only SSH and the signed-in CLIs, not this plugin. Each host pins its SSH machine identity; if it changes, add the machine again.

Before running discovery or a CLI, SSH loads the remote user’s interactive login environment for Bash, Zsh and Fish. This includes proxy, authentication and configuration-directory variables that may be set only in interactive startup files. Startup output is separated from CLI protocol output, and startup scripts cannot consume CLI input. Other login shells keep the POSIX launch path. The plugin retains an already configured Node.js ≥22. If the current runtime is too old, the plugin selects a compatible installed nvm or Homebrew runtime. Without one, it keeps the existing environment and reports CLI errors; it never installs or upgrades Node automatically.

### Uploaded attachments

Paste or upload images and files in DSH’s normal composer. An attachment-only message is supported. Each message’s copies live under `.dsh-remote-agents/attachments/<task>/<message>/` in the remote workspace, with private directories, read-only files and SHA-256 verification. The files remain available for follow-ups and resumed CLI sessions; you can remove the remote attachment directory when it is no longer needed. Deleting a plugin session clears its local staging copies.

Files are streamed without buffering the entire upload in memory. Images use DSH’s normalized request versions (up to a 1568-pixel edge and a 4 MiB target); each must fit the CLI’s 5 MB limit, with at most 20 images and 32 MiB of image data per request. A failed upload does not start a CLI turn, and retrying an already recorded message does not upload or send it again.

## Install and upgrade

Requires Node.js ≥22.15.0 and DSH ≥0.2.1-rc.2, <0.3.0. Build and install the archive into a DSH profile:

```sh
pnpm --filter dsh-remote-agents pack:plugin
dsh plugin --profile web add "$PWD/dist/dsh-remote-agents-0.2.23.tgz"
```

Restart that profile and refresh the browser. For the Desktop app, fully quit it and use the app's bundled `dsh` with `--profile desktop`.

**Upgrading from 0.2.27:** In a conversation on a remote workspace, the right sidebar's **Workspace files** and ⌘P open the remote files, and **Remote workspace** is listed there only in remote conversations. Local conversations keep DSH's own Workspace files. Refresh the client after updating.

**Upgrading from 0.2.26:** Adds the integrated **Remote workspace** panel (files, commands, sync, tunnels and remote DSH) and a `remote_workspace` tool for DSH models; see [Integrated workspace tools](#integrated-workspace-tools). Machines saved in dsh-remote can be imported from **Settings → Remote agents**. Restart DSH and refresh the client after updating.

**Upgrading from 0.2.25:** Provider groups in the model menu fold again in DSH builds whose model rows carry no model ids, such as the Desktop app: those groups remember their folding by provider name. Groups that already folded keep their saved choices. Refresh the client after updating.

**Upgrading from 0.2.24:** A conversation whose remote CLI failed to start (for example, because the SSH host had no Node.js) no longer stays stuck with "This agent is still working" after the host is fixed: the next message starts the CLI with that message, keeping earlier messages as context. Restart DSH after updating.

**Upgrading from 0.2.23:** A remote CLI is no longer started when its SSH host cannot run the background relay (no Node.js 18+ on the login PATH, or the relay cannot be installed); the response fails with the reason instead of silently using a direct SSH pipe that ends with DSH. Install Node.js 18 or newer on such hosts. New conversations are titled from your first message instead of DSH's title instruction; existing titles are not changed. Restart DSH after updating.

**Upgrading from 0.2.22:** Claude and Codex in the main chat now follow the conversation's DSH permission (the composer or `/permission`) instead of always using the remote CLI's own settings: Workspace Write runs Claude in Accept edits, Full access runs without approval prompts, and Auto review runs Claude in Auto. The DSH permission overrides a mode chosen in Open sessions from the next message. Restart DSH after updating.

**Upgrading from 0.2.21:** Every turn's usage, main chat included, now reaches `dsh-usage-stats` through the `remote-agents/usage` event with the machine name and remote directory, so usage can be broken down by host and workspace. Main chat no longer reports a turn's total to DSH as model usage, because it spans many model calls and would misstate the conversation's context size. Update `dsh-usage-stats` to 0.1.5 together with this version, or main-chat turns are counted twice. Restart DSH after updating.

**Upgrading from 0.2.20:** Each finished turn now records the tokens it used (Claude Code, Codex, and ACP CLIs that report usage). With `dsh-usage-stats` 0.1.3 or later, they appear under **Remote agents** in **Settings → Usage statistics**: main-chat turns through their DSH model call, delegated agents and turns sent from **Open sessions** through a `remote-agents/usage` event. Turns from before the update are not imported. Restart DSH after updating.

**Upgrading from 0.2.19:** **Add workspace** gains a **Remote machine** tab that adds a saved machine's directory as a DSH workspace. Codex now also offers **Remote CLI settings**, which leaves approval policy and sandbox to `~/.codex/config.toml` on the remote machine. New main-chat conversations and agents DSH starts without an explicit mode use it for both Claude and Codex. Existing sessions keep their saved mode. Restart DSH and click **Refresh models** beside each machine after updating.

**Upgrading from 0.2.18:** Remote CLIs now keep running when DSH quits or SSH disconnects, and DSH reconnects and catches up automatically. This needs Node.js 18+ on the SSH host. Restart DSH after updating; sessions created earlier switch to a relay the next time their CLI starts.

**Upgrading from 0.2.17:** Remote sessions use a two-pane reading layout with active/history views, date groups, bulk archiving, Markdown replies and collapsed tool activity. Permission mode and renaming are in the header’s Session options. Existing history and native CLI sessions remain available. Restart DSH and refresh the client after updating.

**Upgrading from 0.2.12:** Adds image and file transfer from the main composer. Restart DSH and refresh the client after updating; refresh host models to pick up each CLI’s declared image capabilities.

**Upgrading from 0.2.11:** Claude now inherits remote permission settings by default. Permission modes and matching session/project approvals are available in **Open sessions**. Existing sessions keep their explicit mode; stop an active session and select **Remote CLI settings** to inherit the remote default.

**Upgrading from 0.2.10:** Fixes `3: Bad file descriptor` when remote login scripts close inherited descriptors, blocking model discovery or CLI startup. Restart DSH after updating, then refresh the host’s models.

**Upgrading from 0.2.9:** Hosts with saved sessions can now be removed after an SSH error. Confirm removal to delete their plugin sessions and saved output without reconnecting.

**Upgrading from 0.2.8:** Remote CLIs now load the remote shell’s interactive login environment. This addresses authentication failures caused by missing shell environment when the same Claude command succeeds in an interactive terminal. Update and restart DSH, refresh the machine’s models, and retry the conversation.

**Upgrading from 0.2.7:** Remote sessions now open only through settings; the sidebar entry has been removed. Update the plugin and refresh the client.

**Upgrading from 0.2.6:** Main-chat models are filtered by the workspace machine and verified again before sending. Existing conversations can continue only when their machine and directory match. Update the server plugin and refresh the client; machines and model caches need no migration.

**Upgrading from 0.2.5:** Fixes provider folding failing to activate on the real DSH client because the previous version redeclared an existing child slot. The native model seat is now preserved. Restart DSH and refresh the client; saved folding preferences still apply.

**Upgrading from 0.2.4:** Provider headings in the composer model menu now expand and collapse. Refresh the client after upgrading; no machine or session migration is needed.

**Upgrading from 0.2.3:** Per-machine CLI selection is now available, and SSH no longer selects an old nvm runtime ahead of a compatible installed Node. Adjust the checkboxes and click **Apply selection**.

**Upgrading from 0.2.2:** Click **Refresh models** beside each machine to populate the machine-wide model menu. Existing project-bound conversations keep their saved working directories; legacy project routes remain resolvable but are hidden from the new picker.

**Upgrading from 0.2.1:** Remote models are grouped directly under their CLI providers and keep the native composer. A unified Remote sessions entry is available in the sidebar. Saved hosts, projects, conversations and output are preserved; the old aggregate route remains resolvable for saved conversations but is not advertised in the model picker.

**Upgrading from 0.2.0:** Main

# DSH Session Models

**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

Supports English and Simplified Chinese, following DSH’s language setting with live updates. English is the fallback when the host has no locale service.

`dsh-session-models` shows which model each conversation uses in the DeepSeek Harness sidebar. A vendor icon (Claude, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Gemini, Grok, Qwen, Kimi, GLM, Doubao, MiniMax, Mistral, Antigravity, CodeBuddy, or a generic mark) fills the cell before each session title. DSH’s own status mark stays visible as a small badge in the icon’s corner: a spinner while the session runs, a yellow dot while it waits for approval or an answer, green when finished, red on failure, and the clock for scheduled tasks. The row’s hover card adds the exact model and, for `dsh-remote-agents` sessions, the remote CLI.

Build and install:

```sh
pnpm --filter dsh-session-models check
pnpm --filter dsh-session-models pack:plugin
dsh plugin --profile web add "$PWD/dist/dsh-session-models-0.1.0.tgz"
```

The icon follows the model the session will use next, the same one DSH’s model picker shows. The model name decides the vendor first, so an aggregator or a multi-model CLI shows the model’s maker; otherwise the provider decides. Sessions whose history is not loaded get one read of DSH’s session projections when their row appears, without opening the conversation. Sessions saved in DSH’s older storage format report no model until they are opened once, which upgrades them; rows without a known model and archived rows keep DSH’s default look.

It never modifies DSH’s DOM. A DSH update that changes that markup can hide the icons until the plugin is updated; status and navigation keep working.

`pnpm --filter dsh-session-models test:ui` runs a browser regression against a copy of the host row markup and requires `agent-browser`. Set `DSH_TEST_SCREENSHOTS=<dir>` to keep light and dark screenshots.

Logos come from [LobeHub Icons](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-icons) (MIT); see [third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). Regenerate them with `node scripts/vendor-icons.mjs <extracted @lobehub/icons-static-svg>`.

| `dsh-remote-agents` | [packages/remote-agents](packages/remote-agents/README.md) | Native DSH chat and task delegation over SSH: run Claude Code, Codex, DSH, Grok, CodeBuddy and Antigravity on remote machines, steer them, and let DSH delegate tasks to them |

Plugin interfaces support English and Simplified Chinese. English is the source and fallback language. On hosts with the DSH locale service, plugins follow **Settings → General → Language** and update immediately, including open panels and known error messages. Requires Node.js ≥ 22.15.0 and pnpm **10.34.7**, pinned in `package.json`.

```sh

corepack pnpm check
corepack pnpm pack:plugins
```

If pnpm is already available at the pinned version, use `pnpm` directly. The repository uses a single `pnpm-lock.yaml`; run dependency installation at the workspace root.

```sh
pnpm build          # Build every package
pnpm typecheck      # Type-check every package
pnpm test           # Run package tests
pnpm check          # Type-check, test, then build
pnpm test:ui        # Run available browser regression suites
pnpm pack:plugins   # Build and pack packages into dist/
```

Work on one plugin with a package filter:

```sh
pnpm --filter dsh-remote-agents pack:plugin
```

Remote Agents **0.2.23** lists only the current workspace machine’s remote models, grouped by Claude, Codex and other CLIs, in DSH's model picker and main conversation. Build `dist/dsh-remote-agents-0.2.23.tgz` with `pnpm --filter dsh-remote-agents pack:plugin`. See [install and upgrade](packages/remote-agents/README.md#install-and-upgrade), including what changed from 0.1.x.



```text
packages/
  remote-agents/        # dsh-remote-agents: source, tests, manifest, docs
  session-models/       # Model icons and status badges on sidebar sessions
  workspace-tags/       # Workspace tags and tag/status grouping in the sidebar
  usage-stats/          # DSH and Claude SSH usage statistics
  gallery/              # Local wallpaper library and DSH backgrounds
  browser-devtools/     # Docked / separate-window debugger for Sidebar Browser tabs
  translate/            # Chat selection and composer translation
scripts/
  build-client.mjs      # Shared DSH web client bundler
tsconfig.base.json     # Shared TypeScript compiler options
pnpm-workspace.yaml    # Discovers packages/*
pnpm-lock.yaml         # Workspace dependency lock
dist/                  # Generated installable archives (ignored)
```

# DSH Usage Statistics

**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

Supports English and Simplified Chinese, following DSH’s language setting with live updates. English is the fallback when the host has no locale service.

`dsh-usage-stats` tracks DSH model calls and remote CLI turns (Claude Code, Codex and ACP CLIs) run through `dsh-remote-agents`. Open **Settings → Usage statistics** and pick a category at the top: provider (remote turns by CLI, such as Codex or Claude Code), workspace, model, model vendor or host. The **Usage breakdown** panel, the detail table and the CSV export all group by that category, with each group's token total, share and request count; switching categories needs no new request. Filter by UTC date, provider, model or session. The `groupBy` API parameter accepts the same five categories, plus `day`, `session` and `source`; `model` groups by the shown model name across providers. DSH's own model calls run on **This computer** and use their conversation's workspace. A **Today** pill at the right of the conversation header, beside the other header utilities, shows today's reported total in your local time zone, refreshes every 10 seconds, and is marked `*` when some of today's requests returned no usage; hover it for exact numbers. The API accepts `tz` (minutes east of UTC, −840 to 840) to bucket days in a local time zone; the dashboard itself stays on UTC.

The dashboard includes four headline metrics, a Token/request trend, category tabs, date presets, expandable filters and a paginated detail table. It supports light/dark themes and narrow windows. Trends include quiet dates and aggregate long ranges into at most 48 equal time buckets without dropping usage.

From the workspace root, with Node.js ≥ 22.15.0 and DSH `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0`:

```sh
corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
corepack pnpm --filter dsh-usage-stats check
corepack pnpm --filter dsh-usage-stats pack:plugin
dsh plugin --profile web add "$PWD/dist/dsh-usage-stats-0.1.5.tgz"
```

For Desktop, fully quit DSH, install with `--profile desktop`, and reopen. For Web, restart the profile and refresh. Install `dsh-remote-agents` 0.2.22 or later to collect the Remote agents source.

Each public `llm/stream` call counts once, including title generation and compaction. This counts stream calls, not individual HTTP attempts. Remote agents are counted once per remote turn, even if the CLI made several model calls. Every remote turn (main chat, delegated agents and turns sent from **Open sessions**) arrives through an event from `dsh-remote-agents` 0.2.22 or later, with the machine and remote directory it ran in; the plugin's own `remote-cli-*` model calls are not counted again. Their providers are `remote-cli-<cli>` and models keep the model name plus any speed tier. Codex turns are the difference in its running thread totals; ACP CLIs are counted only when they report usage. Records from the retired Claude SSH source (`claude-ssh-<host>` providers) are counted under Remote agents. CLIs launched independently outside DSH are not collected. Collection starts when enabled; there is no historical import or account billing access.

Input tokens exclude cache reads/writes. Total tokens use the adapter's explicit total when available, otherwise input + output + cache reads + cache writes. Reasoning is already included in output. The last valid usage snapshot wins. Failed/cancelled calls retain reported usage; calls without usage count toward requests and are visibly marked as missing, with no estimated tokens. Disconnection may prevent final remote usage from arriving. Date bounds are inclusive and use the call's start time in UTC. Active calls appear after closing; the page refreshes every five seconds. Date presets roll forward across UTC midnight on automatic or manual refresh; custom date bounds stay fixed. Currency costs and subscription quota are not estimated.

Data is stored at `${DSH_HOME:-~/.dsh}/storages/dsh-usage-stats/usage.json`; configure `stateDir` to change it. Use separate directories per process/profile: concurrent processes writing to the same file are unsupported. Within one process, plugin reloads share the active store until all tracked calls finish, preserving records from both old and new calls. Records contain IDs, time, provider/model, session, purpose, status, duration and usage, without prompts, responses, tool contents or credentials. Writes use serialized atomic snapshots with mode `0600`. Write failures are logged and shown in the dashboard without breaking model calls. The failure count resets once the plugin is fully disabled and all tracked calls have finished. Invalid existing files prevent startup and remain untouched. All records currently reside in one JSON snapshot; costs grow with history size, with no automatic archival or retention policy.

Run `corepack pnpm --filter dsh-usage-stats test:ui` for browser checks using `agent-browser` and Chrome (`DSH_TEST_BROWSER_PATH` can override the executable). These exercise the real React component against a fixture API; they do not modify a DSH profile or call a real model. See the [Chinese documentation](README.zh-CN.md) for the accounting rules, host interfaces and validation scope.

Run `corepack pnpm --filter dsh-usage-stats preview:ui` to open a demo-only preview at `http://100.96.195.115:4182/#demo`. The server binds to `0.0.0.0`; override the port with `DSH_USAGE_PREVIEW_PORT`. It does not read real usage records.

# DSH Workspace Tags

**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

Supports English and Simplified Chinese, following DSH’s language setting with live updates.

`dsh-workspace-tags` adds colored tags to the workspaces in the DeepSeek Harness sidebar, and two more **Group by** choices in the sidebar’s view options:

- **Tag**: one section per tag, in name order, then **Untagged**. A workspace with several tags appears under each of them.
- **Status**: **Running** (an agent in the workspace is executing), **Waiting for you** (an agent is waiting for an approval, a plan review or an answer), **Completed** (a session finished and you have not opened it yet), then **Idle**. Each status has its own icon. A workspace with sessions in several states appears in each of those sections, and the sections follow live as agents start and stop.

Right-click a workspace, or choose **Tags…** in its **⋯** menu, to tick its tags, create a tag (name and color) that is added to that workspace, or open **Manage tags…** to rename, recolor or delete tags. A workspace’s tags show as small dots at the end of its row in every grouping mode. Sections fold, and the Group by choice and folded sections are remembered per browser. Inside a section, workspaces keep the sidebar’s order; drag workspaces into order under Workspace grouping, since a workspace can appear in several sections.

Tags are stored on the DSH host in `~/.dsh/storages/dsh-workspace-tags/tags.json` (under `DSH_HOME` when set), so the desktop app and remote web clients of the same host share them; open clients pick up changes from others within 30 seconds or when their window regains focus. Deleting a workspace in the sidebar removes its tags.

Build and install:

```sh
pnpm --filter dsh-workspace-tags check
pnpm --filter dsh-workspace-tags pack:plugin
dsh plugin --profile web add "$PWD/dist/dsh-workspace-tags-0.1.0.tgz"
```

Requires DSH 0.2.1-rc.3 or a later 0.2 release.

## How it replaces the sidebar

DSH’s sidebar workspace browser (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace`) offers no extension point for workspace rows or grouping modes, so this package contains a copy of it from DSH 0.2.1-rc.3 with the tag features added, and its bundle patch disables the stock browser. Everything else in the browser, including search, pinning, archiving, drag ordering, shortcuts, and plugins’ **Add workspace** flows such as dsh-remote-agents’ remote workspaces, works as in DSH. Uninstalling the package restores the stock browser.

The copy follows the DSH release it was taken from. After a DSH update the sidebar keeps that release’s browser behavior until the package is updated; see [docs/upstream.md](docs/upstream.md) for how the copy is kept in step and what to do if DSH refuses the plugin.

The copied DSH code is MIT-licensed; see [third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

# DSH Plugins

**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

A pnpm workspace for independently versioned DeepSeek Harness plugins. Each plugin has its own manifest, source, tests, documentation, and installable package.

| Package | Directory | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dsh-remote-agents` | [packages/remote-agents](packages/remote-agents/README.md) | Native DSH chat and task delegation over SSH: run Claude Code, Codex, DSH, Grok, CodeBuddy and Antigravity on remote machines, steer them, and let DSH delegate tasks to them |
| `dsh-session-models` | [packages/session-models](packages/session-models/README.md) | Model icons and status badges on sidebar sessions, with the exact model in the hover card |
| `dsh-workspace-tags` | [packages/workspace-tags](packages/workspace-tags/README.md) | Colored workspace tags, with sidebar grouping by tag or by running status |
| `dsh-usage-stats` | [packages/usage-stats](packages/usage-stats/README.md) | Track DSH and Claude SSH token usage with filters, grouped reports and CSV export |
| `dsh-gallery` | [packages/gallery](packages/gallery/README.md) | Bing daily wallpapers, local uploads, pinned backgrounds and image previews for DSH |
| `dsh-browser-devtools` | [packages/browser-devtools](packages/browser-devtools/README.md) | Chrome-style Elements, Console and Network debugger, docked or in a separate Chrome/Edge window |
| `dsh-translate` | [packages/translate](packages/translate/README.md) | Translate selected chat text and composer drafts through an OpenAI-compatible API |

## Languages

Plugin interfaces support English and Simplified Chinese. English is the source and fallback language. On hosts with the DSH locale service, plugins follow **Settings → General → Language** and update immediately, including open panels and known error messages. Older hosts without that service use English. API diagnostics and CSV column names use English; user content, model IDs and command syntax stay in their original language.

The private `packages/i18n` helper is bundled into each client at build time, so plugin archives remain independently installable.

## Setup

Requires Node.js ≥ 22.15.0 and pnpm **10.34.7**, pinned in `package.json`.

```sh
corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
corepack pnpm check
corepack pnpm pack:plugins
```

If pnpm is already available at the pinned version, use `pnpm` directly. The repository uses a single `pnpm-lock.yaml`; run dependency installation at the workspace root.

## Development

```sh
pnpm build          # Build every package
pnpm typecheck      # Type-check every package
pnpm test           # Run package tests
pnpm check          # Type-check, test, then build
pnpm test:ui        # Run available browser regression suites
pnpm pack:plugins   # Build and pack packages into dist/
```

Work on one plugin with a package filter:

```sh
pnpm --filter dsh-remote-agents check
pnpm --filter dsh-remote-agents pack:plugin
```

## Installation

Remote Agents **0.2.23** lists only the current workspace machine’s remote models, grouped by Claude, Codex and other CLIs, in DSH's model picker and main conversation. The Open sessions button in settings brings history, follow-ups and pending approvals together; delegation tools remain available. Build `dist/dsh-remote-agents-0.2.23.tgz` with `pnpm --filter dsh-remote-agents pack:plugin`. See [install and upgrade](packages/remote-agents/README.md#install-and-upgrade), including what changed from 0.1.x.

Install an individual built archive into the desired DSH profile:

```sh
pnpm pack:plugins
dsh plugin --profile web add "$PWD/dist/dsh-remote-agents-0.2.23.tgz"
```

For Desktop, fully quit DSH and use the desktop application's bundled `dsh` command with `--profile desktop`, then reopen the app; the npm CLI cannot manage this reserved profile. For Web, restart the updated profile and refresh the browser. Plugins are not currently published to npm. The repository root is a private workspace; install individual plugin archives rather than the GitHub root.

### Plugin market

`pnpm release:market` builds every plugin, commits the install-ready packages to the `market` branch, and updates `index.json` there: a DSH plugin market index listing every released version, each pinned to a commit. Publish with `git push origin market`. A release requires a clean working tree; versions already in the index are skipped, and a plugin that changed without a version bump is reported. `--dry-run` previews the release. Never rewrite or force-push `market`, because installed versions resolve through its commits.

To install and update from DSH, open **Plugins**, switch on **Custom plugin markets** under experimental plugins, and add this index source on the **Discover** tab:

```text
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lalaze/dsh-plugins/market/index.json
```

Discover marks a newer release **Update available** and opens the installed plugin’s detail page when clicked. Third-party plugins currently require uninstalling the old version before installing the new version from Discover or Add plugin; an installed plugin has no Install button. DSH offers one-click updates only for its official plugins.

## Layout and new plugins

```text
packages/
  remote-agents/        # dsh-remote-agents: source, tests, manifest, docs
  session-models/       # Model icons and status badges on sidebar sessions
  workspace-tags/       # Workspace tags and tag/status grouping in the sidebar
  usage-stats/          # DSH and Claude SSH usage statistics
  gallery/              # Local wallpaper library and DSH backgrounds
  browser-devtools/     # Docked / separate-window debugger for Sidebar Browser tabs
  translate/            # Chat selection and composer translation
scripts/
  build-client.mjs      # Shared DSH web client bundler
tsconfig.base.json     # Shared TypeScript compiler options
pnpm-workspace.yaml    # Discovers packages/*
pnpm-lock.yaml         # Workspace dependency lock
dist/                  # Generated installable archives (ignored)
```

Add each plugin under `packages/<plugin-name>` with a unique package name, its own version, and the standard `build`, `typecheck`, and `test` scripts. Root commands discover it automatically. Shared tools live at the root; plugin-specific dependencies belong to the plugin. Release plugins independently.

See [the development guide](docs/development.md) (Chinese) for manifests, client builds, packaging, and shared-code conventions.

MIT. See each plugin's documentation for third-party acknowledgments.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dshell

`dshell` is a Claude Code-style terminal frontend for an already-running
DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Host. The Web UI and the terminal are two frontends over
the same live Agents and durable Sessions:

```text
                    one dsh Host
        ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
        │ ctx.agents / ctx.sessions        │
        │ ctx.workspaceRegistry            │
        │ ctx.sessionQuery / ctx.approval  │
        └───────────────┬──────────────────┘
                        │
        ┌───────────────┴──────────────────┐
        │  @landasika/dshell Host plugin   │
        │  $DSH_HOME/run/dshell.sock       │
        └───────────────┬──────────────────┘
                        │ NDJSON, no token
             ┌──────────┴──────────┐
             │   dshell TUI / CLI  │
             └─────────────────────┘
```

The CLI never starts a second Host, never copies durable events into a second
truth, and never owns an Agent. Quitting a terminal only closes its view.

**V1 supports Linux only.** See [Supported versions](docs/SUPPORTED-VERSIONS.md).

## Status

P0–P6 are complete for the V1 candidate `0.1.0`:

- full-screen TUI, plus scriptable `dshell -p`;
- text / JSON / NDJSON output;
- workspace and session creation, history, cancel, steer;
- first-answer-wins approval bridge shared with the Web UI;
- fail-closed approvals for non-interactive and disconnected frontends;
- Node 22/24 CI and a verified npm tarball.

## Requirements

- Linux (x64 tested)
- Node `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`
- pnpm 11.x for development
- DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` (tested; other versions are best-effort)
- an already-running `dsh --profile web`

## Quick start

### 1. Build and install the Host plugin

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Landasika/dshell.git
cd dshell
pnpm install
pnpm build

# Load the plugin into the DSH web profile. The package is a DSH bundle, so
# this updates dsh.profile.bundles automatically.
dsh plugin --profile web add "$PWD"
```

Start the Host:

```bash
dsh --profile web
```

Look for:

```text
[dshell-host] listening on /home/<user>/.dsh/run/dshell.sock
```

The plugin must be present when the Host boots; it cannot be injected into an
already-running Host.

### 2. Local development Host (no global `dsh`)

If `dsh` is not on `PATH`, use the development wrappers. They boot a Host with
the plugin in an isolated `.dsh-dev/` home (never touching `~/.dsh`) and
auto-detect a bundled DSH runtime:

```bash
# terminal 1 — Host and Web UI
./scripts/dev-host.sh

# terminal 2 — TUI against that Host
./scripts/dev-tui.sh
```

`./scripts/dev-host.sh` installs this checkout into a dedicated `dshell`
profile and rebuilds the profile when the plugin changes. Override `DSH_BIN`,
`DSH_HOME`, or `DSH_PROFILE` to use another CLI/home/profile.

### 3. Install the CLI

While developing, run the built binary directly:

```bash
node dist/bin/dshell.js doctor
node dist/bin/dshell.js
```

Or install it globally:

```bash
npm install -g @landasika/dshell
# or, before npm publication, from a verified tarball:
npm install -g ./landasika-dshell-0.1.0.tgz
```

### 4. Open the TUI

```bash
dshell
```

In a non-TTY (pipe, CI), `dshell` prints help instead of writing control
sequences.

## TUI

```text
dshell
dshell --resume <sessionId>
dshell --no-color
```

The terminal is a daily tool, so the first screen is the session list you
actually need — no splash art:

```text
🐳 dshell · DeepSeek Harness
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

choose session
/home/landasika/dshell

↑/↓ move · enter attach · n new session · q quit

▸ Socket client hardening                                    live 2m ago
  TUI redesign notes                                        cold 1h ago
  Release checklist                                         cold 3d ago
```

`live`/`cold` is the attachment state; the age is the session's **last edit**
(the newest durable prompt, from the Host's session-list projection, falling
back to the creation time), and rows are ordered by it — the session you last
touched is always first.

Inside a session:

```text
🐳 dshell · session title                              ● running · /project
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  transcript: streaming markdown, reasoning, tool cards, diffs, approvals
⚓ thinking · 412 tok · ctrl+o expand
│ 先确认每个应用的启动方式，再分派给子代理。
│ venv 已就绪，可以直接跑冒烟门。
⇢ agent started  接入 OctoPrint harness · 18b9d1cc
⢿ Running command · rg reconnect src · 12s · ctx 84%
▸ 1/3 · Adding bounded backoff                                    ctrl+t hide
────────────────────────── ctx ▰▰▰▱▱▱▱▱▱▱ 25% · 42 tps
❯ ask anything
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  enter send · / commands · @ files · ctrl+r history · ? help
deepseek-relay/deepseek-v4.1-flash  ~/dshell  main [↑10]  ✓ agents 1/1  cache ▰▰▰▰▰ 91%  ↑12.4k ↓840
```

- startup picker: drawn before the first Host round-trip, so the chat shell
  never flashes while connecting. Rows use the DSH title snapshot (the same
  one the Web UI shows) and fall back to `untitled session`, never to a bare
  UUID; subagent child sessions are hidden and remain reachable through the
  parent's `Ctrl-G` roster. Listing is scoped to the current workspace, cached
  for a few seconds, and titles are resolved progressively so a large shared
  `~/.dsh` stays responsive.
- header: brand (`🐳 dshell`), session title, status (idle / running /
  approval / error) and working directory. The assistant's first block in a
  turn is signed `🐳 dshell`.
- markdown: headings, lists, quotes, fenced code, diffs and **tables**. Tables
  are drawn as a box grid with per-column alignment (`:---`, `:--:`, `---:`),
  cells wider than the terminal wrap instead of being cut off, and CJK/emoji
  count as two cells so the borders stay aligned.
- user prompts: drawn on a grey band with white text and a `>` marker, so the
  prompt that started a turn is easy to find when scrolling back. Assistant
  text carries a single `dshell` header per turn — later steps after a tool
  call are not labelled again.
- tool calls: folded to one line, Claude-Code style — `✓ Bash(rg --files -g "*.ts")`,
  with the identifying argument only and a trailing `…` when it does not fit.
  `Ctrl-O` expands every call's argument summary and output inline; selecting
  one with `Alt+↑/↓` and pressing `Enter` opens the same detail in a scrollable
  panel. A failed call keeps its first two output lines visible.
- thinking: folded to a `⚓ thinking · N tok · ctrl+o` header plus the last
  three reasoning lines on a dim rail. `Ctrl-O` expands the full text; live
  reasoning streams on the same rail while the model is thinking.
- subagents: a `⇢ agent started` card when a child is spawned, updated to
  `✓ finished` / `✗ failed` from the durable settlement notice. `Ctrl-G` (or
  `/agents`) lists every child with its status; `Enter` opens that child's
  transcript in a read-only panel.
- live activity: spinner, current tool/verb, elapsed turn time and context
  pressure. Only shown while a turn runs; the header carries the idle state.
- scrolling: the mouse wheel (and `PgUp`/`PgDn`) scrolls the transcript, never
  the composer. While scrolled up a right-aligned `↓ N new · End` pill appears
  above the composer; click it, press `End`/`Enter`, or `Esc` to return to the
  live tail. `DSHELL_NO_MOUSE=1` disables mouse capture so the terminal keeps
  its own scrollback and text selection.
- composer (frameless, Claude-Code style): a horizontal rule, the `❯` input,
  another rule, then a dim shortcut hint. The top rule carries the context
  gauge (`ctx ▰▰▰▱▱▱▱▱▱▱ 25%`) and token speed (`42 tps`) right-aligned. Wide
  terminals get the 10-cell bar with TPS; narrower ones drop TPS, then collapse
  the bar to a plain percentage, then drop the gauge. Rules never wrap.
- usage rail (bottom, under the composer): provider/model route (`provider/model`),
  the cwd (`~/…`), the Git branch with ahead/behind counts (`main [↑10]`, `*`
  when dirty), subagent progress (`✓ agents 1/1`, `✗` plus a failed count),
  the cache hit rate (`cache ▰▰▰▰▰ 91%`) and, when space allows, session
  input/output totals and estimated spend (`~¥`). On narrow terminals it drops
  totals → spend → cwd → git → agents → cache, keeping the model route.
  Model and provider details, the peak/idle split and per-model rows live in
  `Ctrl-B`.
- context bar: measured occupancy from the latest usage, split into
  system / prompt / assistant / thinking / tools; amber at 80%, red at 95%.
  The bar is the readout's boundary, local estimates only divide the used span.
- todo strip: current task and completion count, foldable with `Ctrl-T`; the
  session panel keeps the full list.
- status strip (above the composer, only when non-empty):
  `✓ agents 1/1  ● jobs 1  ● todo 0/6`. `✓` means every subagent settled,
  `●` a child/job is still running; `✗` flags failed jobs. Jobs are folded from
  durable `job/registered` / `job/settled` events, so the count survives
  reconnects and history replay.
- composer: rounded frame that grows with the draft (up to seven rows); the
  shortcut hint sits in its bottom border.

### Spend estimate

DSH reports tokens, not money. The usage rail converts durable
`assistant/message.usage` events with DeepSeek's published per-million-token
rates (CNY, idle price; peak hours are doubled). Cache reads use the hit rate;
cache writes and uncached input use the miss rate; output uses the output rate.
Peak hours are Beijing time, Monday–Friday 09:00–12:00 and 14:00–18:00.

`~¥0.42` is an **estimate, not a bill**: prices can change, and the balance is
deducted on DeepSeek's side. Models missing from the rate table show tokens but
no amount (`unpriced`); the same applies to routes whose billing differs from
the official API.

### Keys

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Enter` | send / run command; while a turn runs it **steers** (joins that turn) |
| `Alt+Q` | queue the prompt for the next turn instead of steering (`Alt+Enter` also works when the terminal forwards it) |
| `Ctrl+Enter`, `Shift+Enter` | newline (`Ctrl-J` also works everywhere; dshell enables the kitty keyboard protocol so `Ctrl+Enter` is distinguishable) |
| `Tab` | complete `/` command or `@` file |
| `↑`/`↓`, `Ctrl-P/N` | completion, picker, or prompt history (seeded from the session's durable transcript) |
| `Alt+↑`/`Alt+↓` | move a selection from block to block: messages, tool calls, subagent rows, then the queued prompts |
| `Enter` (with a selection) | open it: tool details, the subagent list (`≈ /agents`), or pull a queued prompt back into the composer to edit it |
| `Alt+Backspace` | delete the selected queued prompt |
| `Esc` | clear the selection |
| `PgUp`/`PgDn`, wheel | page or line scroll of the transcript |
| drag | select transcript text and copy it (OSC 52); `Shift+drag` uses the terminal's own selection |
| `Ctrl-R` | search prompts sent in this session |
| `Ctrl-B` | session panel: context breakdown, session spend, tokens, speed, todos, agents |
| `Ctrl-G` | subagent list; `Enter` opens that child's transcript |
| `q` | quit from the startup picker |
| `End` / `Enter` / `Esc` | jump back to the live tail while scrolled up |
| wheel, `PgUp`/`PgDn` | scroll the transcript |
| `Ctrl-T` | fold/show the todo strip |
| `Ctrl-O` | expand/fold tool output, thinking and lifecycle blocks |
| `?` | help & shortcuts (when the composer is empty) |
| `Esc` | close a menu/overlay or clear the composer; double-`Esc` on an empty idle composer opens rewind |
| `Ctrl-C` | clear input, cancel a running turn (the `Alt+Q` queue continues), or quit |
| `Ctrl-D` | quit when the composer is empty |

Typing while a turn is running does not get lost, and `Enter` keeps the Claude
Code habit: the message is **steered** into the running turn, so the agent sees
it at its next step and the transcript shows it as a normal user message
(`◷ steering · …` marks the gap until then). `Alt+Q` queues the prompt
instead — the Host holds it and starts a fresh turn after the current one
(`◷ queued · …`). `Ctrl-C` aborts the running turn and the prompts you queued
with `Alt+Q` continue right after it: the Host drops its inbox with an abort,
so the TUI hands those prompts back itself.

`Alt+Q` rather than `Alt+Enter`: plenty of terminals (Windows Terminal included)
bind `Alt+Enter` to fullscreen and never forward the key, so dshell's queue
shortcut is a plain `Alt`+letter. `Alt+Enter` is still accepted where the
terminal does send it.

`Ctrl-C`/`Ctrl-D`/`Esc` quitting only closes this view; it never cancels the
Host turn. Cancel explicitly with `Ctrl-C` while a turn is running or
`/cancel`.

Commands: `/sessions` (aliases `/session`, `/resume`), `/workspaces`, `/new`,
`/attach`, `/cancel`, `/clear`,
`/reconnect`, `/rewind`, `/history`, `/panel`, `/status`, `/agents`, `/model`,
`/provider`, `/verbose`, `/help`, `/quit`. Approvals are modal: `a` allow once, `r` reject, `d` details.

### Models

`/model` asks the Host for its live provider/model catalog and opens a picker:

- `↑/↓` move, `Enter` switches the current session
- models that declare reasoning levels step into a level list first
  (`off` / `low` / `high` / `max`, each with its own description); `Enter`
  there commits model **and** level in one selection
- in the level list `↑/↓` moves and `1`-`9` jumps straight to that level
  (Enter or `Shift+Enter` commits it); `e` reopens the level list for the
  highlighted model, `←` goes back
- `d` saves the highlighted model (and shown level) as the default
- `/model provider/model` switches directly; `/model default provider/model`
  saves a default without touching the current session

Switching is a Host operation, not a TUI guess: the `dshell-host` plugin
bridges DSH's `sessionController.modelCatalog()` and `selectModel()`, so the
same catalog the Web UI shows is used. DSH applies the selection on the next
request and appends a durable "model changed" notice; the selection also
becomes the saved default. The level a model was last switched with is
remembered per `provider/model` and shown in the bottom rail
(`deepseek-official/deepseek-flash · high`).

### Providers

If the Host drops the socket (it exits, or DSH re-creates the plugin after the
profile's linked package changes), the TUI notices and reattaches by itself:
`host connection lost · reconnecting`, then `host back · reattached`. Nothing
to run by hand, and `/reconnect` remains for a manual nudge.

`/provider` lists the provider rows of the patch file the Host booted with
(`$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml`, else the active profile's), read through the
`dshell-host` plugin:

- `Enter` opens a field editor for `baseURL`, `apiKeyEnv` and `displayName`
- `Enter` on a field edits it, `Ctrl-U` clears it, `Enter` commits the field
- `s` writes the changed fields back and raises a confirmation:
  `Restart the Host now?` — `y` re-execs the Host and reattaches the session,
  `n` keeps the file change for the next manual start
- `a` adds a provider: `id`, optional `displayName` / `apiKeyEnv`, `baseURL`
  and a comma- or space-separated model list; the block is appended to the
  `providers` map and the same restart confirmation follows
- `x` deletes the selected provider (after a `y` confirmation, then the same
  restart prompt). The last remaining provider cannot be deleted
- `r` restarts the Host without editing

The editor only touches the lines it needs — a field edit rewrites that
scalar, `a` inserts one block, `x` splices one block out — so comments, model
lists and `!!js` expressions elsewhere in the patch file survive, and an
add/delete round trip leaves the file byte-identical. API keys themselves are
never stored there: the file carries the environment-variable name
(`apiKeyEnv`) and the secret stays in the environment or DSH's credential
store. Providers are read at Host boot, so an edit needs the restart the
confirmation offers — there is no live provider reload.

### Herdr

Run the TUI inside a [Herdr](https://herdr.dev) pane and it integrates itself:

- the pane shows `dshell` with `working`, `blocked` (approval waiting) or
  `idle` state in Herdr's sidebar and in `herdr agent list`
- the DSH session id and a resume command are reported, so a Herdr server
  restart reopens the same conversation in that pane
- quitting releases the agent from the pane
- outside Herdr it is a no-op; `DSHELL_NO_HERDR=1` disables it explicitly

Unlike Claude Code, which needs `herdr integration install claude` to write a
`SessionStart` hook into its settings, dshell speaks Herdr's
`pane.report_agent` socket protocol directly (the "Add Herdr support to your
agent" path), so there is no hook or settings file to install.

See [TUI design](docs/TUI-DESIGN.md) for the palette, metric sources and
responsive rules.

## Scriptable CLI

```bash
dshell -p "summarize this repository"
dshell -p --session <sessionId> "continue"
dshell -p --new --cwd /path/to/project "initialize the project"
printf 'summarize this repo\n' | dshell -p

dshell -p --json "..."                       # one JSON result object
dshell -p --output-format stream-json "..."  # NDJSON start/event/result
```

`-p` writes only the result to stdout; diagnostics go to stderr. It never
prompts: any approval is rejected and the exit code is `5` (fail closed).

Exit codes:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | turn completed |
| 1 | Host/connection/protocol/internal error |
| 2 | invalid usage |
| 3 | turn failed, cancelled, or abnormal end |
| 4 | `--timeout` reached |
| 5 | approval denied in non-interactive mode |
| 130 | SIGINT |

### Low-level commands

```bash
dshell doctor
dshell workspaces
dshell list [workspaceId]
dshell new [cwd]
dshell attach <sessionId>
dshell prompt <sessionId> '…'
dshell steer <sessionId> '…'
dshell cancel <sessionId>
```

Options:

```text
--socket <path>       control socket override
--timeout <ms>        turn timeout (default 120000)
--verbose             context/lifecycle diagnostics
--resume <id>, -r     TUI: open a session directly
--no-color            disable ANSI colors
-p, --print           one-shot mode
--output-format <f>   text | json | stream-json
--json                shorthand for --output-format json
-s, --session <id>    use an existing session
-w, --workspace <id>  workspace for a new session
--cwd <path>          cwd for a new session
--new                 always create a session
```

Environment:

```text
DSH_HOME              DSH home (default: ~/.dsh)
DSHELL_SOCKET         control socket override
```

## Approvals and safety

- DSH approval is answered by a Host bridge. The Web UI and a CLI/TUI can race;
  the **first valid answer wins**.
- The bridge registers with `{ global: true, prepend: true }` so the agent-scoped
  Web answerer cannot block it.
- Timeout, Host shutdown, request abort, and last-watcher disconnect return
  `unavailable`; they never auto-allow.
- `dshell prompt` on a TTY asks `[a]llow once / [r]eject`; non-TTY rejects.
- `dshell -p` always rejects and exits `5`.
- Approval request ids come from the Host bridge, never from a replayed
  `approval/asked` durable event.

The socket is `$DSH_HOME/run/dshell.sock`, directory `0700`, socket `0600`.
There is no token or Cookie. Run dshell as the same user that started the Host.

## Design notes

- The Host owns all live Agents and Sessions.
- The plugin holds the Agent handles it resumes; a CLI disconnect only drops
  subscriptions.
- Durable truth is `session/event`; `agent/assistant-stream` is a live
  presentation channel only.
- One Host per `DSH_HOME`. A second Host refuses to bind the same socket.
- The plugin is a DSH bundle (`package.json:dsh.bundle.patch`); no DSH source
  changes are required.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `HOST_NOT_RUNNING` / no socket | Start `dsh --profile web` with the plugin installed, or run `./scripts/dev-host.sh`. |
| `PLUGIN_MISSING` | The Host booted without `dshell-host`; add the plugin to the web profile and restart. |
| `PROTOCOL_MISMATCH` | Install the CLI and plugin from the same dshell version. |
| `SOCKET_PERMISSION_DENIED` | Run dshell as the Host user; check `DSH_HOME` ownership and socket mode `0600`. |
| `[warn] dsh version` in doctor | Your DSH is outside the tested matrix; see [Supported versions](docs/SUPPORTED-VERSIONS.md). |
| Approval seems to wait | Check the Web UI and any other dshell client; only one answer wins. Disconnect/unanswered requests fail closed. |
| TUI won't start in a pipeline | It needs a TTY. Use `dshell -p` for scripts. |
| Second Host fails to start | Stop the first Host; only one dshell Host per `DSH_HOME`. |

## Development

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm typecheck
pnpm lint
pnpm test          # 30 tests
./scripts/ci.sh    # full local gate, including clean pack/install
```

Release artifacts are verified with `scripts/verify-pack.sh`. The tag workflow
`.github/workflows/release.yml` runs the same gate and uploads the tarball plus
`SHA256SUMS`; npm publication is a manual, credentialed step.
